srcs: Charity begins at home is a proverb that means that people should take care of their own family and community before helping others.
The phrase is often used to encourage people to be more charitable to those in need, but it can also be used to justify selfishness or inaction.
One example of how the phrase might be used is if someone is asked to donate to a charity that helps people in a foreign country.
The person might say that they would rather donate to a local charity that helps people in their own community.
This is because they believe that it is more important to help those who are close to them than those who are far away.
The phrase "charity begins at home" can be traced back to the Bible.
In the book of Matthew, Jesus says, "If you give to the poor, your gift will be given back to you full measure, pressed down, shaken together, and running over.
For by your standard of measure it will be measured to you in return." (Matthew 6:20).
This verse suggests that people should be generous to others, but it also implies that they should start by being generous to those who are close to them.

Ezali mpo akanisi ete ezali ntina mingi kosalisa bato oyo bazali pene na ye na esika ya kosalisa bato oyo bazali mosika.

Na mokanda ya Matai, Yesu alobaki ete, "Soki opesi babola, likabo na yo ekozongiselama na lolenge ya monene, oyo bafini, baningisi elongo, mpe eleki ndelo.

srcs: The hippie movement was a social and cultural phenomenon that emerged in the United States during the 1960s.
It was characterized by its rejection of mainstream values and its emphasis on peace, love, and freedom.
Music played an important role in the hippie movement, as it helped to create a sense of community and shared identity among its members.
The music of the hippie movement was diverse, but it was often characterized by its experimental nature and its focus on spirituality and social change.
Some of the most popular hippie bands included the Grateful Dead, Jefferson Airplane, and the Doors.
These bands created a new sound that was unlike anything that had come before, and their music helped to inspire the counterculture movement.
The hippie movement has had a lasting impact on music, and its influence can still be seen today.
Many modern bands continue to draw inspiration from the hippie era, and its values of peace, love, and freedom continue to resonate with people around the world.
One of the most important aspects of hippie music was its emphasis on balance.

Hippie musicians sought to create music that was both beautiful and meaningful, and they often drew inspiration from a variety of sources, including Eastern philosophy, world music, and psychedelic drugs.

srcs: In a Google spreadsheet, an absolute reference will always refer to the same cell, regardless of where it is copied or moved to.
Absolute references are useful for cells that contain data that you do not want to change when you copy or move the formula.
For example, if you have a formula that calculates the total sales for each month, you would want to use an absolute reference for the cell that contains the starting date.
This way, the formula will always refer to the same cell, even if you copy it to a different row or column.
You can create an absolute reference by adding a dollar sign ($) to the row number and column letter of the cell reference.
For example, the absolute reference for the cell A1 would be $A$1.
You can also use absolute references to reference a range of cells.
To do this, add a dollar sign to the row number and column letter of each cell in the range.
For example, the absolute reference for the range A1:B1 would be $A$1:$B$1.
Absolute references are a powerful tool that can be used to make your formulas more flexible and easier to use.
By understanding how to use absolute references, you can create formulas that will work even when you copy or move them to different locations.
Here are some additional tips for using absolute references:
* Use absolute references for cells that contain data that you do not want to change.
* Use relative references for cells that contain data that you do want to change.
* Be careful when using mixed references, which are references that contain both absolute and relative references.
* Use the F4 key to toggle between absolute, relative, and mixed references.
By following these tips, you can use absolute references to create powerful and flexible formulas that will make your work in Excel easier and more efficient.

srcs: He taught that all beings are caught in a cycle of birth, death, and rebirth, and that this cycle is perpetuated by our attachments to things in the world.
These attachments can be to anything, from material possessions to ideas and beliefs.
When we are attached to something, we become possessive and controlling, and we suffer when we lose or cannot have what we want.
The Buddha taught that the way to end suffering is to let go of our attachments.
This is not easy, but it is possible through meditation and other spiritual practices.
When we let go of our attachments, we become free from the cycle of birth, death, and rebirth, and we can experience true peace and happiness.
One of the most important things to remember when trying to let go of our attachments is that we are not our possessions.
We are not our ideas or beliefs.
We are simply beings who are experiencing the world through our senses.
When we can see ourselves in this way, it becomes easier to let go of the things that we think we need to be happy.
Letting go of our attachments does not mean that we have to give up everything.
It simply means that we need to be able to let go of things when it is time.
We need to be able to let go of the things that are no longer serving us, and we need to be able to let go of the things that we are attached to out of fear or insecurity.
When we can let go of our attachments, we open ourselves up to a new world of possibilities.
We become free to live our lives in a way that is true to ourselves, and we become free to experience the joy and happiness that is our birthright.

srcs: Trains have been a vital part of transportation for centuries.
They are a safe, efficient, and reliable way to travel long distances.
However, the railroad industry requires regular updates to keep pace with the changing needs of passengers.
One of the most important updates that trains need is the installation of new safety features.
In recent years, there have been a number of high-profile train accidents, which have highlighted the need for better safety measures.
New safety features such as positive train control (PTC) can help prevent accidents by automatically stopping trains that are traveling too fast or that are about to collide with another train.
Another important update that trains need is the installation of new technology.
In the past, trains were powered by steam engines.
However, steam engines are inefficient and pollute the environment.
Today, most trains are powered by diesel engines or electric motors.
These engines are more efficient and environmentally friendly.
In addition to safety and technology updates, trains also need to be updated to accommodate the needs of passengers.
In recent years, there has been an increase in the number of passengers who travel by train.
This has led to overcrowding on trains, which can make for a less comfortable and enjoyable experience.

Na mibu euti koleka, ezalaki na ba aksida mingi ya makasi ya bingunduka, oyo emonisaki polele mposa ya miango ya malamu ya libateli to sécurité.

Biloko ya sika ya libateli neti kolandela malamu engunduka (PTC) ekoki kosalisa na kokanga aksida esalema te na kokangaka automatiquement engunduka oyo ezali kotambola mbango koleka to oyo elingi kotutana na engunduka mosusu.
Eloko mosusu ya sika ya ntina oyo bingunduka ezali na mposa na yango ezali kotya teknolozi ya sika.
Na kala, bazalaki kotambwisa bingunduka na bamashine ya mopepe.
Kasi, bamashine ya mopepe ezali makasi te mpe ebebisaka mopepe.
Lelo, bingunduka mingi esalaka na bamashine ya mazute to ya bamotere ya lotiliki.
Bamotere oyo ezali malamu mpenza mpe ebebisaka te mopepe.
Longola biloko ya sika ya securité to libateli mpe ya teknolozi, bingunduka ezali mpe na ntina ya kobakisa biloko ya sika mpo na komesana na bamposa ya bakiliya.
Na mibu euti koleka, motango ya bato oyo basalaka mobembo na bingunduka emataki makasi.
Yango esala ete bato bazala ebele mpenza na kati ya bingunduka, ekoki kosala ete mobembo ezala malamu te to kitoko te.

srcs: She had always been a talented painter, but after her loss, she found that she was no longer interested in painting pretty landscapes or still lifes.
Instead, she began to create dark, brooding works of art that reflected her inner turmoil.
One of her most famous paintings, "The Death of My Son," is a stark and disturbing image of a young boy lying in a coffin.
The boy's face is peaceful, but his body is twisted and contorted in pain.
The painting is full of symbolism, and it is clear that Mary is using her art to process her grief and anger.
Mary's shift in artistic style was not without its critics.
Some people accused her of being exploitative and insensitive.
Others said that her paintings were too depressing and that they should not be shown in public.
However, Mary refused to back down.
She believed that her art was important, and she wanted to share it with the world.
Mary's work eventually found an audience, and she became one of the most respected artists of her time.
Her paintings are now considered to be masterpieces, and they are still studied and admired by people all over the world.
Mary's story is a reminder that art can be a powerful tool for expression.
It can be used to process grief, anger, and other difficult emotions.
It can also be used to communicate important messages about the human condition.
Mary's paintings are a testament to the power of art, and they continue to inspire people to this day.
trgs: Azalaka ntango nyonso peintre ya mayele, kasi nsima ya kobungisa ye, amonaki azalaki kosepela lisusu te na kosala bapeinture ya ba paysage to ya biloko oyo etambolaka te.
Ksi, abandaka kosala misala ya art ya moindo mpe ezali kotungisa oyo ezali komonisa mitungisi azali na yango.
Moko ya ba peinture eyebana mingi, "Liwa ya Mwana na Nga," ezali elili ya kokesena mpe ezali kotungisa ya elenge mobali alili na kati ya sanduku.
Elongi ya elenge mobali ezali na kimya, kasi nzoto na ye ebebi mpe azali na mpasi.
Peinture etondi na bilembo, mpe ezali polele ete Maria azali kosalela art na ye mpo na kolakisa mawa mpe nkanda na ye.
Mbongwana ya lolenge ya kosala art ya Maria ezali na bato oyo bazalaki kolobela yango mabe.
Bato mosusu bafundaki ye ete azali kobuba mpe kokipe te mayoki ya bato.
Basusu balobaki ete ba peinture na ye ezalaki ya mawa mingi mpe ete basengeli kolakisa yango te na bato nyonso.
Kasi, Maria aboyaki kozonga nsima.
Azalaki kokanisa ete art na ye ezalaki ntina, mpe azalaki kolinga kokabola yango na mokili mobimba.
Nsukansuka mosala ya Maria ezwaki bayoki, mpe akomaki moko ya bato ya art oyo bato batosaka mingi na ntango na ye.
Bato balobaka sikoyo ete ba peinture na ye ezali misala ya kitoko koleka, mpe bato bakobaka koyekola yango mpe kosepela na yango na mokili mobimba.
Lisolo ya Maria ezali kokundwela biso ete art ekoki kozala esaleli ya makasi ya komonisa makanisi.
Ekoki kosalelama na kobimisa mawa, nkanda, mpe mayoki mosusu ya mpasi.
Ekoki kosalelama mpe mpo na kolobela bansango ya ntina etali ndenge bato bazali.
Ba peinture ya Maria ezali kondimisa nguya ya art, mpe ezali kokoba kopesa bato makanisi kino lelo.

srcs: Sudan is a country in northeastern Africa.

It is bordered by Egypt to the north, Libya to the northwest, Chad to the west, the Central African Republic to the southwest, South Sudan to the south, Ethiopia to the southeast, and Eritrea to the east.
Sudan has a population of over 40 million people and a land area of over 1.8 million square kilometers.
Sudan's history is long and complex.
The area has been inhabited by humans for thousands of years, and the first known civilization in Sudan was the Kingdom of Kush, which flourished from around 750 BC to 350 AD.
Kush was a powerful kingdom that controlled much of the Nile River valley.
In the 7th century AD, Sudan was conquered by the Arabs, who brought Islam to the region.
Sudan was ruled by a series of Arab sultanates for centuries, until it was conquered by Egypt in 1821.
Egypt ruled Sudan until 1885, when it was conquered by the Mahdi, a religious leader who led a rebellion against Egyptian rule.
The Mahdi's rule was short-lived, and Sudan was reconquered by the British in 1898.
trgs: Soudan ezali ekolo moko ya ezali na norde-este ya Afrika.
Ekangama na Ezipito na norde, na Libye na norde-weste, na Tchad na weste, na Repiblike Centre Africaine na sude-weste, na Soudan du Sud na sude, na Ethiopie na sude-este, mpe na Érythrée na este.
Soudan ezali na bato koleka bamilio 40 mpe mokili na yango ezali monene koleka 1,8 milio ya bakilometre.
Lisolo ya Soudan ezali ya molai mpe ya mindondo.
Bato bafandaka kuna banda bankoto ya bambula, mpe sivilizasio ya liboso eyebana na Soudan ezalaki Bokonzi ya Kush, oyo ezalaki kotambola malamu pene ya 750 BC kino 350 AD.
Kush ezalaki bokonzi ya makasi oyo ezalaki koyangela eteni monene ya lobwaku ya Ebale Nile.
Na ekeke 7 AD, balongaki Soudan na ba Arabe, oyo bamemaki lingomba ya mizilma kuna.
Soudan eyangelamaki na bakonzi ebele ya ba Araba na bikeke ebele, kino balongaki yango na Ezipito na 1821.
Ezipito eyangelaki Soudan kino 1885, ntango balongaki yango na Mahdi, mokonzi moko ya lingomba oyo akambaki bato oyo batombokelaki bokonzi ya Ezipito.
Boyangeli ya Mahdi esalemi ntango moke, mpe balongaki lisusu Soudan na Grande-Bretagne na 1898.

srcs: My dear daughter, I know you've been wondering about the nature of light and darkness.
It's a big question, and one that scientists have been trying to answer for centuries.
But I think I can give you a simple explanation that will help you understand it a little better.
Light is a kind of energy that travels in waves.
We can see light because it enters our eyes and stimulates the retina, which is a light-sensitive tissue at the back of the eye.
The retina sends signals to our brain, which interprets them as images.
Darkness is the absence of light.
When there is no light, we can't see anything.
Light and darkness are two opposites, but they're also two sides of the same coin.
Light is needed for us to see, but darkness is also important.
Darkness helps us to rest and sleep.
It also creates a sense of mystery and wonder.
So next time you're outside at night, take a moment to appreciate the darkness.
It's just as important as light, and it has its own beauty.
trgs: Mwana na nga ya mwasi oyo nalingaka, nayebi ozali komitungisa mpo na pole mpe molili.
Ezali motuna monene, mpe motuna oyo bato ya siansi bazali koluka kozwa eyano banda bikeke ebele.
Kasi nakanisi nakoki kopesa yo ndimbola ya pete oyo ekosalisa yo na koyeba yango mwa malamu.
Pole ezali lolenge ya energie oyo etambolaka lokola mopepe.
Tomonaka pole mpo ekotaka na miso na biso mpe elendisaka retina, oyo eloko oyo ezali sensible na pole mpe ezalaka na nsima ya liso.
Retina etindaka ba signale na boongo na biso, mpe boongo ezwaka yango lokola bilili.
Molili ezali kozanga pole.
Soki pole ezali te, tokoki komona eloko te.
Pole na molili ezali biloko mibale ekeseni, kasi ezali mpe bangombo mibale ya mbongo kaka moko ya libende.
Pole ezalaka ntina mpo tomona, kasi molili ezali mpe ntina.
Molili esalisaka biso na kopema mpe kolala.
Esalisaka mpe na komona neti ezali na limbombami mpe komitungisa.
Yango wana mbala ya nsima oyo okozala libanda na butu, zwa ntango ya kosepela na molili.
Ezali mpe ntina lokola pole, mpe ezali mpe na kitoko na yango.

srcs: Esteban was a concerned father.
His daughter, Marcela, was listening to music that he didn't approve of.
The lyrics were explicit and violent, and he didn't want his daughter exposed to that kind of material.
He tried to talk to her about it, but she just shrugged him off.
He didn't know what else to do.
One day, Esteban was listening to the radio when he heard a song that he thought Marcela would like.
It was a catchy tune with a positive message.
He decided to burn a copy of the song and give it to her.
When she got home from school, he gave her the CD and told her to listen to it.
Marcela was surprised by the gift, but she was also intrigued.
She put the CD in her stereo and listened to the song.
She liked it so much that she listened to it over and over again.
The next day, Esteban asked Marcela what she thought of the song.
She told him that she loved it and that it had made her think about things in a new way.
Esteban was thrilled.
He knew that he had made a difference in his daughter's life.
From that day on, Marcela listened to more positive music.
trgs: Esteban azalaki papa oyo azalaki komitungisa.
Mwana na ye ya mwasi, Marcela, azalaki koyoka miziki oyo papa azalaki kolinga te.
Maloba ezalaki ya mabe mpe ya mobulu, mpe papa azalaki kolinga te ete mwana na yo alanda makambo ya ndenge wana.

Mokolo moko, Esteban azalaki kolanda radio mpe ayokaki loyembo moko oyo akanisaki ete Marcela akolinga.
Ezalaki na ton mpe nsango ya malamu.
Azwaki ekateli ya kosala kopi ya loyembo wana mpe kopesa mwana na ye.
Ntango mwana azongaki ndako nsima ya kelasi, papa apesaki ye CD mpe ayebisaki ye na koyoka yango.
Marcela akamwaki kado wana, kasi azalaki komituna.
Akotisaki CD wana na stereo na ye mpe ayokaki loyembo wana.
Alingaki yango mingi yango wana ayokaki yango mbala ebele.

srcs: Question: My male neighbor complains of fatigue, sleep disturbances and thinks he has Sleeping sickness (Human African Trypanosomiasis) and asks, Doctor, how can I manage this sleeping sickness, as it has been affecting my work schedule?

Answer: While I understand your concern about sleeping sickness and how it's impacting your work, it's extremely unlikely that you have it, especially if you live in an area where it isn't endemic (like North America or Europe).
Human African Trypanosomiasis is primarily found in rural Africa and is transmitted through the bite of the tsetse fly.
Have you recently travelled to sub-Saharan Africa?

Your symptoms of fatigue and sleep disturbances are common and can be caused by a wide range of things, from stress and poor sleep hygiene to underlying medical conditions like sleep apnea, thyroid issues, or even depression.
It's crucial to see a doctor to get a proper diagnosis.
They will likely ask you detailed questions about your symptoms, medical history, travel history, and lifestyle.
They might also recommend some tests, like blood work, to rule out other potential causes.
Do not self-treat or attempt to diagnose yourself with sleeping sickness.
It's a serious disease that requires specialized medical care and specific medications.
Trying to treat it yourself could delay a proper diagnosis and treatment for the real cause of your symptoms.
So, to manage your fatigue and sleep disturbances, your first and most important step is to schedule an appointment with your doctor as soon as possible.
Explain your concerns and be honest about your symptoms.
They are the best resource to help you figure out what's going on and recommend the right course of action.
In the meantime, try to practice good sleep hygiene: maintain a regular sleep schedule, create a relaxing bedtime routine, and avoid caffeine and alcohol before bed.
trgs: Motuna: Mozalani na ngai azali koyoka kolemba, mpongi ezali kokimakima ye mpe azali kokanisa ete azwi maladi ya mpongi (Trypanosomiase ya bato ya Afrika) mpe atuni, Monganga, lolenge nini nakoki kolandela maladi oyo ya mpongi, mpamba te, ezali kobebisa pologalame na ngai ya mosala?

Eyano: Atako nazali koyoka mitungisi na yo na oyo etali maladi ya mpongi mpe bopusi na yango na mosala na yo, ezali mpasi ozala na yango, mingimingi soki ofandaka na bisika oyo maladi epalangani makasi te (lokola Amerika ya Nordi mpe mikili ya Mpoto).
Maladi ya mpongi ezwamaka mingimingi na bamboka ya Afrika mpe ewutaka na koswa ya nzinzi ya etuná.
Owuti kosala mobembo na mboka moko ya Afrika ya sudi ya Sahara?

Bilembo na yo ya nzoto kolemba mpe kozanga mpongi ezali eloko oyo ekomaka mpe ekoki kowuta na biloko kilikili, totangi konyokwama na makanisi, nzoto bosoto, maladi oyo ebombami na nse lokola kokangama ya mpema, maladi ya thyroide mpe mpasi ya makanisi.
Kokende epai ya monganga ezali eloko ya motuya mpo na kosalisa ekzame oyo esengeli.
Bakotuna yo mituna ebele na mae matali bilembo na yo, maladi na yo ya kala, bisika oyo osala mobembo mpe lolenge ya bomoi.
Bakoki mpe kosenga yo osalisa baekzame misusu, lokola baekzame ya makila, mpo na kolongola biwutelo misusu.
Komizwela yo moko nkisi te mpe komeka te komisala yo moko baekzame ya maladi ya mpongi.
Ezali bokono ya makasi oyo ezali kosenga bolandeli ya monganga monene mpe bankisi oyo esengeli.
Komeka kobundisa yango biso moko ekoki kowumisa elombo moko mpe nkisi oyo esengeli mpo na ewutelo ya solo ya bilembo na yo.
Na yango mpo na kobundisa kolemba na yo mpe kozanga na yo ya mpongi, etambe ya liboso mpe ya motuya ezali ya kozwa programe ya kokutana na monganga na yo ntangu nyonso.
Limbolela ye mitungisi na yo mpe loba solo na mae matali bilembo na yo.
Bazali lisungi monene mpo na kosalisa yo na koyeba penza oyo ozali na yango mpe kolakisa yo lolenge malamu ya kosala makambu.

Liboso, meka kozala na bopeto ya malamu na mae matali mpongi: landela programe moko ya kolala, luka momesano moko ya kosala yambo ya kolala mpe tika komela biloko oyo ezali na kafé liboso ya komata na mbetu.

srcs: Question: My female friend complains of bleeding, neck pain and thinks she has Crimean-Congo Hemorrhagic Fever and asks, I hope it is not a dreadful thing?
Answer: Tell your friend to immediately go to a hospital or doctor.
Crimean-Congo Hemorrhagic Fever (CCHF) is a serious viral disease and requires prompt medical attention.
It's not something to take chances with.
Trying to self-diagnose or treat it is dangerous.
While bleeding and neck pain can be symptoms of CCHF, they are also symptoms of many other illnesses, some far less serious.
A doctor will be able to determine what's actually causing her symptoms and provide appropriate treatment.
Reassure her that getting checked out is the best course of action, regardless of the cause.
Early diagnosis and treatment are crucial for CCHF and many other conditions.
trgs: Motuna: Moninga na ngai ya mwasi azali kobimisa makila, azali koyoka mpasi na kingo mpe azali kobanza ete azali na fefele ya makila ya Crimee-Congo mpe Atuni, Nazali kolikya ete ezali likama monene penza te?
Eyano: Yebisa moninga na yo akende na lobangu epai ya monganga moko to na lopitalo.
Fefele ya makila ya Crimee-Congo (CCHF) ezali bokono ya makasi oyo esengaka kolandelama na monganga.
Ezali eloko ya kosakana na yango te.
Komeka komizwela nkisi to komitalela yo moko ezali likama.
Atako kobimisa makila mpe koyoka mpasi na kingo ezalaka bilembo ya bokono ya CCHF, ezalaka mpe bilembo ya maladi kilikili, misusu oyo ezalaka makasi penza te.
Monganga akoki kozala na makoki ya koyeba ndimbola ya solo ya bilembo na ye mpe kopesa ye nkisi oyo ebongi.
Kitisa motema na ye na kolakisa ye ete kokende kosalisa baekzame ezali eloko ya malamu ya kosala, ezala bilembo ya ndenge nini.
Ekzame moko mpe nkisi na lobangu ezali eloko ya motuya mpo na bokono ya CCHF mpe bamaladi misusu.

srcs: Question: My male neighbor complains of jaundice, fever, bleeding and thinks he has Yellow Fever and asks, What are the causes
Answer: While your neighbor's symptoms do overlap with Yellow Fever, it's crucial to understand that self-diagnosing is dangerous, especially with a serious illness like Yellow Fever.
He needs to see a doctor immediately for proper testing and diagnosis.
Yellow fever is caused by the yellow fever virus, which is spread through the bite of an infected Aedes aegypti mosquito.
These mosquitoes also transmit diseases like Zika and Dengue.
It's not contagious from person to person.
Essentially, the only cause of Yellow Fever is infection with the yellow fever virus transmitted by the bite of an infected mosquito.
There's no other way to contract it.
It's important to reiterate that your neighbor needs professional medical attention.
His symptoms could be from a number of other illnesses, some serious, and delaying proper diagnosis and treatment can have serious consequences.
trgs: Motuna: Mozalani na ngai ya mobali azali na loposo ya mosaka, azali na fefele mpe kobima makila. Azali kobanza ete azali na bokono ya Kongo mpe atuni boye: Ewutaka wapi

Eyano: Atako bilembo ya mozalani na yo ezali ndenge moko na oyo ya bokono ya Kongo, ezali likambo ya ntina koyeba ete komitalela biso moko ezalaka likama, mingimingi mpo na maladi lokola bokono ya Kongo.
Asengeli kokutana na monganga na lobangu mpo na kosalisa baekzame oyo esengeli.
Bokono ya Kongo ewutaka na virisi ya Kongo, oyo epalanganaka na koswa ya ngungi babengi Aedes aegypti oyo azali na maladi.
Bangungi yango epesaka lisusu bamaladi lokola Zika mpe Dengue.
Okoki kopesa yango bato mosusu te.
Na bokuse, Bokono ya Kongo ewutaka na virisi ya Kongo oyo yaka na koswa ya ngungi oyo ezali kobela yango.
Lolenge mosusu ya kozwa bokono yango ezali te.
Ezalika eloko ya motuya mingingi kokundola ete mozalani na yo azali na mposa ya lisalisi ya monganga.
Bilembo na ye ekoki kowuta na bamaladi misusu kilikili, misusu ezali ya makasi koleka, kozongisa ekzame mpe nkisi oyo ebongi na nsima ekoki komema mbeba ya makasi.

srcs: Question: My female classmate complains of fever, chills, headache and thinks she has Malaria and asks, Malaria is more common with people coming from Mozambique.
So are you from there and how do you know you got it?
Answer: "I understand you're not feeling well and are worried about malaria.
It's definitely important to take symptoms like fever, chills, and headache seriously.
However, I can't diagnose you, and self-diagnosing can be risky.
Lots of illnesses share those symptoms.
As for your question about where I'm from and my health, I’d prefer not to share personal details.
The most important thing right now is for you to see a doctor to figure out what's going on and get the right treatment.
They can run tests to determine if it’s malaria or something else and give you the best advice.
Delaying proper medical care can be harmful, so please make an appointment as soon as possible."
trgs: Motuna: Moninga na ngai ya kelasi ya mwasi azali na fefele, kolenga mpe mutu mpasi. Azali kokanisa etre azali na malaria mpe atuni soki malaria ezalaka mini na bato oyo bautaka mboka ya Mozambique.
Toloba ete owuti kuna mpe ndenge nini oyebi ete ozali na yango?
Eyano: Nazoyokela yo mawa na ndenge ozali komiyoka malamu te mpe mitungisi na yo mpo na malaria.
Ezali mpeza eloko ya motuya kotalela bilembo lokola bafefele, kolenga mpe mutu mpasi.
Kasi nakoki kosala penza ekzame te mpe mbano ekoki kopesa likama.
Maladi ebele ezalaka na bilembo ya lolenge moko.
Na oyo etali motuna na yo mpo na mboka na ngai mpe kolongono ya nzoto na ngai, nalingi te tolobela yango.
Eloko ya ntina na miniti oyo ezali ete okokoka kokutana na monganga mpo na ozwa ndimbola ya makambu mpe kozwa nkisi oyo ebongi.
Bakoki kosala baekzame mpo na koyeba soki ezali malaria penza, to biloko mosusu mpe kopesa yo ba toli ya malamu.
Kozangisa na nsima likambu ya kolanda nkisi epai ya monganga ekoki kozala mabe, kende kokutana na monganga noki.''

srcs: Question: My female classmate complains of fever, chills and thinks she has Malaria and asks, "What specific precautions or measures should I take to prevent malaria recurrence?"
Answer: Tell your classmate that it's crucial she doesn't self-treat and sees a doctor immediately for diagnosis and treatment.
Malaria can be serious, even fatal, if not treated promptly.
Suspecting malaria isn't the same as having a confirmed diagnosis.
Once she has seen a doctor and if she is diagnosed with malaria and completes her prescribed medication, these are some precautions she can take to prevent recurrence:
Continue preventative medication as prescribed: Her doctor may prescribe medication to be taken regularly during and after travel to malaria-endemic areas.
It’s crucial to adhere to the prescribed regimen.
Mosquito bite prevention is paramount:
Sleep under insecticide-treated mosquito nets (ITNs): Ensure the net is properly tucked in and has no holes.
Wear long-sleeved clothing and long pants, especially during dawn and dusk: Mosquitoes are most active during these times.
Use insect repellents containing DEET (diethyltoluamide), picaridin, or IR3535: Follow the instructions on the product label.
Consider using mosquito coils or insecticide-treated vaporizers indoors.
Eliminate mosquito breeding grounds around her home: This includes removing standing water from flower pots, buckets, and other containers.

If travelling to malaria-endemic regions again, consult her doctor well in advance: They can recommend appropriate preventative medication and other precautionary measures based on the specific region and her medical history.
Be aware of potential relapse symptoms and seek immediate medical attention if they occur: Even after treatment, malaria parasites can sometimes persist in the liver and cause a relapse.
Again, the most important first step is to encourage her to seek immediate medical attention.
Don't delay!
trgs: Motuna: Moninga na ngai ya kelasi ya mwasi azali na fefele, kolenga mpe azali kobanza ete azali na malaria mpe Atuni boye, "Makambu nini nakosala penza mpo na koboya kozonga ya malaria ?"
Eyano: Yebisa moninga na yo ya kelasi ete asengeli komizwela nkisi te mpe akende kokutana na monganga na lobangu mpo na kosalisa ekzame mpe kozwa nkisi.
Malaria ekoki kozala makasi penza, ntangu mosusu ekoki koboma, soki ozweli yango nkisi na lobangu te.
Kobanza ete ozali na malaria ezali lolenge moko te na kozwa mbano na yango na nsima ya ekzame.
Ntangu akokutana na monganga moko, soki bayebisi ye ete azali na malaria mpe ntangu akosilisa komela bankisi oyo bakokomela ye, tala makambu asengeli kosala mpo na koboya ezongela ye lisusu:

Kokoba komela bankisi ya komibatela oyo bokomeli ye: Monganga na ye akoki kokomela ye bankisi ya komela mikolo nyonso na boumeli mpe na nsima ya kosala mobembo na bisika oyo malaria epalanganaka makasi.
Ezali eloko ya motuya kolandela nkisi bakomeli yo.
Komibatela na koswa ya bangungi ezali eloko ya motuya:
Lela na mosikitele oyo ezali na nkisi ya koboma banyama-nkeke (ITNs): sala ete mosikitele ezala ya kokota malamu mpe ezali na lidusu te.
Lata bilamba ya maboko milayi mpe bapatalo ya milayi, mingimingi na ntongo mpe na mpokwa: Bangungi bazalaka makasi na ntangu wana.
Salela bankisi oyo ebenganaka ba nyama-nkeke oyo ezali na DEET (diethyltoluamide), pikardini to IR3535: landa malako oyo ezali na nkoma oyo ezali likolo.
Kanisa kosalela bibaluka oyo ebenganaka bangungi to masini ya kopupola oyo ezali na nkisi ya nyama-nkeke na kati.
Boma bandako ya banyama oyo bangungi esalaka na nzinganzinga ya naku: Yango elakisi kolongola mayi oyo etelamaka na banzungu ya fololo, bakatini to bibombeli misusu.

Soki akosala lisusu mobembo na bisika oyo malaria ezali kopalangana makasi, kutana liboso na monganga: akoki kokomela ye bankisi oyo ebongi ya komela liboso mpe kosala makambu misusu na kolanda esika mpe maladi na ye ya kala.

Tya likebi penza na bilembo oyo ekoki komonisa konzolea ya maladi mpe kutana na lobangu na monganga soki bilembo ezongi lisusu: Atako na nsima ya komela nkisi moko, virisi ya malaria ekoki kobombama na libale mpe kozongela yo lisusu.
Nalobi yango lisusu, litambe ya liboso oyo ezali ya ntina ezali kolendisa ye mpo na kokutana na monganga moko na lobangu.
Kozela te!

srcs: Question: What precautions should I take to prevent the spread of typhoid fever to others, particularly my household members or close contacts?
Answer:
Typhoid fever is a serious bacterial infection that can spread easily to others through contaminated food and water or close contact.
Here's a breakdown of the precautions:
Handwashing: This is the single most important measure.
Thorough handwashing with soap and water, especially after using the toilet and before handling food, removes bacteria and prevents transmission.
Disinfecting Contaminated Surfaces: Typhoid bacteria can survive on surfaces.
Regularly disinfecting frequently touched surfaces like countertops, doorknobs, and bathroom fixtures with a household disinfectant helps prevent spread.
Food Handling Precautions: Individuals with typhoid fever should not prepare or serve food for others while they are ill and for a period after recovery as determined by a healthcare professional.
This prevents contamination of food.
Avoid Sharing Personal Items: Sharing personal items like towels, utensils, and drinking glasses can spread the bacteria.
Each individual should use their own dedicated items.
Vaccination: Typhoid vaccines are available and can provide substantial protection against the disease.
Vaccination is recommended for travelers to areas where typhoid is common and for individuals with close contact with a typhoid carrier.
Prompt Treatment: Getting prompt medical treatment with appropriate antibiotics helps shorten the duration of illness and reduces the risk of complications and spread to others.
It's also crucial to complete the full course of antibiotics even if symptoms improve.
trgs: Motuna: Makambo nini nakoki kosala mpo na koboya kopalangana ya fefele ya typhoide na batu mosusu, mingimingi na bato na ngai ya libota mpe bamisusu oyo nafandaka na bango?
Eyano:
Fefele ya typhoide ezali bokono moko ya mikrobe ya makasi oyo ekoki kopalangana na pete na batu mosusu na nzela ya bilei mpe mayi to na kosimba makasi.
Tala bozongeli moko ya makambu ya kosala:
Kosukola maboko: Ezali likambu ya motuya mingi.
Kosukola maboko malamu na mayi mpe sabuni, mingimingi na nsima ya kowuta zongo mpe liboso ya kosimba bilei, ezali koboma mikrobe mpe kopekisa kopalangana na yango.
Kopetolama ya bisika oyo ezali na mikrobe: Mikrobe ya typhoide ekoki kofanda na bisika mingi.
Petola mbala na mbala bisika ya polele oyo osimbaka mingimingi lokola kontware, bisimbeli ya bikuke mpe bisaleli ya kikoso na nkisi ya kopetola na yango, ezali kopekisa kopalangana.

Makebisi na kosalela bilei: bato oyo bazali na fefele ya typhoide basengeli te kolamba to kokabola bilei na batu misusu na boumeli ya bokono na bango mpe na nsima ya eleko moko soki basilisi komela nkisi, na kolanda lolenge ekomama na monganga.
Yango nde ezali kopekisa bokono na bilei.
Tika kosalela biloko moko na bato misusu: Kosalela biloko moko na batu lokola esume, bisaleli mpe bakopo ekoki kopalanganisa bamikrobe.
Moto na moto asengeli kosalela biloko na ye moko.
Kokatama mangwele: Mangwele mpo na kobundisa typhoide ezali komonana mpe ekoki kobatela moto na maladi.
Mangwele masengami na baoyo bazali kosala mobembo na bisika oyo bokono ya typhoide ezali mingi mpe mpo na bato oyo bafandaki penza na baoyo babandaki kobela bokono ya typhoide.
Nkisi na lobangu: Komela bankisi lokola baantibiotique oyo ebongi na lobangu ezali kosunga na kokitisa koumela ya maladi mpe kobatela na makama mpe na kopalanganisa yango na bamisusu.
Ezali mpe malamu makasi kokende kino na nsuka ya baantibiotique oyo ozali komela atako bilembo esi esila.

srcs: Question: My male coursemate complains of fever, chills, sweats and thinks he has Malaria and asks, I have had malaria for the 3rd time this year, Is there any preventive measures that can be taken?
Answer: "It sounds pretty rough dealing with what you think is malaria multiple times.
It's definitely worth getting checked out by a doctor each time to confirm the diagnosis and get the right treatment, because recurring fevers can be a sign of other things too.
Self-treating can sometimes mask the real problem.
As for prevention, there are a few things you can do, especially if you're in an area where malaria is common.
Using mosquito nets, especially ones treated with insecticide, is really important.
Also, wearing long sleeves and pants, particularly during dawn and dusk when mosquitoes are most active, can help.
There are also insect repellents containing DEET or picaridin that are effective.

Some people also take antimalarial medication preventatively if they're traveling to or living in high-risk areas, but you should talk to a doctor about that to see if it's the right option for you and what type would be best.
They can assess your individual risk and make sure you're aware of any potential side effects."
trgs: Motuna: Moninga na ngai ya kelasi azali na fefele, kolenga mpe motoki. Abanzi azali na malaria mpe atuni: Nazali na malaria elandani mbala 3 na mobu oyo. Ezali na makambu moko nakoki kosala mpo na kopekisa yango ezwa ngai?
Eyano: ''Ezali mpasi mingi kofanda na maladi oyo ozali kobanza ete ezali malaria mbala mingi bongo.

Ezali penza eloko ya motuna kokutana na monganga mbala nyonso mpo kondimisa ete ezali bongo maladi yango mpe kozwa lisalisi lisengeli, mpamba te, bafefele ya mbala na mbala ekoki mpe komonisa bokono mosusu.
Komizwela biso moko nkisi ekoki kobomba bokono ya solo.
Na mae matali komibatela, ezali na makambo moko oyo okoki kosala, mingimingi soki ofandaka na bisika malaria ezalaka ebele.
Kosalela musikitele, mingimingi oyo ezali na nkisi ya bangungi, ezali eloko ya motuya.
Kolata mpe biloko ya maboko milayi mpe bapatalo, mingimingi na ntongo mpe na mpokwa ntangu bangungi bazali ebele, ekoki mpe kosunga.
Ezali mpe na nkisi ya kobengana nango bangungi oyo ezali na DEET to pikaridini ya makasi na kati.

Batu misusu bamelaka bankisi ya kobundisa malaria mpo na komibatela na ntangu ya kosala mobembo to soki bafandaka na bisika ya likama makasi, kasi osengeli kolobela yango monganga moko mpo na kopesa yo liponi ya malamu mpo na yo.
Bakoki kotalela likama na yo moko mpe kolakisa yo bampasi nyonso oyo eyaka na nsima.''

srcs: Question: My male neighbor complains of joint pain, vomiting and thinks he has Rift Valley fever and asks, What measures can I take to prevent further transmission of Rift Valley fever to others, especially considering its potential for spreading through mosquito bites or contact with infected animals?
Answer: Tell your neighbor he needs to see a doctor immediately to get a proper diagnosis and treatment.
Rift Valley Fever can be serious, and self-treating is dangerous.
While waiting for medical attention, he should take the following precautions to minimize the risk of spreading the disease (if it is indeed RVF):
Mosquito bite prevention: This is paramount.
He should use mosquito repellent containing DEET, picaridin, or IR3535 liberally.
He should wear long sleeves, long pants, and socks whenever possible, especially during dawn and dusk when mosquitoes are most active.
Mosquito netting around his bed would also be helpful.
Eliminate standing water around his home where mosquitoes breed (e.g., flower pots, buckets, discarded tires).
Animal contact precautions: Avoid contact with any animals, especially livestock, that appear sick or are dead.
If he must handle animals (e.g., he's a farmer), he should wear protective clothing, including gloves and a mask.
He should not slaughter any animals himself and should report any suspicious animal deaths to the local veterinary authorities.
Raw milk should not be consumed – it must be pasteurized.
Hygiene: Frequent handwashing with soap and water is crucial, especially after handling animals or animal products.
Avoid touching his eyes, nose, and mouth with unwashed hands.
He should also practice good hygiene when coughing or sneezing, covering his mouth and nose with a tissue or his elbow.
He should avoid sharing personal items like towels, eating utensils, and drinking glasses.

Isolation (to a reasonable extent): While complete isolation might not be necessary at this stage (before a diagnosis), he should limit close contact with others as much as possible until he sees a doctor.
This is particularly important for pregnant women, who are at higher risk of severe complications from RVF.
Emphasize to your neighbor again that these are precautionary measures and do not replace the need to see a doctor immediately.
A blood test is needed to confirm the diagnosis and appropriate treatment will be necessary.
Also, if he suspects he has RVF, he needs to inform local health authorities so they can monitor the situation and take appropriate public health measures.
trgs: Motuna: Mozalani na ngai azali koyoka matonga mpasi, kosanza mpe abanzi azali na bokono ya fefele ya ngomba ya Rift. Atuni: Makambo nini nakoki kosala mpo na kozanga kopanza bokono ya fefele ya ngomba ya Rift na batu mosusu, na kotalela mingimingi bokasi ya bopalangani bwa yango na koswa ya bangungi to kosimbasimba ba nyama oyo bazali kobela yango?
Eyano: Yebisa mozalani na yo ete asengeli kokende kokutana na monganga kaka sikoyo mpo na kosalisa baekzame mpe kozwa lisalisi oyo esengeli.
Fefele ya ngomba ya Rift ekoki kozala makasi mpe komizwela nkisi ekoki kobimisa likama monene.
Na kozela nkisi ya monganga, asengeli kosala makambu oyo mpo na kokitisa likama ya kopanza bokono oyo (soki ezali penza bokono ya RVF):
Komibateka na koswa ya bangungi: Ezali eloko ya motuya koleka.
Asengeli kosalela makasi penza nkisi ya kobenganela bangungi oyo ezali na DEET, pikardini, to IR3535.
Asengeli kolata biloko ya maboko milayi, pantalo ya molayi mpe elamba ya nse ya bozito, mingimingi na ntongo mpe na mpokwa ntangu bangungi bazalaka mingi.
Kotya musikitele na mbetu na ye ezali mpe na motuya.
Kolongola mayi oyo etelemaka na nzinganzinga ya ndaku esika wapi bangungi babotamaka (na ndakisa, nzungu ya fololo, bakantini, piné ya kala).
Libateli na oyo etali kosimbasimba ba nyama: Boya kosimbasimba nyama nyonso, mingimingi bibwele oyo ezali komonana maladi to baoyo bakufa.
Soki asengeli kosimbasimba banyama (na ndakisa soki azali mosali bilanga) asengeli kolata bilamba ya komibatela, mingimingi ba gan mpe maske.
Asengeli te komibomela ye moko banyama mpe asengeli kolakisa liwa nyonso ya nyama oyo ezali kokamwisa na baminganga oyo balandelaka makambu ya nyama.
Asengeli komela miliki ya malili te, asengeli kotya yango na moto.
Bopeto: Kosokola mingi maboko na mayi mpe sabuni ezali eloko ya motuya koleka, mingimingi na nsima ya kosimbasimba banyama to biloko oyo ewutaka na bango.
Tika komisimba misu, zolo mpe monoko na maboko oyo esokolami naino te.
Asengeli lisusu kozala na bopeto ya malamu ntangu azali kokosola to kosala likisé, na kozipa monoko to zolo na mwa elamba ya maboko to lipeko.
Asengeli kotika kosalela biloko na ye moko elongo na batu misusu lokola sani to kopo.

Kokabwana na bato (na lolenge moko ya malamu): Atako kokabwana penza na batu nyonso ezali naino na ntina te (liboso ya kosalisa ekzame), asengeli kokitisa bokutani na bato misusu tii na ntangu akokutana na monganga.
Yango ezali na motuya mingi mpo na basi ya zemi oyo bazali na likama monene ya kozwa mikakatano mingi oyo ewuti na RVF.
Yebisa lisusu mozalani na yo ete oyo elandi ezali bongoi makambu ya kosala kaka mpo na komibatela kasi ezali kolongola ata moke te bokutani na monganga na lombangu.
Asengeli kosalisa ekzame ya makila mpo na kondimisa bokono mpe kozwa nkisi oyo esengeli.

Kutu soki azali komiyoka ete azwi bokono ya Fefele ya ngomba ya Rift (RVF) asengeli koyebisa yango na mbala moko bataleli ya makambu ya kolongono ya nzoto mpo bakoka kotalela likambo mpe kozwa bikateli bisengeli mpo na kobatela bato.

srcs: Question: My female classmate complains of fever, chills, headache and thinks she has Malaria and asks, Besides testing for malaria, are there any other potential causes for my symptoms, especially considering my recent travel history?
Answer: Yes, absolutely.
While malaria is a possibility, especially with travel to a malaria-endemic region, several other illnesses can cause fever, chills, and headache.
Depending on where she traveled, some of the possibilities include:
Other mosquito-borne illnesses: Dengue fever, Zika virus, Chikungunya virus, and West Nile virus all share similar symptoms with malaria.
Viral infections: Influenza, common cold, COVID-19, and other viral infections can cause these symptoms.
Bacterial infections: Typhoid fever, urinary tract infections, and bacterial pneumonia can also present with fever, chills, and headache.
Tick-borne illnesses: Lyme disease, Rocky Mountain spotted fever, and other tick-borne illnesses can cause these symptoms, though headache is less prominent in some.

Parasitic infections: Other parasitic infections besides malaria, like amebiasis or giardiasis (depending on where she travelled and what she ate/drank) are possibilities, though they often come with gastrointestinal symptoms as well.
Heat stroke/heat exhaustion: If she was in a hot climate and exerted herself, this could be a cause.
Other less common infections: Depending on the region of travel, things like leptospirosis or brucellosis could be considered, although these are less common.
It's crucial that she tell her doctor exactly where she traveled and what she did there (e.g., hiking, swimming in fresh water, eating street food).
This information will help the doctor narrow down the possibilities and order the appropriate tests.
It's important she doesn't self-treat and seeks professional medical advice.
trgs: Motuna: Moninga na ngai ya kelasiazali kolenga, koyoka mutu pasi mpe azali kobanza ete azali kobela malaria mpe Atuni boye, Longola ekzame ya kotalela malaria, ekoki kozala na biwutlo mosusu ya bilembo na ngai, na kotalela mingimingi mibembo na ngai nawuti kosala?
Eyano: Ee, ezali.
Atako ekoki kozala malaria, mingimingi soki osalaki mobembo na esika oyo malaria epanzanaka mpamba mpamba, babokono misusu ekoki mpe kosala yo fefele, kolenga mpe mutu pasi.
Na kolanda bisika akendaki, botala makoki:
Bokono misusu ewutaka na bangungi: maladi ya dengue, irisi ya z, virisi ya chikungunya mpe virisi ya Nile, yango nyonso ezali na bilembo ya ndenge moko na malaria.
Bokono ya mimpumpululu: Gripe, miyoyo, corona mpe bokono misusu ya mimpumpululu ekoki komonisa mpe bilembo yango.
Bokono ya bavirisi: fefele ya typhoidi, bokono ya nzela ya masuba mpe bokono ya mpema ekoki mpe komonisama na fefele, kolenga mpe moto mpasi.
Mpe bokono misusu ewutaka na basili ekoki kobimisa bilembo yango, atako mutu mpasi eyokanaka mingi te epai bato misusu.

Bokono ya mikrobe: Bokono misusu ya mikrobe na malaria na kati, lokola amibiaze to giardiaze (na kolanda bisika wapi asalaki mobembo, biloko alyaki mpe amelaki) ekoki komonana, atako mingimingi yango ebelisaka libumu.
Moto na nzoto/kolemba likolo ya moto: Soki azalaki na klima ya moto mpe asalaki mosala makasi, ekoki kozala moko ya biwutelo.
Bokono misusu oyo ekutanaka na mpasi: Na kolanda esika oyo asalaki mobembo, maladi lokola leptospirose to brucellose ekoki mpe kotangama, atako ezwamaka na mpasi.

Ezali likambo ya ntina akoka koyebisa polele na monganga na ye esika wapi asalaki mobembo mpe makambo asalaki kuna (na ndakisa, kotambola makolo, kosukola na mayi ya moto, bilei batekaka na balabala).
Makambo yango ekosalisa monganga ya kokitisa motango ya makoki mpe kokomela yo baekzame oyo esengeli.
Ezali ntina makasi koboya komizwela nkisi ye moko mpe akende kokutana na monganga.

srcs: Question: My male coursemate complains of fever, chills, sweats and thinks he has Malaria and asks, What specific precautions or preventive measures should I take to avoid contracting malaria in the future, especially if I'm traveling to endemic areas?
Answer: Tell your friend to see a doctor immediately to get tested and treated if he does have malaria.
It's not something to mess around with.
As for his question about prevention, here's what you can tell him:
Malaria prevention is multi-pronged and depends heavily on where he's travelling, as different regions have different mosquito species and resistance patterns.
He should consult a travel health specialist or his doctor for personalized recommendations, but generally speaking, here are the key precautions:
Antimalarial medication: This is crucial.
There are several different types, and the best one for him will depend on his destination, medical history, and other factors.
A doctor needs to prescribe this, and it's often taken before, during, and after the trip.
Do not self-medicate.
Mosquito bite prevention: This is the cornerstone of malaria prevention and includes:
Insect repellent: Use repellents containing DEET (20-50%), picaridin (20%), or IR3535 (20-30%).
Apply to exposed skin and clothing, following product instructions.
Long-sleeved clothing and pants: Wear loose, light-colored clothing that covers most of your body, especially during dawn and dusk when mosquitoes are most active.
Treat clothing with permethrin insecticide for added protection (don't apply directly to skin).
Mosquito nets: Sleep under insecticide-treated mosquito nets, ensuring they are properly tucked in and have no holes.
Mosquito-proof accommodation: Stay in places with screened windows and doors, or use air conditioning to keep mosquitoes out.
Consider mosquito coils or vaporizers if needed.
Environmental control: While this is more of a public health measure, being aware helps.
Minimizing standing water around accommodations can reduce breeding grounds for mosquitoes.
Be aware of symptoms: Even with precautions, there's a small risk of contracting malaria.
Knowing the symptoms (fever, chills, sweats, headache, muscle aches, fatigue, nausea, vomiting) is crucial.
If he develops any of these during or after travel to a malaria-endemic area, he should seek medical attention immediately.
Early diagnosis and treatment are essential.
Again, emphasize to your friend that seeing a doctor right away is the most important step right now for his health.
These prevention tips are for future trips.
trgs: Motuna: Moninga na ngai ya kelasi azali kolenge lenga, azali kotoka mpe abanzi ete azali na malaria. Makambo nini akoki kosala mpo na komibatela na likama oyo ya kozwa malaria na mikolo mizali koya, mingimingi soki nasali mobembo na bisika epai wapi malaria ezali kopalangana makasi?
Eyano: Yebisa moninga na yo mpo akende kokutana mbala moko na monganga mpo asalisa baekzame mpe azwa nkisi ya malaria.
Ezali eloko ya kozwa na maseki te.
Na oyo etali motuna na ye mpo na komibatela, tala makambo oyo tokoki koyebisa ye:

Komibatela na bokona ya malaria ezali na makambo ebele ya kosala mpe ezali kotalela mingimingi bisika epai wapi asalaka mibembo, mpamba te, bisika kilikili ezali na bangungi ya ndenge na ndenge mpe bokasi na bango ezalaka na lolenge moko te.

Asengeli kokutana na nganga buka ya makambu ya kolongono ya nzoto ya baoyo basalak amibembo to mpe monganga na ye moko mpo na kopesa ye ba toli ebongi na ye, kasi na bokuse, tala makambo ya ntina oyo akoki kosala:
Ba nkisi ya kobundisa malaria: Ezali eloko ya motuya koleka.
Ezalaka ya ndenge na ndenge, mpe oyo ya malamu penza ekotalela esika azali kosala mobembo, makambo na ye ya kala na mae matali maladi mpe makambu mosusu.
Monganga moko asengeli kokomela ye yango mpe mingi mingi ezwamaka liboso ya kosala mobembo wana, na nzela mpe na nsima na yango.
Komizwela nkisi yo moko te.
Komibatela na koswa ya bangungi: ezali libanga ya litumu na mae matali komibatela na malaria mpe osengeli:
Nkisi ya kobenga nango bangungi: Salela nkisi oyo ezali na DEET (20-50%), pikardini (20%) to IR3535 (20-30%).
Kotya yango na loposo ya polele mpe na bilamba, na kolanda malako mapesameli na mosali na yango.

Bilamba ya maboko milayi mpe bapatalo: Lata bilamaba oyo etiki nzoto mpe ya langi ya pole oyo ezali kozipa eteni monene ya nzoto na yo, mingimingi na ntongo mpe na mpokwa, ntangu bangungi bazalaka makasi.
Tya nkisi ya koboma na yango nyama-nkeke oyo esalema na permethrine na kati na bilamba na yo mpo na komibatela na bangungi (kopakola nkisi yango na loposo ya nzoto te).
Mosikitele: Lala na nse ya mosikitele oyo etyami na nkisi ya nyama-nkeke, tala soki okotisi yango malamu mpe soki ezali na madusu te.
Ndaku oyo ekotisaka bangungi te: Fanda na bisika oyo ezali na maninisa mpe bikuke ebombama na mosikitele, to salela bapakapaka ya malili mpo na kopekisa kokota ya bangungi.
Kanisa mpe kosalela bilingama oyo ebenganaka bangungi to masini ya kopupola.
Kotalela nzinganzinga: Atako ezali likambo oyo etalaka misala ya leta oyo elandelaka kolongono ya nzto ya bayi mboka, bolendisi ezali na motuya.
Kokitisa mayi oyo etelemaka nzinganzinga ya ndaku ekoki koboma bisika mingi oyo ebotaka bangungi.
Tya llikebi na yo na bilembo: Atako osali makambo wana mpo na komibatela, okoki kaka kozwa maladi ya malaria.
Koyeba bilembo (fefele, kolenga, motoki, mpasi na misunyi, kolemba, koyoka motema ya kobaluka, kosanza) ezali na ntina mingi.
Soki abandi moko ya bilembo oyo naboumeli to na nsima ya kosala mobembo moko na esika epai wapi malaria epalanganaka mingi, asengeli kokutana na monganga mbala moko.
Kosala ekzame mpe kozwa nkisi noki ezali malamu penza.
Loba lisusu na moninga na yo ete, kokende noki kokutana na monganga na ye ezali litambe moko ya motuya mpo na kolongono ya nzoto na ye.
Ba toli ya lolenge ya komibatela oyo ezali mpo na mibembo na yo mizali koya.

srcs: Question: My male neighbor complains of fever, rash and thinks he has Dengue Fever and asks, "What specific precautions should I take to prevent dengue fever complications?"
Answer: Tell your neighbor that since he suspects dengue fever, it's crucial he see a doctor immediately for proper diagnosis and management.
Dengue can be dangerous, and complications can arise quickly.
Self-treating is risky.
While waiting for his appointment, he should:
Rest: This helps the body fight the infection.
He needs to avoid strenuous activities.
Hydrate: Drink plenty of fluids, like water, electrolyte solutions, or broths, to prevent dehydration, which is a common dengue complication.
Avoid sugary drinks.
Pain Relief: He can take over-the-counter pain relievers like acetaminophen (Tylenol) to manage fever and pain.
Absolutely avoid ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin), aspirin, and naproxen (Aleve) as these can increase the risk of bleeding, a serious dengue complication.
Monitor for Warning Signs: He should watch closely for any warning signs like severe abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, bleeding gums, rapid breathing, or fatigue/restlessness.
If any of these occur, he should seek immediate medical attention, potentially going to the emergency room.
These could indicate severe dengue.
Mosquito Control: Even though he's already likely infected, he should prevent further mosquito bites to avoid spreading dengue to others.
This means using mosquito repellent, wearing long sleeves and pants, and sleeping under a mosquito net.
Emphasize again that he needs to see a doctor as soon as possible.
This advice is not a substitute for professional medical care.
trgs: Motuna: Mozalani na ngai azali na fefele mpe azali kobanza ete azali kobela bokono ya Dengue. Azali kotuna ngai: "Makambu nini oyo nakoki kosala mpo na koboya mikakatano ya fefele?''
Eyano: Yebisa mozalani na yo ete lokola azali kobanza na fefele ya Dengue, ezali malamu makasi akende kosalisa baekzame noki epai ya monganga mpo na koyeba mpe kozwa lisalisi oyo ebongi.
Fefele ya Dengue ekoki kokoma likama monene mpe kokola na yango ekoki kosalema mbangu.
Komizwela nkisi ekoki komema likama penza.
Na kozela bokutani na ye, asengeli:
Kopema: Yango ezali kosalisa nzoto mpo na kobundisa bokono.
Asengeli koboya kosala misala ya makasi.
Mela mayi: Mala biloko ya maimai ebele, lokola mayi ya komela, biloko mosusu to supu, mpo na kopekisa kozanga mayi na nzoto, likama oyo ewutaka mingimingi na fefele ya Dengue.
Boya bimeli oyo esalemi na sukali.
Kosilisa mpasi: Akoki kosomba nkisi ya kokitisa na yango mpasi oyo eekemaka pambapamba lokola acetaminophene (Tylenol) mpo na kokitisa fefele mpe mpasi.
Boya penza ibuprofene (Advil, Motrin), aspirine mpe naproxene (Aleve), mpamba te ekoki kobimisisa yo makila, oyo ezali likama monene ya fefele ya Dengue.
Kotalela bilembo ya likebisi: Asengeli kolandela elembo nyonso ya likebisi lokola mpasi makasi na libumu, kosanzasanza, makila na minu, kopema na lobangu, kolemba/ kozala likolo likolo.
Soki moko ya bilembo oyo emonani, asengeli kokutana noki na monganga, mpe ntangu mosusu kokende na lopitalo.
Makambo oyo elandi ekoki komonisa fefele ya Dengue ya makasi.
Bundisa bangungi: Atako azali kobela bokono yango, asengeli kokima koswa mosusu ya bangungi mpo na koboya kopalanganisa Dengue epai ya bato misusu.
Elingi koloba kosalela nkisi ya kobengana bangungi, kolata bapatalo ya mikuse mpe kolala na nse ya mosikitele.
Lobela ye lisusu ete asengeli kokutana na monganga.
Toli oyo ezali kopekisa te kozwa misala ya nganga buka.

srcs: Question: My female friend complains of varied by disease and thinks she has Zoonotic Diseases and asks, What are the specific zoonotic diseases I should be concerned about based on my activities, lifestyle, and environment, and how can I prevent them
Answer: It's important to preface this by saying I am not a medical professional.
Your friend needs to see a doctor, not ask the internet, especially since she believes she has multiple diseases.
Self-diagnosing zoonotic diseases is particularly dangerous as some can be serious if left untreated.
I can give some general information, but it should not be taken as medical advice.
To answer her question properly, she needs to provide more information to a doctor.
However, some common zoonotic diseases and associated risk factors include:
Common Zoonotic Diseases & Associated Risk Factors:
Lyme disease: Transmitted by ticks.
Risk factors include spending time in wooded or grassy areas, having pets that go outdoors, and not performing regular tick checks.
Rocky Mountain spotted fever: Also tick-borne.
Similar risk factors to Lyme disease.
Toxoplasmosis: Caused by a parasite often found in cat feces and undercooked meat.
Pregnant women and individuals with weakened immune systems are at higher risk.
Gardening and handling cat litter are risk factors.
Rabies: Transmitted through the bite of an infected animal (e.g., bats, raccoons, skunks).
Risk factors include contact with wildlife, especially if the animal is behaving strangely.
Salmonella and Campylobacter: Bacterial infections often acquired through contact with contaminated food (especially poultry, eggs, and unpasteurized milk), reptiles, or contaminated water.
Ringworm: A fungal infection that can be transmitted from animals (especially cats and dogs) to humans through direct contact.
Psittacosis (Parrot Fever): A bacterial infection spread by birds, particularly parrots, parakeets, and pigeons.
Risk factors include handling infected birds or inhaling dust from their droppings.
Leptospirosis: A bacterial infection spread through contact with the urine of infected animals (e.g., rodents, livestock).
Risk factors include exposure to contaminated water or soil.
Prevention:
General preventative measures for zoonotic diseases often include:
Regular handwashing: Especially after handling animals, their food, or waste.
Safe food handling: Cook meat thoroughly, wash fruits and vegetables, and avoid unpasteurized dairy products.
Tick checks: After spending time outdoors, thoroughly check yourself, your children, and your pets for ticks.
Remove them promptly and correctly.
Vaccinations: Vaccinate your pets against rabies and other diseases.
There are also human vaccines for some zoonotic diseases (e.g., rabies).
Pest control: Control rodent and insect populations in and around your home.
Avoid contact with wildlife: Do not handle or feed wild animals.
Be cautious around unfamiliar animals, especially those exhibiting unusual behavior.
Protective clothing: Wear long sleeves, pants, and closed-toe shoes in areas where ticks or other disease-carrying insects may be present.
Use insect repellent containing DEET.
Again, this is not medical advice.
Your friend needs to consult a doctor.
Her concerns about having multiple zoonotic illnesses warrant professional medical evaluation.
It's possible her symptoms have a different underlying cause altogether.
Encourage her to seek medical attention as soon as possible.
trgs: Motuna: Moninga na ngai ezali komonisa bilembo kilikili, azali kobanza ete azali na maladi ya nyama babengi zoonoses mpe autuni ngai boye, Nasengeli kolandela virisi nini ya zoonoses na kotalela misala na ngai, lolenge na ngai ya kosalela bomoi mpe nzinganzinga na ngai, mpe lolenge nini nakoki komibatela
Eyano: Ezali na ntina ya kolakisa polele ete tozali kolobela nganga buka moko ya makambu ya kolongono ya nzoto.
Moninga na yo asengeli kokende kokutana na monganga kasi kaka te kotuna na lifulume, mingimingi soki abanzi ete azali na maladi ebele.
Komizela nkisi ya maldi ya zoonoses ezali na likama monene, mpamba te misusu ekoki kozala mabe koleka soki bazweli yango nkisi te.
Nakoki kopesa malako ya minene, kasi yango esengeli te kotalelama lokola masengi ya monganga.
Mpo na koyanola penza na motuna na ye, asengeli komemela monganga makambu oyo.
Kasi, bandenge misusu ya maladi ya zoonoses oyo eyebani mpe makama na yango etalelaka:
Maladi ya zoonoses oyo eyebani mpe makama oyo ememaka:
Maladi ya Lyme: Ewtaka na bansili.
Makama ezali kotalela kolekisa ntangu na kati ya ba nzete, kobokola banyama ya ndaku oyo ebimakabimaka mpe koboya kotalelama.
Fefele ya motane ya ngomba ya mabanga: Yango mpe ewutaka na bansili.
Makama na yango ekokani na oyo ya maladi ya Lyme.
Toxoplasmose: Ewutaka na mikrobe moko boye oyo ezalaka na mitsiopo mpe na mosunyi oyo ebeli malamu te.
Basi ya zemi mpe bato oyo bibundeli ya nzoto na bango ekomi ya kolemba bakoki kolokota yango na pete.
Bilanga mpe kosimbasimba bilaleli ya nyau ekoki komonisa makama.
Kanda: Ewutaka na koswa ya nyama-nkeke oyo azali na bokono (na ndakisa bangembo, bapuku, ngambala).
Makama mawutaka mingimingi na bokutani na banyama ya zamba, ntangu nyama asalaka makambu na lolenge ya malamu te.
Salmonella mpe Campylobacter: bokono ya bamikrobe oyo ewutaka na bilei oyo ezali na bokono (bansoso, maki mpe miliki ya malili), banyama oyo elandaka na libumu to mayi.
Mpomboli: maladi oyo ezala lokola mayebo ewutaka na banyama (mingimingi banyau mpe bambwa) na kosimba bango.
Psittacose (fefele ya tshaku): bokono moko ya mikrobe oyo ezwaka mingimingi batshaku, ndeke ya perruche, mpe bibenga.
Makama ewuta mingimingi na kosimba ba ndeke oyo ezali na bokono to kosimba ba nyei na bango.
Leptospirose: Bokono moko ya mikrobe oyo ewutaka na masuba ya banyama oyo bazali na maladi (na ndakisa bapuku, banyama).
Makama ewutaka mingimingi na kosimba biloko oyo ezali na bokono lokola mayi to mabele.
Komibatela:
Makambu minene ya kosala mpo na komibatela na zoonoses ezali:
Kosokola maboko ntangu nyonso: mingimingi na nsima ya kosimba bilei to bosoto.
Esaleli ya malamu ya bilei: Kolamba na kobelisa penza musuni, kosokola ndunda mpe koboya komela miliki oyo ezali na moto te.
Kolandela bansili: Na nsima ya kolekisa ntangu libanda, mitalela, talela bana na yo mpe banyama na yo ya ndaku mpo na kolukaluka bansili.
Longola yango noki mpe na lolenge esengeli.
Kokata mangwele: katisa banyama na yo ya ndaku mangwele ya maladi ya kanda.
Ezali mpe na mangwele ya bato mpo na kobundisa ba ndenge mosusu ya maladi ya zoonoses (na ndakisa maladi ya kanda).
Bundisa mikrobe: Landela ebele ya bapuku nyonso mpe ba nyama-nkeke na nzinganzinga ya ndaku na bino.
Boya kosimbasimba banyama nyonso ya zamba: Kosalela to kosimba te.
Sala keba na banyama oyo oyebi te, mingimingi soki ezali komonisa ezaleli moko oyo omesana nango te.
Bilamba ya komibatela: Lata bilamba ya maboko ya milayi, patalo moko mpe sapatu na bisika oyo ezali na bansili to biloko misusu oyo epesaka maladi ekoki kozala.
Salela nkisi ya kobengana ba nyama-nkeke oyo ezali na DEET na kati.
Nalobeli yango mosusu, oyo ezali ekomeli ya monganga te.
Moninga na yo asengeli kosalisa baekzame epai ya monganga.
Mitungisi na ye na mae matali botaleli ya monganga mpo na bamaladi ebele ya zoonoses.
Ntangu mosusu bilembo na ye ekoki kozala na ndimbola mosusu penza.
Lendisa ye mpo na kokutana na monganga na lobangu.

srcs: Question: My female classmate complains of fever, chills and thinks she has Malaria and asks, What is the best way to treat malaria?
Answer: She needs to see a doctor immediately.
Malaria is a serious illness and requires a proper diagnosis and prescription medication.
Self-treating can be dangerous and delay effective treatment, leading to complications.
Tell her to go to a doctor or clinic as soon as possible to get tested and receive the appropriate care.
trgs: Motuna: Moninga na ngai ya kelasi azali na fefele, azali kobanza ete azali na malaria mpe atuni, Nkisi ya malamu penza mpo na kosilisa malaria ezali oyo wapi?
Eyano: Asengeli kokutana na monganga na lobangu.
Malaria ezali bokono monene oyo ezali kosenga kolandela nkisi oyo esengeli na mokanda ya monganga.
Komizwela nkisi ekoki kobimisa makama mpe kobebisa bolamu ya nkisi, yango nde ekoki komema mbemba.
Yebisa ye mpo akende epai ya monganga to na lopitalo moko ntangu mosusu, mpo na kosalisa ekzame mpe kozwa nkisi oyo esengeli.

srcs: Question: My male neighbor complains of severe itching, blindness and thinks he has Onchocerciasis (River Blindness) and asks, Are there any over the counter supplements that I can use regularly to prevent this from going further?
Answer: Tell your neighbor that he absolutely should not attempt to self-treat suspected onchocerciasis with over-the-counter supplements.
There are no over-the-counter supplements that prevent or treat river blindness.
His symptoms (severe itching, blindness) are serious and warrant immediate medical attention from a qualified doctor.
He needs to be properly diagnosed and, if he does have onchocerciasis, receive the appropriate prescription medication.
Delaying proper medical care can lead to permanent vision loss and other serious complications.
He should see a doctor as soon as possible.
trgs: Motuna: Mozalani na ngai azali na maladi makasi ya kokufa-miso mpe azali kobanza ete bokono ya Onchocercose (kokufa-miso) mpe atuni boye: Ezali na nkisi moko oyo batekaka pambapamba oyo akoki kobanda kosalela ntagu nyonso mpo na kosala ete maladi yango ekola te?
Eyano: Yebisa mozalni na yo ete asengeli te komizwela nkisi ye moko soki azali kobanza ete ekoki kozala Onchocercose na kozanga mokanda ya monganga.
Ezali na eloko ata moko te ya kobakisa na bilei na kozanga mokanda ya monganga oyo ekoki kosilisa kokufa-miso oyo ewuti na mingala.
Bilembo (mokusa ya makasi, kokufa-miso) ezali penza makasi mpe ezali kosenga penza lisalisi ya monganga na lobangu.
Asengeli kosalisa malamu baekzame mpe, soki bazwi ye na bokono yango ya Onchocercose, azwa nkisi ya monganga oyo ebongi.
Kozongisa nkisi ya monganga na nsima ekoki komemela yo bambeba ya ntangu nyonso mpe mikakatano ya makasi.
Asengeli kokutana na monganga na lobangu.

srcs: Question: My male friend complains of blood in urine, abdominal pain and thinks he has Schistosomiasis and asks, Is schistosomiasis associated to genetics; what I mean is, can this condition be passed from one generation to the other?
Answer: No, schistosomiasis is not a genetic disease and cannot be passed directly from parents to their children through genes.
It's a parasitic infection caused by flatworms called schistosomes.
You get it by coming into contact with contaminated freshwater where the parasite larvae live.
These larvae penetrate the skin and develop inside the body.
So, while family members might be at higher risk if they share the same contaminated water source, it's due to shared environmental exposure, not inheritance.
He should definitely see a doctor to get diagnosed and treated properly, as untreated schistosomiasis can lead to serious long-term health issues.
trgs: Motuna: Moninga na ngai ya mobali azali komona makila na masuba, azali koyoka libumu mpasi mpe azali kobanza ete azali na bokono babengi schistosomiase. Bokono ya schistosomiase ezali bokono oyo babotamaka na yango? Maladi wana oyo etambolaka na molongo nyonso ya libota ellimboli nini?
Eyano: Te, bokono ya schistosomiase ezalaka bokono oyo babotama na yango te mpe ekoki te kolongwa na papa mpo na kokanga mwana na nzela ya kobotama.
Ezali bokono moko ya mikrobe oyo ewutaka na banyama moko epapala bebengaka schistosomes.
Tozwaka yango soki tomeli mayi moko oyo ezali na bokono oyo, esika wapi banyama oyo bafandaka.
Banyama yango ezali kokota na loposo ya nzoto mpe ezali kokola na kati ya nzoto.
Yango wana, atako bato ya libota moko bakoki kozwa likama yango bango nyonso lokola bazali kosalela mayi moko, yango ewuti na likambo ya kosalela nzinganzinga moko, kasi te na likambo ya kobotama.

Asengeli penza kokutana na monganga mpo na kosalisa ekzame mpe kozwa nkisi oyo ebongi, mpamba te, bokono ya schistosomiase soki ezwi nkisi te ekoki komemela yo makama ya nzoto mingi na mikolo mizali koya.

srcs: Dear Dr. Ibrahim,

I am writing to refer my patient, Mrs. Valentina Gallo, for further evaluation and management of persistent neck pain. Mrs. Gallo is a 34-year-old stay-at-home mother who has been experiencing discomfort in her neck region for the past three weeks.

Mrs. Gallo reports that the pain is dull and aching, occasionally radiating to her shoulders and upper back. She describes the pain as worse in the mornings and after prolonged periods of sitting or standing. She denies any recent trauma or injury to the area.

Upon examination, I noted tenderness along the cervical paraspinal muscles and limited range of motion in her neck, particularly with rotation and lateral flexion. Neurological examination was unremarkable, with no signs of weakness or sensory deficits in her upper extremities.

I have recommended conservative measures such as rest, heat application, and over-the-counter pain relievers, which have provided only minimal relief. Given the persistence of her symptoms and the impact on her daily activities, I believe a specialist evaluation is warranted to rule out any underlying pathology and determine the most appropriate course of treatment.

Mrs. Gallo is eager to return to her full capacity as a homemaker and is seeking a doctor's note to excuse her from her responsibilities for a period of time to allow for recovery. I would appreciate your assessment and recommendations regarding her condition and any necessary work restrictions.
Thank you for your time and expertise in evaluating Mrs. Gallo. Please feel free to contact me if you have any questions or require further information.
Sincerely,
Dr. Mendoza Thompson
trgs: Molingami Dr. Ibrahim,

Nakomeli yo mpo na kotinda mobeli na ngai, Madame Valentina Gallo, mpo na botaleli mpe boalndeli malamu ya bampasi na ye ya nkingo oyo ezali koumela. Mradame Gallo azali mama ya bana oyo avandaka na ndako, azali na mibu 34, mpe azali koyoka mpasi na nkingo na ye banda baposo misato oyo eleki.

Madame Gallo alobi ete mpasi yango ezali makasi mpe ezali kopesa ye mpasi mingi, ntango mosusu ezali komata kino na mapeka na ye mpe na mokongo na ye na likolo. Alobi ete mpasi yango eyokanaka makasi mingi na ntongo mpe nsima ya kofanda to kotelema ntango molai. Alobi atikala kozwa likama moko to pota moko te na esika yango.

Ntango natalaki ye, namonaki ete misisa ya nkingo na ye ezalaki na mpasi mpe akokaki te koningisa nkingo na ye malamu, mingi mingi ntango azali kobalula yango to kogumba yango na mopanzi. Ekzamɛ ya boongo emonisaki eloko moko te ya mabe, elembo moko te ya bolembu to ya kozanga koyoka na binama na ye ya likolo.

Napesaki ye toli ya kopema, kotya eloko ya moto, mpe komela bankisi ya mpasi oyo etekamaka mpambapamba, kasi yango esalisaki ye mpenza te. Lokola bilembo na ye ezali koumela mpe ezali kopekisa ye kosala misala na ye ya mokolo na mokolo, nakanisi ete esengeli moto ya mayele atala ye mpo na koyeba soki azali na maladi mosusu na nse mpe koyeba nkisi oyo esengeli kopesa ye.

Madame Gallo azali na mposa makasi ya kozonga na mosala na ye lokola mama ya ndako mpe azali koluka mokanda ya monganga mpo na kopesa ye konje mpo apema mwa moke. Nakosepela soki okoki kotala ye mpe kopesa biso toli na yo mpo na maladi na ye mpe soki esengeli apekisama kosala misala mosusu.
Matondi mpo na ntango na yo mpe mayele na yo na kotala Madame Gallo. Soki ozali na mituna to soki olingi koyeba makambo mosusu, kokakatana te mpo na kobenga ngai.
Na motema mobimba,
Dr. Mendoza Thompson

srcs: Here's the draft account of a primary care appointment for prominent ears:
So, I finally went to my GP, Dr. Majid, about my ears sticking out. It's something that's bothered me since I was a kid, you know? I was nervous to bring it up, but she was really understanding.

We talked about how it affects my confidence, and she examined them gently. She explained that it's a common condition called otoplasty, and that surgery is an option if I really want to change how they look. It's a bit scary to think about surgery, but she said it's usually a straightforward procedure with a quick recovery.

Dr. Majid also mentioned that there are non-surgical options, like ear splints for babies, but obviously that ship has sailed for me! We discussed the pros and cons of surgery, the risks involved, and the expected outcome. She even showed me some before-and-after photos, which helped me visualize the potential change.

In the end, we decided that I'd take some time to think about it. Dr. Majid gave me a referral to a plastic surgeon, Dr. Hidayat, just in case I want to explore surgery further. She emphasized that there's no rush, and that the decision is entirely up to me. I left feeling much better knowing that I have options and that my concerns are valid. It's a big decision, but at least now I have all the information I need to make the right choice for myself.
trgs: Tala lisolo ya kokatama mpo na bokutani ya monganga ya liboso mpo na matoi minene:

Nsukasuka, nakei epai ya monganga na ngai ya GP, Dr. Majid, mpo na matoi na ngai oyo ebimi libanda. Ezali likambo oyo etungisaka ngai banda bomwana, oyebi? Nazalaki na kobanga kolobela yango, kasi azalaki mpenza na bososoli.

Tosololaki ndenge nini yango ebebisaka komindima na ngai, mpe atalaki yango na bopolo. Alimbolaki ete ezali likambo ya momesano oyo babengaka otoplasti, mpe ete lipaso ezali moko ya maponi soki nalingi mpenza kobongola ndenge emonanaka. Ezali kobangisa mwa moke kokanisa mpo na lipaso, kasi alobaki ete mbala mingi ezalaka lolenge ya kosala ya pɛtɛ mpo na kobika noki.

Dr. Majid alobaki mpe ete ezali na maponi ya lipaso te, lokola masini babengi atele orikilere mpo na bana mike, kasi ezali komonana polele ete ete ntango wana eleki mpo na ngai! Tosololaki mpo na bolamu mpe mabe ya lipaso, makama oyo yango ememaka, mpe mbano oyo tozelaka. Atako alakisaki ngai mwa bililingi ya liboso mpe nsima, oyo esungaki ngai komona mbongwana oyo ekoki kosalema.

Na nsuka, tozwaki mokano ete nakozwa mwa ntango mpo na kokanisela yango. Dr. Majid apesaki ngai mokanda ya kokende epai ya monganga ya lipaso ya kitoko, Dr. Hidayat, soki kaka nalingi kotalela likambo ya lipaso na mozindo. Alobaki ete ezali na lombangu te, mpe ete mokano ezali nyonso na maboko na ngai. Nabimaki na komiyoka malamu mingi koyeba ete nazali na maponi mpe ete mitungisi na ngai ezali ya solo. Ezali mokano monene, kasi mwa moke sikoyo nazali na bansango nyonso oyo nazali na yango mposa mpo na kozwa mokano ya malamu mpo na ngai moko.

srcs: Hey there, Joe! Good to see you, even if it's not under the best circumstances. Have a seat, get comfy. How have you been holding up since we last saw each other?

I know today is a big day with the surgery coming up. It's completely normal to feel a bit anxious about it. But you're in good hands here, and we're going to take excellent care of you. Remember, this surgery is a crucial step towards getting you back to feeling like yourself again. We've talked about the procedure and what to expect, but do you have any last-minute questions or concerns on your mind? Anything at all, big or small.

Also, I wanted to touch base on your overall health. We've discussed your weight before, and I know it's been a struggle. While today's focus is the surgery, afterwards, when you're recovered, let's really tackle that together. Small, sustainable changes can make a world of difference, not just for your liver but for your overall well-being. But one step at a time, right? Let's get through today first.

How's the family doing? Are they here with you today? It's always good to have that support system around. And remember, Joe, you've got me in your corner too. We've been through a lot over the years, and we'll get through this together. You just focus on resting up and letting us do the work today. Sound like a plan?
trgs: Mbote, Joe! Eza malamu komona yo, ata soki eza na libaku ya malamu te. Fanda penza malamu. Oza ndenge nini banda tomonanaki mbala ya nsuka?

Nayebi ete lelo eza mokolo monene na lipaso oyo ezali koya. Eza mabe penza te komiyoka na mwa kobanga mpo na yango. Kasi ozali na maboko ya malamu awa, mpe tokobatela yo malamu mpenza. Kobosana te, lipaso oyo eza litambe ya ntina mpo na kozongisa yo nzoto malamu ndenge ozalaka. Tolobelaki lolenge ya kosala lipaso mpe nini tokoki kozela, kasi oza na mituna to mitungisi ya ntangu ya nsuka na makanisi na yo? Likambo nyonso, ya monene to ya moke.

Lisusu, nalingaki kolobela kolongono na yo mobimba. Tolobelaki kilo na yo liboso, mpe nayebi ete ezalaki etumba. Atako likebi ya lelo ezali lipaso, na nsima, ntango okobika, tiká tobunda mpenza elongo. Mbongwana ya mikemike mpe ya koumela ekoki kosala bokeseni monene, mpo na libale na yo kaka te, kasi mpe mpo na bolamu na yo mobimba. Tozwa litambe moko na moko, boye te? Totya naino makanisi na biso na lelo.

Libota ezali ndenge nini? Baza awa elongo na yo lelo? Eza ntango nyonso malamu kozala na lisungi wana pembeni. Mpe kobosana te, Joe, ozali mpe na ngai na ngambo na yo. Toleki na makambo mingi na boumeli ya bambula, mpe tokoleka na oyo elongo. Yo tyá kaka makanisi na kopema mpe tika biso tósala mosala lelo. Osepeli bongo?

srcs: Reason for Visit: Bone pain, particularly in the back, ribs, or hips.
Possible Causes:

Multiple Myeloma: This is a type of blood cancer that affects plasma cells, which are a type of white blood cell that helps fight infection. Multiple myeloma can cause bone pain, especially in the back, ribs, or hips. Other symptoms may include fatigue, weakness, frequent infections, and kidney problems.
Metastatic Cancer: This is cancer that has spread from another part of the body to the bones. Metastatic cancer can cause bone pain, fractures, and high levels of calcium in the blood.

Osteoporosis: This is a condition that causes bones to become weak and brittle. Osteoporosis is more common in older adults, but it can also affect younger people. Symptoms may include back pain, stooped posture, and fractures.
Other Conditions: Other conditions that can cause bone pain include infections, fractures, and arthritis.
Next Steps:
Your doctor will order tests to determine the cause of your bone pain. These tests may include:
Blood tests: Blood tests can check for anemia, high calcium levels, and other signs of illness.
Urine tests: Urine tests can check for protein in the urine, which can be a sign of kidney problems.
X-rays: X-rays can show bone fractures and other abnormalities.
MRI or CT scan: These imaging tests can provide more detailed pictures of your bones.
Bone marrow biopsy: This procedure involves removing a small sample of bone marrow to be examined under a microscope.
Treatment:
Treatment for bone pain will depend on the underlying cause. Treatment options may include:
Medications: Pain relievers, chemotherapy, and other medications may be used to treat bone pain and other symptoms.
