Radiation therapy: Radiation therapy uses high-energy beams to kill cancer cells and relieve pain.
Surgery: Surgery may be used to repair fractures or stabilize bones.
It is important to follow your doctor's instructions carefully and attend all follow-up appointments. If you have any questions or concerns, please do not hesitate to ask.
Please note: This handout is for informational purposes only and does not constitute medical advice. Please consult with a qualified healthcare professional for diagnosis and treatment.
trgs: Ntina ya bokutani: mpasi na mikuwa, mingi mingi na mokongo, mipanzi, to loketo.
Makambo oyo ekoki kopesa yango:

Myelome multiple: Oyo ezali lolenge ya kanser ya makila oyo ekendaka na baselile ya plasma, oyo ezali lolenge ya baselile ya pembe ya makila oyo esalisaka mpo na kobundisa bokono. Myelome multiple ekoki kopesa mpasi na mikuwa, mingi mingi na mokongo, mipanzi, to loketo. Bilembo misusu ekoki kozala bolembu, kozanga makasi, kozwama na babokono mbala na mbala, mpe mikakatano ya bangei.
Kanser métastatique: Oyo ezali kanser oyo eutaki esika mosusu ya nzoto mpe ekendeke na mikuwa. Kanser métastatique ekoki kopesa mpasi na mikuwa, kobukana, mpe kozala na kalsium mingi na makila.

Ostéoporose: Oyo ezali maladi oyo esalaka ete mikuwa ezala na makasi te mpe ebukana noki. Ostéoporose emonanaka mingi epai ya mikolo, kasi ekoki mpe kozwa bilenge. Bilembo ekoki kozala mpasi ya mokongo, kotambola ya kogumbama, mpe kobukana.
Bokono misusu: Makambo misusu oyo ekoki kopesa mpasi na mikuwa ezali babokono, kobukana, mpe maladi ya mingai.
Makambo oyo ekolanda:
Monganga na yo akosenga ba ekzamɛ mpo na koyeba ntina ya mpasi na yo na mikuwa. Ba ekzamɛ yango ekoki kozala:
Ekzamɛ ya makila: Ekzamɛ ya makila ekoki koluka kosila makila, nivo ya kalsium ya likolo, mpe bilembo misusu ya maladi.
Ekzamɛ ya masuba: Ekzamɛ ya masuba ekoki koluka protéini na masuba, oyo ekoki kozala elembo ya mikakatano ya bangei.
Ekzame ya Radio: Ekzame ya Radio ekoki komonisa mikuwa oyo ebukani mpe mikakatano misusu.
IRM to skaner CT: Ba ekzamɛ ya bililingi oyo ekoki komonisa bafoto ya polele ya mikuwa na yo.
Bolongoli ya ndambo ya libubu ya mikuwa: Mayele oyo esengaka kolongola mwa ndambo ya mikuwa mpo na kotala yango na mikroskope.
Lisungi:
Lisungi ya mpasi na mikuwa ekotalela euteli ya likambo yango. Mayele ya lisungi ekoki kozala:
Nkisi: Nkisi ya kosilisa mpasi, chimiothérapie, mpe nkisi misusu ekoki kosalelama mpo na kosunga mpasi na mikuwa mpe bilembo misusu.
Radiothérapie: Radiothérapie esalelaka ba rayons ya nguya mingi mpo na koboma baselile ya kanser mpe kosilisa mpasi.
Lipaso: Lipaso ekoki kosalelama mpo na kobongisa mikuwa oyo ebukani to kopesa mikuwa makasi.
Ezali ntina kolanda malako ya monganga na yo na likebi mpe kokende na bokutani nyonso ya bolandeli. Soki ozali na mituna to mitungisi, kokakatana te na kotuna yango.
Tika ete: Mokanda oyo ezali kaka mpo na kopesa nsango mpe ezali toli ya monganga te. Kende kosolola na monganga oyo azali na mayele mpo na koyeba maladi mpe lisungi.

srcs: I am so sorry for my lateness, doctor. My wife, Martha, usually drives me to my appointments, but she's laid up with a bad cold, so I had to figure out the bus schedule on my own. It's been a while since I've had to navigate public transportation, and I got a bit turned around.

Anyway, I'm calling because I've noticed a bulge near my old surgery scar. It's been bothering me for a few weeks now, especially when I lift anything heavy or even just cough too hard. It's not exactly painful, more like a dull ache, but it's definitely noticeable. I'm worried it might be an incisional hernia. I had surgery for gallstones about two years ago, and the scar healed up fine initially, but now this lump has appeared.

I've been trying to lose some weight recently, thinking that might help, but it's been slow going. I know being overweight puts extra pressure on the abdominal wall, which probably isn't helping matters. Plus, I've been feeling a bit confused lately, forgetting things more often than usual. Martha says I'm just getting old, but it feels like more than that sometimes. I'm not sure if the confusion is related to the hernia or if it's something else entirely, but I thought I should mention it just in case.

I haven't seen my primary care doctor about this yet because getting an appointment takes forever, and I figured a telehealth consultation might be quicker. I'm hoping you can give me some advice on what to do next. Should I be worried about this lump? Is surgery the only option, or are there other treatments? And do you think my confusion could be connected to all of this? I appreciate any guidance you can offer, doctor.
trgs: Nazali kosenga bolimbisi mpo na retare na ngai, monganga. Mwasi na ngai, Martha, amemaka ngai mbala mingi na bokutani na ngai, kasi azali kobela maladi ya miyoyo makasi, yango wana esengelaki nabunda ngai moko mpo na koyeba bangonga ya bisi. Nasali mikolo ebele oyo nabandaki kosalela babisi te, mpe natungisamaki mwa moke.

Na bokuse, nazali kobenga mpo namoni mwa kovimba moko pembeni ya esika basalaki ngai lipaso kala. Ezali kotungisa ngai sikoyo banda mwa baposo, mingimingi ntango nazali komema eloko ya kilo to ata kaka ntango nazali kokosola makasi. Mpasi ezali koyokana penza te, ezali kaka mpasi ya moke, kasi ezali mpenza komonana. Nazali komitungisa mbala mosusu ezala litutu ya pota. Basalaki ngai lipaso mpo na maladi ya nsongi esali soki bambula mibale, mpe elembo ya pota ya lipaso ebikaki malamu na ebandeli, kasi sikoyo kovimba oyo eye kobima.

Namekaki kokitisa kilo na mikolo oyo mileki, kokanisa ete ekoki kosalisa, kasi ezali kokende malembe. Nayebi ete monene mingi epesaka pressio mingi na efelo ya libumu, oyo ekoki kosalisa te. Lisusu, nazali komiyoka mwa mobulu mikolo oyo, kobosana makambo mingi koleka na momeseno. Martha alobi ete nazali kokoma mobange, kasi nazali kobanza ete ezali kaka yango te. Nayebi te soki mobulu ezali na boyokani na litutu to soki ezali eloko mosusu, kasi nakanisaki ete nasengeli kolobela yango kaka mpo toyebi te.

Namoni naino monganga na ngai ya liboso te mpo na likambo oyo mpamba te, kozwa bokutani na ye ezwaka ntango mingi, mpe namilobeli ete botaleli na monganga ya mosika ekoki kozala mbangu. Nazali kolikya ete okoki kopesa ngai mwa toli na oyo nasengeli kosala. Nasengeli komitungisa mpo na kovimba oyo? Lipaso ezali kaka nzela moko oyo esengeli, to ezali na banzela misusu ya kozwela lobiko? Mpe okanisi ete mobulungano na ngai ekoki kozala na boyokani na biloko wana nyonso? Nazali kosepela na toli nyonso oyo okoki kopesa nagi, monganga.

srcs: I've got a new patient here, his name is Didymus. He's a 42-year-old male who was recently referred to us for rehabilitation following a knee replacement surgery. He mentioned experiencing significant fatigue and shortness of breath during his physical therapy sessions. His recent lab work reveals low hemoglobin and hematocrit levels, indicating anemia. He also mentioned feeling dizzy and having frequent headaches. I suspect his anemia is causing these symptoms, hindering his rehabilitation progress. Could you please review his lab results and assess him for any underlying causes of anemia? We may need to address this before he can fully participate in his rehabilitation program.
trgs: Nazali na mobeli ya sika awa, kombo na ye Didymus. Azali mobali ya mibu 42 oyo atindami sika awa mpo na bonzongisami na kosala bamuvema na nsima ya lipaso ya libolongo. Alobi azali koyoka kolemba makasi mpe kokatana mpema ntango ya seansi na ye ya konyolola nzoto. Bambano na ye ya labo ya sika emonisi ete hemoglobine mpe hematocrite na ye ezali na nse, elakisi akosila makila. Alobi mpe azali koyoka kizunguzungu mpe motó ezali kobeta mbala na mbala. Nazali kokanisa kosila na ye ya makila nde ezali kopesa ye bilembo oyo, mpe ezali kopekisa ye akende liboso na bozongisami na ye na likoki ya kosala bamuvema. Okoki naino kotalela mbano ya labo mpe koluka biutelo misusu ya kosila na ye ya makila?  Ezali na ntina kosilisa likambo yango yambo ete akoka komipesa mobimba na programe na ye ya bozongisami na kosala bamuvema.

srcs: I remember back in 2019, I was really worried about this lump I found in my breast. My primary care doctor sent me for a mammogram, and they saw something suspicious, so they recommended a core needle biopsy. I wasn't too thrilled about the idea, so I decided to get a second opinion.

I made an appointment with a specialist, Dr. Gupta. She was really nice and took the time to listen to my concerns. She explained the biopsy procedure in detail and answered all my questions. She even showed me some diagrams to help me understand what was going on.

After the consultation, I felt much better about going ahead with the biopsy. Dr. Gupta made me feel comfortable and confident in her expertise. The biopsy itself wasn't too bad, just a little pinch. And thankfully, the results came back benign!

Getting a second opinion was definitely the right decision for me. It gave me peace of mind and helped me make an informed decision about my healthcare. I would recommend it to anyone facing a similar situation.
trgs: Nabanzi lisusu na 2019, namitungisaki mpenza mpo na mwa mbuma moko namonaki na libele na ngai. Monganga na ngai atindaki ngai nasala ekzame ya kosimbasimba libele, mpe bamonaki eloko moko ya kokamwa, yango wana bapesaka ngai toli ete nasala biolongoli misuni na ntonga. Nasepelaki mpenza te na likanisi yango, yango wana nazwaki ekateli ya kozwa botaleli ya mibale.

Nazwaki mokolo ya bokutani na monganga moko ya mayele, Dr. Gupta. Azalaki mpenza malamu mpe azwaki ntango ya koyoka mitungisi na ngai. Alimbolelaki ngai malamu lolenge oyo basalaka bolongoli ya misuni mpe ayanolaki na mituna na ngai nyonso. Atalisaki ngai mpe mwa bandakisa mpo na kosunga ngai nasosola nini ezalaki koleka.

Na nsima ya kosolola na ye, namiyokaki malamu mpenza mpo na kokoba na ekzame ya bolongoli misuni. Dr. Gupta asalisaki ngai mpo namiyoka malamu mpe nazala na elikya na mayele na ye. Bolongoli misuni yango moko ezalaki mpasi mingi te, kaka mwa kotutula moke. Mpe eloko ya malamu, bambano ebimaki malamu!

Kozwa likanisi ya mibale ezalaki mpenza ekateli ya malamu mpo na ngai. Epesaki ngai kimya ya makanisi mpe esalisaki ngai nazwa ekateli ya malamu mpo na kolongono ya nzoto na ngai. Nakoki kopesa toli yango na moto nyonso oyo azali na likambo ya ndenge wana.

srcs: I'm calling because I'm having a horrible headache, like the worst one of my life, and I'm worried it might be an aneurysm. My name is Brenda, and I'm 54. I'm a bit overweight, about 250 pounds, and I've been feeling a bit dizzy too. My neck feels stiff, and I'm getting a bit nauseous. I don't have a history of aneurysms in my family, but I do have high blood pressure. Should I go to the emergency room?
trgs: Nazali kobenga mpo motó ezali koswa ngai na ndenge ya somo, lokola moto oyo eswaka ngai te banda nabotama, mpe nazali komitungisa ete ekoki kozala aneurysm. Kombo na ngai Brenda, mpe nazali na mibu 54. Nazali na kilo mwa mingi, pene na 250 kilo, mpe nazali koyoka lokola miso ezali kozunguluka. Nkingo na ngai ezali makasi, mpe nazali koyoka mwa katu. Nazali na moto na libota te oyo aza na maladi ya aneurysm, kasi nazali na tansyo. Nasengeli kokende na lobiko ya lobangu?

srcs: Hi, Harold! It's always good to see you. I understand you're interested in exploring some options for your spasticity. You mentioned reading about Dr. Amelia Grant online and her work with spasticity management.

I'm happy to refer you to Dr. Grant. I've actually heard good things about her from other patients as well. She's a neurologist who specializes in movement disorders, and she has a lot of experience with spasticity.

Before we send off the referral, let's chat a bit about what to expect. Spasticity can be tricky to manage, and finding the right approach often involves some trial and error. Dr. Grant will likely start by doing a thorough evaluation to understand your specific symptoms and how they're affecting your daily life. She might also order some tests, like an MRI or EMG, to get a better picture of what's going on.

Based on her assessment, she'll develop a treatment plan tailored to you. This could include things like physical therapy, medications, or even injections. She'll also work with you to set realistic goals and track your progress.

Remember, managing spasticity is a journey, not a sprint. It might take some time to find the right combination of treatments that work for you. But with Dr. Grant's expertise and your commitment, I'm confident you'll find some relief.
I'll get that referral sent over right away. In the meantime, if you have any questions or concerns, please don't hesitate to call me. You know where to find me!
trgs: Mbote, Harold! Ezalaka ntango nyonso esengo komona yo. Nayoki ete ozali na mposa ya koluka makambo oyo okoki kosala mpo na makolo na yo oyo ezali kokatana. Olobaki ete otangaki makomi na internet na oyo etali Dr. Amelia Grant mpe mosala na ye ya kosunga baoyo bazali na makolo oyo ezali kokatana.

Nazali kotinda yo penza epai ya Dr. Grant. Nayoki mpe makambo ya malamu mpo na ye epai ya babeli misusu. Azali monganga ya misisa ya boongo oyo ayebi mingi makambo ya koningana ya nzoto, mpe azali na eksperiansi mingi na makambo ya makolo oyo ezali kokatana.

Liboso ya kotinda bosenga na yo ya bokutani, tosolola mwa moke mpo na koyeba nini okokutana na yango kuna. Makolo oyo ezali kokatana ekoki kozala mpasi mpo na kosungama, mpe mpo na kozwa lisungi ya malamu esengaka komekameka makambo mingi. Dr. Grant akobanda na kotala yo malamu mpo na koyeba bilembo na yo mpe bopusi na yango na bomoi na yo ya mokolo na mokolo. Akoki mpe kosenga yo osalisa ba ekzame misusu, lokola MRI to EMG, mpo na kolimbola malamumalamu likambu.
Na kotalela oyo akomona, akopesa yo lobiko oyo ebongi na yo. Ekoki kozala masaje, bankisi ya komela, to mpe tonga. Akosalisa yo mpe mpo bozwa mikano oyo bokoki kokokisa mpe kolandela bokoli na yo.

Kobosana te ete, kosunga makolo oyo ezali kokatana ezali lokola kobanda mobembo, ezali te kokima mbangu. Ekoki kozwa ntango mpo na kozwa lobiko oyo ekosunga yo. Kasi na mayele ya Dr. Grant mpe milende na yo, nandimisami ete oko bika.
Nakotinda mokanda wana kaka sikoyo. Na ntango wana, soki ozali na mituna to mitungisi, kokakatana te na kobenga ngai. Oyebi esika nini okoki kokuta ngai!

srcs: To Whom It May Concern,

I'm here for my DOT physical because my grandfather and two uncles had aplastic anemia, and I know that puts me at higher risk. But honestly, that's just the tip of the iceberg when it comes to my health. It feels like I've got a laundry list of issues going on.

Fatigue is a big one. I'm constantly tired, even after a full night's sleep. It's a deep kind of exhaustion that makes it hard to get through the day, especially with the physical demands of my job. I also get short of breath pretty easily, even with just moderate exertion. Sometimes I get dizzy spells too, which can be a little scary when I'm driving or operating machinery.

I bruise really easily. I'll bump into something lightly and end up with a huge purple mark that takes forever to go away. And I get nosebleeds more often than I'd like to admit. Sometimes my gums bleed when I brush my teeth, too.

I've been dealing with these persistent infections lately. Seems like I catch every cold or flu that goes around, and they linger for weeks. I've had a few bouts of pneumonia in the last couple of years, which really knocked me down.

On top of that, I have type 2 diabetes, high blood pressure, and high cholesterol. I take medication for all of those, but it's a lot to manage. And I have this chronic back pain from an old injury that flares up whenever I do too much heavy lifting.

So yeah, it's a lot. I'm hoping this physical goes well, but I'm definitely worried about all these symptoms and how they might affect my ability to keep working. I just want to make sure I'm doing everything I can to stay healthy and keep providing for my family.
Sincerely,
Michael Harris
trgs: Likambo oyo etali nani,

Nazali awa mpo na ekzame na ngai ya DOT mpo nkoko na ngai ya mobali mpe ba noko na ngai mibale bazalaki na anemi aplastique, mpe nayebi ete yango etye ngai na likama ya makasi. Kasi ya solo, oyo ezali kaka ebandeli ya makambo matali kolongono na ngai ya nzoto. Emonani lokola nazali na liste ya molayi ya mikakatano ya nzoto.

Kolemba ezali likambo monene. Nazalaka na bolembu ntango nyonso, ata soki nalali butu mobimba. Ezali bolembu moko ya makasi oyo esalaka ete ezala mpasi kolekisa mokolo, mingi mingi na kotalela mosala na ngai ya makasi. Nakatanaka mpema noki, ata soki nasali kaka mwa mosala moke. Ntango mosusu nazalaka mpe na kizunguzungu, oyo ekoki kozala na likama penza ntango nazali kokumba motuka to kosalela bamasini.

Nazokaka noki mpenza. Nakoki kotutana na eloko moko mpe nakozoka pota monene ya violé oyo eumelaka mpo na kolongwa. Mpe zolo na ngai etangaka makila mbala mingi koleka ndenge nalingaka kondimela. Ntango mosusu nonga na ngai ebimaka mpe makila ntango nasukolaka mino na ngai ya bibubutu.

Nazalaki komona mpasi na maladi oyo eumelaka mikolo oyo. Emonani lokola nazwaka maladi ya miyoyo mpe bagripe nyonso oyo elekaka, mpe eumelaka baposo mingi. Nazalaki na maladi ya mpema mbala moke na mibu mibale mileki, oyo elembisaki ngai mpenza.

Likolo ya yango, nazali na diabeti ya tnivo 2, tensyo ya komata, mpe kolesterole ya likolo. Namelaka nkisi mpo na yango nyonso, kasi ezali mpasi mpo na kokoba. Mpe nazali na mpasi oyo esilaka te na mokongo kouta na pota moko ya kala oyo eyaka lisusu ntango nyonso oyo namemaka biloko ya bozito mingi.

Ya solo, ezali mingi. Nazali kolikya ete ekzame oyo ekoleka malamu, kasi nazali mpenza komitungisa mpo na bilembo oyo nyonso mpe bopusi na yango na likoki na ngai ya kokoba kosala mosala. Nalingi kaka komindimisa ete nazali kosala nyonso oyo nakoki mpo na kozala na kolongono ya nzoto mpe kokoba kokokisa bamposa ya libota na ngai.
Na motema mobimba,
Michael Harris

srcs: A 55-year-old male overnight warehouse stocker, Michael, presented to the emergency department with concerns regarding prostate cancer screening. Michael reported feeling generally unwell for the past few weeks, experiencing fatigue and mild lower back pain. He expressed worry about his risk of prostate cancer due to his age and a family history of the disease. He specifically inquired about the Prostate-Specific Antigen (PSA) test. The attending physician conducted a physical examination and discussed the benefits and limitations of PSA screening with Michael. The physician explained that while PSA levels can indicate prostate issues, they can also be elevated due to benign conditions. Given Michael's symptoms and concerns, the physician ordered a PSA test along with other routine blood work to assess his overall health. Michael was advised to follow up with his primary care physician to discuss the results and determine if further evaluation, such as a biopsy, was necessary. The physician also provided Michael with educational materials on prostate health and cancer screening guidelines. Michael was discharged with instructions to monitor his symptoms and seek medical attention if they worsened. He expressed relief at having addressed his concerns and planned to schedule a follow-up appointment with his primary care doctor. The physician documented the visit and the discussion regarding PSA screening in Michael's medical record. Michael left the emergency department feeling reassured and informed about his next steps.
trgs: Mobali moko ya mbula 55 oyo asalaka mosala ya kobomba biloko na butu, Michael, ayaki na departema ya lobiko ya lombangu mpo na mitungisi na ye etali komekama ya kanser ya prostate. Michael alobaki ete azali koyoka nzoto malamu te mposo oyo eleki, azali koyoka bolembu mpe mpasi na mokongo na nse. Amonisi mitungisi na ye mpo na likama ya kozwa kanser ya prostate mpo na mbula na ye mpe lisolo ya libota na ye na maladi yango. Atunaki mpenza mpo na komekama ya Prostate-Specific Antigen (PSA). Monganga oyo azalaki wana asalaki ekzame ya nzoto mpe asololaki na Michael matomba mpe bandelo ya komekama ya PSA. Monganga alimbisaki ete atako nivo ya PSA ekoki komonisa mikakatano ya prostate, ekoki mpe komata mpo na maladi oyo ezali na likama te. Na kotalela bilembo mpe mitungisi ya Michael, monganga apesaki mitindo ya kosala komekama ya PSA elongo na komekama mosusu ya makila mpo na kotalela sante na ye mobimba. Michael asengamaki akende komona monganga na ye ya liboso mpo na kosolola na ye mpo na biyano mpe koyeba soki esengeli kosala evaluasion mosusu, lokola kosala biopsie. Monganga apesaki mpe Michael mikanda ya kotangisa mpo na sante ya prostate mpe mitindo ya komekama ya kanser. Michael abimaki na lopitalo na mitindo ya kokeba na bilembo na ye mpe koluka lisungi ya monganga soki yango ekomi mabe. Amonisi soulagement na ndenge asilisi mitungisi na ye mpe abongisi kosala rendez-vous na monganga na ye ya liboso. Monganga akomaki vizite mpe lisolo etali komekama ya PSA na dosyé ya Michael. Michael atikaki departema ya lobiko na lobangu na liyoki ya kozala na kimya mpe koyeba malamu bitambe na ye oyo ekolanda.

srcs: My heart is racing again, like it's trying to jump out of my chest. I feel hot and sweaty all the time, even when it's freezing outside. My hands won't stop shaking, and I'm losing weight no matter how much I eat. My eyes feel bulging and irritated, and I'm constantly on edge. I can't sleep, and my periods have been all over the place. I feel like I'm going crazy, and my poor kid is acting out because I'm such a mess. I need help, this isn't just wrinkles.
trgs: Motema na nga ezobeta lisusu makasi, neti ezo elingi kobima libanda ya tolo na ngai. Nazali koyoka nzoto moto mpe nazali kotoka ntango nyonso, ata soki malili ezali libanda. Maboko na ngai ezali kolenga ntangu nyonso, mpe nazo konda ata soki nazolia ndenge nini. Miso na nga ezo vimba mpe ezali koswa, mpe nazali ntango nyonso na nkanda. Nazo lala te, mpe komona sanza na ngai eza kobongwanabongwana. Nazomona neti nazo bela  liboma, mpe mwana na ngai azali kosala buzoba mpo nazali komiyoka bongo. Naza na mposa ya lisungi, oyo eza kaka konuna te.

srcs: Patient presents to the urgent care clinic with dystonia. The patient's child, Leo, is present and quite active during the examination.
History:

Patient reports involuntary muscle contractions, causing repetitive or twisting movements. These symptoms started recently and have been causing significant discomfort. The patient denies any recent trauma or changes in medication. No family history of dystonia or other neurological disorders.
Physical Exam:

Patient appears uncomfortable due to muscle spasms. Vital signs are stable. Neurological exam reveals sustained muscle contractions in the neck and shoulders, consistent with cervical dystonia. No other neurological deficits noted. Leo is energetic and curious, exploring the exam room throughout the visit.
Assessment:
Likely cervical dystonia. Will need to rule out other causes and consider referral to a neurologist for further evaluation and management.
Plan:
1. Prescribed muscle relaxant to help alleviate symptoms.
2. Referral to Dr. Fischer Chen, a neurologist specializing in movement disorders, for further evaluation.
3. Advised patient to rest and avoid strenuous activities that may exacerbate symptoms.
4. Follow up in one week or sooner if symptoms worsen.
Reassurance:

Provided reassurance to the patient regarding the diagnosis and treatment plan. Addressed concerns about Leo's behavior, emphasizing that children are naturally curious and active. Encouraged the patient to reach out with any further questions or concerns. Leo was given a sticker for being a good helper during the visit.
trgs: Mobeli aye na ndako ya lisalisi na lombango mpo na dystonie. Mwana na ye, Leo, azali wana mpe azali na makasi mingi ntango ya ekzame.
Lisolo:

Mobeli alobi ete azali koyoka kokangamakangama ya misisa, oyo ezali kosalisa ye bamuvema ya kozongelazongela to ya kobaluka. Bilembo oyo ebandi kala te mpe ezali kopesa ye mpasi mingi. Mobeli awangani ata likama moko mikolo oyo to mbongwana moko ya bankisi. Na libota na ye, lisolo ya bokono ya distoni to bamaladi misusu oyo etali boongo etikala komonana te.
Ekzame ya nzoto:

Mobeli amonani ete azali kobela kokangamakangama ya misisa. Bilembo ya bomoi na ye ezali makasi. Ekzame ya misisa emonisi kokangamakangama ya misisa na nkingo mpe na mapeka, oyo eyokani na distoni ya kingo. Ata mbeba mosusu ya misisa emonani te. Leo azali na makasi mpe na mposa ya koyeba, azali kotambolatambola na ndako ya ekzame na boumeli nyonso ya botaleli.
Botaleli:
Ekoki kozala penza distoni ya kingo. Ekosenga kolongola bantina misusu mpe kokanisa kosalisa ekzame epai ya monganga ya misisa mpo na botaleli mpe boyangeli ya mozindo.
Mwango:
1. Ekomelami nkisi ya kolembisa misisa mpo na kosalisa bilembo.
2. Kotindama epai ya Dr. Fischer Chen, monganga ya misisa oyo ayebi malamu makambu ya mikakatano ya bamuvema mpo na botaleli na mozindo.
3. Mobeli azwaki toli ya kopema mpe koboya misala ya makasi oyo ekoki kobakisa bilembo.
4. Kolandela na poso moko to liboso soki bilembo bibebi.
Kopesa elikya:

Napesi elikya na mobeli na oyo etali bambano ya ekzame mpe mwango ya lobiko. Nalobeli mitungisi mpo na bizaleli ya Leo, na komonisa ete bana bazalaka na mposa ya koyeba mpe bazalaka na makasi. Na lendisaki mobeli mpo na kobenga ngai soki azali na mituna to mitungisi mosusu. Leo azwaki sticker moko mpo azalaki mosungi malamu na ntango ya bokutani.

srcs: My doctor said I have bronchitis, which makes it hard for me to breathe sometimes. I've been coughing a lot, and my chest feels tight. My asthma, heart condition, and diabetes all make it harder for my body to fight off this infection, and I'm feeling pretty tired and weak. I also have some swelling in my ankles, which the doctor said might be related to my heart. I'm hoping the medication will help me feel better soon.
trgs: Monganga na ngai alobaki ete nazali na bronchite, oyo esalaka ete nazala na mpasi ya kopema bantango mosusu. Nazali kosukola mingi, mpe ntolo na ngai ezali konyokwama. Maladi na ngai ya asma, maladi ya motema, mpe diabete nyonso esalaka ete nzoto na ngai ezala na mpasi mpo na kobunda na bokono oyo, mpe nazali koyoka mpema mpe bolɛmbu mingi. Nazali mpe na kovimbana mabe oyo monganga alobaki ete ekoki kozala na boyokani na maladi motema na ngai. Nazali kolikya ete nkisi ekosalisa ngai namiyoka malamu noki.

srcs: Avoid dairy products, caffeine, alcohol, and fatty or spicy foods, as these can trigger or worsen symptoms of irritable bowel syndrome (IBS). Aim for smaller, more frequent meals rather than large ones to help regulate digestion. Increase your fiber intake gradually by eating more fruits, vegetables, and whole grains, but be cautious with high-fiber foods if they worsen bloating or gas. Drink plenty of water throughout the day to stay hydrated and support bowel regularity. Keep a food diary to track what you eat and note any foods that seem to cause symptoms, which will help you identify personal triggers.

Consider stress-reduction techniques such as deep breathing, meditation, or gentle exercise, as stress can impact IBS symptoms. Use over-the-counter medications like antispasmodics or laxatives only as directed by your healthcare provider. If symptoms persist or worsen, or if you experience severe abdominal pain, rectal bleeding, or unintentional weight loss, seek medical attention promptly. Follow up with your primary care physician for ongoing management and to adjust your treatment plan as needed. Make sure to discuss any other medications or supplements you are taking to avoid potential interactions. Regularly review and update your diet and lifestyle choices based on how your body responds.
trgs: Keba na biloko ya mabele, kaféine, masanga, mpe bilei ya mafuta to pilipili, mpo ekoki kobimisa to kobakisa bilembo ya Bokono ya Mikakatano na Misopo (IBS). Meká kolya bilei mike-mike mbala mingi na esika ya kolya bilei minene mpo na kosalisa konikama ya bilei. Bakisa mokemoke fibre na kolya mingi bambuma, bandunda, mpe mbuma ya mobimba, kasi keba na bilei ya fibre mingi soki ebimisaka mopepe to evimbisaka libumu. Mela mayi mingi mokolo mobimba mpo na kozala na mayi mpe kosalisa na bozalani ya libumu. Batela mokanda ya bilei mpo na koyeba oyo ozali kolya mpe koyeba bilei nini ezali kobimisa bilembo, mpo esalisa yo koyeba nini ezali kopesa yo maladi.

Kanisa na ba tekiniki ya kokitisa komitungisi na makanisi lokola kopema na mozindo, komanyola, to ngalasisi ya pɛtɛ, mpo mitungisi ya makanisi ekoki kotambola na bilembo ya IBS. Salela bankisi oyo bakoki kozwa kozanga mokanda ya monganga lokola antispasmodiques to oyo elembisaka libumu kaka ndenge monganga na yo alakisaki. Soki bilembo ezali koumela to kobakisama, to soki ozali koyoka mpasi makasi na libumu, makila na mbudu, to kilo ekiti kozanga kobongisa, luka lisalisi ya monganga noki. Landela na monganga na yo ya liboso mpo na boyangeli ya ntango nyonso mpe kobongisa mwango na yo ya lobiko soki esengeli. Solola na monganga mpo na bankisi to supplements mosusu oyo ozali komela mpo na kokima makambo ya mabe. Talaka mpe bongisaka mbala na mbala bilei mpe bomoi na yo na kotalela ndenge nzoto na yo ezali koyamba.

srcs: It's embarrassing, really. I just stumbled and scraped my leg a few days ago, nothing serious. But this thing, it just won't heal. It's red and angry, oozing a bit, and it hurts more than it should. I tried bandaging it up, putting some ointment on it, but it just seems to be getting worse. I didn't want to bother anyone, figured it would clear up on its own, but my daughter insisted I come in. She worries too much, bless her heart. I just feel silly, taking up the doctor's time with something so small. But honestly, it's starting to worry me a little too. It feels... different than a regular scrape. Deeper maybe? And there's this smell... I don't want to be a bother, but I just want to make sure everything's alright.
trgs: Ezoyokisa mwa nsoni, ya solo. Na betaki libaku kaka ndenge wana mpe na zokaki na lokolo mwa mikolo eleki, ezalaki kak eloko ya moke. Kasi eloko oyo, eboyi kobika. Eza motane mpe evimbi, ezobimisa mwa mayi mpe ezoswa koleka ndenge esengeli. Namekaki kokanga yango na mwa elamba, kopakola mwa pomade, kasi ezomonana neti ezokoma lisusu mabe. Nalingaki kotungisa moto te, nakanisaki ekosila yango moko, kasi mwana na ngai ya mwasi atyé ngai mbamba ete naya kaka awa. Amitungisaka mingi, nzambe na ngai. Nazomimona zoba, kozwa tango ya monganga mpo na eloko ya moke boye. Kasi na bosolo, ebandi kotungisa mpe ngai mwa moke. Nayoki... ndenge mosusu koleka mwa pota ya libaku. Ntangu mosusu eza mozindo? Mpe eza na nsolo oyo... Nalingi kotungisa te, kasi nalingi kaka nayeba soki nyonso ezali malamu.

srcs: Pre-Operative Instructions
Please read and follow these instructions carefully before your hernia repair procedure with Dr. Hiroshi Tanaka.
Fasting:
Do not eat or drink anything (including water, gum, or candy) after midnight the night before your surgery.

If you take medication, please consult with Dr. Tanaka or your primary care physician regarding which medications to take and when. You may be instructed to take certain medications with a sip of water on the morning of surgery.
Medications:
Inform Dr. Tanaka about all medications, vitamins, and herbal supplements you are currently taking.

You may need to stop taking certain medications, such as blood thinners (e.g., aspirin, warfarin) or anti-inflammatory drugs (e.g., ibuprofen, naproxen), several days before surgery. Follow Dr. Tanaka's specific instructions regarding medication adjustments.
Hygiene:
Shower or bathe the night before or morning of your surgery.
Do not shave the surgical area yourself. If shaving is necessary, it will be done at the surgical center.
Remove all jewelry, piercings, and contact lenses before arriving for your surgery.
Clothing:
Wear loose-fitting, comfortable clothing that is easy to put on and take off.
Avoid wearing clothing with zippers or buttons near the surgical site.
Transportation:
Arrange for a responsible adult to drive you home after your surgery. You will not be allowed to drive yourself.
Have someone stay with you for the first 24 hours after surgery.
Post-Operative Care:
Follow all post-operative instructions provided by Dr. Tanaka and the surgical center staff.
Take prescribed pain medication as directed.
Apply ice packs to the surgical area as instructed to reduce swelling.
Avoid strenuous activity and heavy lifting for several weeks following surgery.
Keep the surgical site clean and dry.
Attend all follow-up appointments with Dr. Tanaka.
Contact Information:
If you have any questions or concerns before or after your surgery, please contact Dr. Tanaka's office at 555-0199.
In case of an emergency, call 911 or go to the nearest emergency room.
Additional Instructions:
Bring your insurance card and photo ID to the surgical center.
Leave valuables at home.
Arrive at the surgical center at the designated time.
We look forward to providing you with excellent care during your hernia repair procedure.
trgs: Malako ya liboso ya lipaso
Palado, tanga mpe tosa malako oyo malamumalamu liboso ya lipaso na yo ya hernie epai ya Dr. Hiroshi Tanaka.
Kokila:
Kolya eloko moko te to komela eloko moko te (ata mayi, bazoka, to babonbon) nsima ya midi ya butu liboso ya lipaso na yo.

Soki ozali komela nkisi, kende komona Dr. Tanaka to monganga na yo ya liboso mpo ayebisa yo bankisi nini okoki komela mpe ntango nini. Bakoki koyebisa yo omela bankisi mosusu na mwa mayi na ntongo ya lipaso.
Bankisi:
Yebisa Dr. Tanaka bankisi nyonso, bavitamini mpe bilei mosusu ya kobakisa oyo ozali kozwa sikoyo.

Ekoki kosenga okata komela bankisi mosusu, neti oyo ekómisaka makila pɛtɛpɛtɛ (ndakisa, aspirine, warfarine) to oyo esilisaka mpasi (ndakisa, ibuprofene, naproxene), mwa mikolo liboso ya lipaso. Tosa malako ya Dr. Tanaka mpo na kobongisa komela na yo ya bankisi.
Bopeto:
Sokola nzoto butu moko liboso to na ntongo ya lipaso na yo.
Komikata nsuki te na esika ya lipaso. Soki esengeli bakata suki, bakosala yango na ndako ya lipaso.
Longola mayaka nyonso, piercings, mpe matalatala ya misu liboso osalisa lipaso na yo.
Bilamba:
Lata bilamba oyo ezali na bonsomi mpe ya malamu oyo eza pete na kolata mpe kolongola.
Boyá kolata bilamba oyo ezali na ekoti to babuto pene na esika ya lipaso.
Transport:
Bongama mpo moto moko ya mokolo akende kotika yo na ndako nsima ya lipaso na yo. Bakopesa yo ndingisa ya kokumba yo moko mutuka te.
Senga moto atikala na yo mpo na bangonga 24 ya liboso nsima ya lipaso.
Kobatela nzoto na nsima ya lipaso:
Tosa malako nyonso ya nsima ya lipaso oyo Dr. Tanaka mpe bato ya mosala ya centre ya lipaso basili kopesa.
Mela nkisi ya mpasi oyo bakomeli yo ndenge bapeseli yo yango.
Tya ngalasi na esika ya lipaso ndenge bayebisi yo mpo na kokitisa kovimba.
Boyá kosala misala ya makasi mpe komema kilo mpo na mwa baposo nsima ya lipaso.
Batela esika ya lipaso peto mpe ekauka.
Kende kokutana na Dr. Tanaka na mikolo nyonso oyo bukatani na bino ebongisamaki.
Makambo matali banimero:
Soki ozali na mituna to mitungisi liboso to nsima ya lipaso na yo, benga biro ya Dr. Tanaka na 555-0199.
Soki likama ebimi, benga 911 to kende na ndako ya bosalisi ya lobangu oyo ezali pene.
Malako Mosusu:
Mema karte na yo ya Asiransi mpe karte ya mboka oyo ezali na elongi na yo na centre ya lipaso.
Tika biloko na yo ya nmotuya na ndako.
Koma na centre ya lipaso na ntango oyo bakataki.
Tozali kozela kopesa yo lisalisi ya malamu mpenza na ntango ya lipaso na yo ya hernie.

srcs: "Alright, Joao, let's talk about your lab results. Looking at your blood work, specifically the 'ESR' or erythrocyte sedimentation rate, we can see it's elevated. Think of it like this: imagine your blood cells as little rafts floating down a river. Normally, they float pretty freely. But when there's inflammation in your body, like what's causing your limp, these rafts start clumping together and sinking faster. That faster sinking rate is what we measure with the ESR. A higher ESR tells us there's more inflammation going on."
"Okay, I see. So, the inflammation is making my blood cells clunky and sink faster?"

"Exactly. Now, we also checked your 'CRP' or C-reactive protein. This is another marker for inflammation produced by your liver. Think of it like a smoke alarm going off when there's a fire. A high CRP level is like a loud alarm telling us there's significant inflammation happening somewhere in your body. Both the elevated ESR and CRP confirm that your body is fighting something, likely related to your joint pain."
"So, my body is basically sending out distress signals?"

"Precisely. These results help us understand the severity of the inflammation and guide our treatment plan. We'll likely start with anti-inflammatory medication and physical therapy to help reduce the inflammation and improve your mobility. We'll also monitor these levels over time to see how you're responding to treatment."
trgs: "Malamu, Joao, tolobela mbano ya baekzame na yo. Na kotala mbano ya makila na yo, mingi mingi VS to 'vitesi ya sedimentatio ya erytrocyte, tomoni ete emati. Kanisa bongo: kanisa ete biloko ya mikemike ya makila na yo ezali lokola bamasuwa ya mike oyo ezali kotambola na kati ya ebale. Mbala mingi, yango etambolaka na bonsomi. Kasi soki kovimba moko ezali na kati ya nzoto na yo, lokola oyo ezali kosala ete otenguma, bamasuwa yango ebandi kokangama mpe kozinda na lobangu. Vitesi wana ya kozinda na lobangu nde tomekaka na VS. VS ya likolo elakisi biso ete kovimba ezali mingi."
"Ok, nayoki. Boye, kovimba ezali kosala ete biloko ya mikemike ya makila na ngai ekangama mpe ezinda na lobangu?"

"Ezali bongo. Sikoyo, tomekaki mpe proteine C-reactive na yo to 'CRP'. Oyo ezali elembo mosusu ya kovimba oyo libale na yo ebimisaka. Kanisa yango lokola apareyi oyo elelaka soki milinga etondi na ndako oyo ebɛtaka ntango mɔtɔ ezali. CRP ya likolo ezali lokola apareyi yango oyo ezali koyebisa biso ete kovimba ya makasi ezali na esika moko na nzoto na yo. Komata ya VS mpe CRP endimisaka biso ete nzoto na yo ezali kobunda na eloko moko, oyo mbala mosusu etali mpasi na yo ya matonga."
"Boye, nzoto na ngai ezali kotinda mingimingi bilembo ya mpasi?"

"Yango wana. Mbano oyo esalisaka biso toyeba soki kovimba ezali makasi mpe etambwisaka biso na mwango ya kopesa nkisi na biso. Mbala mosusu tokobanda na bankisi ya kobundisa kovimba mpe ngalasisi mpo na kosalisa yo okitisa kovimba mpe otambola malamu. Tokolandela mpe nivo oyo na ntango mpo na komona ndenge nini ozali koyanola na nkisi."

srcs: My sinuses have been throbbing for almost two weeks now, and I've been hoping it would just pass, but the pressure in my forehead is unbearable. I'm Bruno Alves, and I've already tried over-the-counter decongestants, saline rinses, and even steam inhalation, but nothing seems to touch it. The mucus is thick and yellowish-green, and I've been coughing up phlegm, especially at night, which makes it hard to sleep. I've also had a low-grade fever on and off, and my teeth ache, which I've read can be a sign of a sinus infection. I'm worried it might be something more serious or that it could spread. Would a culture be necessary if this persists? I've had sinus infections before, but this one feels different, more persistent and painful. Is there anything else I should be doing at home to manage the symptoms while I wait to see a doctor? I'm anxious about taking antibiotics unnecessarily, but I also don't want this to get worse. I've heard about antibiotic resistance, and I want to be responsible, but I'm really suffering here. Could it be allergies? I've never had allergies before, but maybe I've developed them recently. What are the signs that distinguish a sinus infection from allergies? I just want to get some relief and make sure I'm taking the right steps.

Nabelaka basinizite liboso, kasi oyo ezali ndenge mosusu, ezali koumela mpe ezali kosala mpasi koleka. srcs: I am a 47-year-old female with a long history of medical issues. I have been dealing with an anal fistula for several months now, and it has become increasingly painful and disruptive to my life. I have tried various home remedies and over-the-counter medications, but nothing has worked. My primary care physician referred me to a colorectal surgeon, who recommended surgery to repair the fistula.

I have a history of Crohn's disease, which was diagnosed in my early 20s. I have had multiple surgeries for Crohn's related complications, including a bowel resection and an ileostomy. I also have a history of depression and anxiety, which have been exacerbated by my chronic health issues. I take several medications for my Crohn's disease and my mental health conditions.

I am very nervous about this surgery. I have had so many surgeries in the past, and I am worried about the recovery process. I am also worried about the possibility of complications, given my complex medical history. However, I know that I need to have this surgery done in order to improve my quality of life. I am hopeful that the surgery will be successful and that I will be able to get back to my normal life soon.
trgs: Nazali mwasi ya mibu 47 oyo azali na lisolo molai ya makambo ya minganga. Nazalaki kotungisama na bozali ya nzela mosusu ya mabe na lifwini na boumeli ya basanza ebele sikoyo, mpe yango ekómaki kopesa mpasi mingi mpe kobebisa bomoi na ngai. Nameki nkisi ndenge na ndenge ya ndako mpe nkisi oyo esengaka mokanda ya monganga te, kasi ata moko te esalaki. Monganga na ngai ya liboso atindaki ngai epai ya monganga ya kolorektale, oyo asɛngaki básala ngai lipaso mpo na kobongisa nzela yango.

Nazali na maladi ya Crohn, oyo emonanaki ntango nazalaki na mibu 20. Nasali mapaso mingi mpo na makambo etali maladi ya Crohn, kati na yango kolongola misopo mpe ileostomi. Nazali mpe na maladi ya mitungisi na makanisi mpe minyoko, oyo ekomaki makasi mpo na makambo ya kolongono ya nzoto na ngai ya mikolo nyonso. Namelaka nkisi ebele mpo na maladi na ngai ya Crohn mpe bokono ya makanisi na ngai.

Nazali na mitungisi mingi mpo na lipaso oyo. Nasalaki mapaso ebele na kotala makambo oyo eleki, mpe nazali na mitungisi mpo na ndenge nakozonga malamu. Nazali mpe na mitungisi mpo na makambo oyo ekoki kobima, kotala lisolo na ngai ya bomoi ya mae matali kolongono ya nzoto na ngai. Kasi, nayebi ete nasengeli kosala lipaso oyo mpo na kobongisa bomoi na ngai. Nazali na elikya ete lipaso yango ekolonga mpe ete nakozonga na bomoi na ngai ya kala mingi te.

srcs: As I sat in the waiting room, clutching my husband's hand, my mind raced through the last few weeks. It felt like a lifetime ago that we were planning weddings, discussing floral arrangements and seating charts. Now, our world revolved around doctors' appointments, medical jargon, and the constant worry etched on our faces.

Our little miracle, baby boy Leo, had been born just a month ago. But instead of joyous coos and sleepless nights filled with cuddles, our first few days were a blur of panic and confusion. Leo had suffered seizures shortly after birth, a terrifying experience that left us feeling helpless and scared.

The doctors had explained that Leo's seizures were caused by a temporary lack of oxygen during birth. They assured us that with proper care and monitoring, he would likely outgrow them. But the fear lingered, a constant shadow over our newfound parenthood.

Today was our follow-up appointment with Dr. Kapoor, the neurologist who had been caring for Leo. I took a deep breath, trying to steady my nerves as we were called into his office. Dr. Kapoor greeted us with a warm smile, his eyes crinkling at the corners. He examined Leo thoroughly, asking us about his progress and any changes we had noticed.

"Leo looks fantastic," Dr. Kapoor announced, his voice filled with genuine delight. "His reflexes are strong, and his development is right on track." He explained that Leo's EEG results showed no signs of seizure activity, a huge relief that washed over me like a wave.

Dr. Kapoor continued, explaining that while we still needed to be vigilant, the chances of Leo having further seizures were minimal. He discussed weaning Leo off his medication gradually, a process that filled me with both hope and trepidation.

Leaving Dr. Kapoor's office, I felt a weight lift off my shoulders. The fear that had been my constant companion for weeks began to recede, replaced by a tentative sense of optimism. Leo was going to be okay. We were going to be okay.

As we walked out of the hospital, the sun shining brightly, I looked at my husband and smiled. "Maybe we can start planning that first birthday party after all," I said, a hint of my old self returning. He squeezed my hand, his eyes filled with love and relief. "Absolutely," he replied. "And maybe even a few weddings too."
trgs: Ntango nazalaki kofanda na esika ya kozela, nasimbaki loboko ya mobali na ngai, nabandaki kokanisi baposo oyo eleki. Emonani lokola eleki ntango mingi penza banda tozalaki kobongisa makambo ya libala, kosolola ndenge ya kotia bafololo mpe esika bato bakofanda. Sikoyo, bomoi na biso ekomi kobalukaka na bakutani na minganga, maloba ya minganga, mpe mitungisi ya ntango nyonso oyo ekomami na bilongi na biso.

Ka mwa likamwisi na biso, mwana na biso ya mobali Leo, abotamaki sanza moko esili koleka. Kasi na esika ya koyoka esengo mpe kozanga mpongi na butu mpo na koyambayamba mwana, mikolo na biso ya liboso etondaki na kobanga mpe kozanga koyeba. Leo azalaki na maladi ya ndeke mwa moke nsima ya kobotama na ye, eksperiansi moko ya kobanga oyo etikaki biso na mawa mpe kobanga.

Minganga balimbolaki ete maladi ya ndeke ya Leo ewutaki na kozanga oxygène mwa ntango moke na ntango na ye ya kobotama. Balobelaki biso ete na lisalisi ya malamu mpe bokengeli oyo esengeli, akoki kolonga yango. Kasi kobanga ezalaki kaka, elili ya ntango nyonso na bomoi na biso ya sika ya kozala baboti.

Lelo ezalaki mokolo ya bokutani na biso na Dr. Kapoor, monganga ya boongo oyo azalaki kosalisa Leo. Napemaki makasi, mpo na komeka kozwa kimya ntango babengaki biso na biro na ye. Dr. Kapoor ayambaki biso na mwa koseka na ye ya esengo, azalki kobalula matúmu ya miso na ye. Asalaki Leo ekzame malamu, abandaki kotuna biso soki akoli ndenge nini mpe mbongwana nini oyo tomoni.

Dr. Kapoor alobaki ete: "Leo azali malamu mpenza," mongongo na ye etondaki na esengo ya solo. "Mimesano na ye ezali makasi, mpe bokoli na ye ezali na nzela ya malamu." Alimbolaki ete mbano ya EEG ya Leo emonisaki elembo ata moko te ya maladi ya ndeke, esengo moko monene oyo elataki ngai lokola mbonge.

Dr. Kapoor akobaki, na kolimbola ete ata soki tosengeli kokeba, litomba mpo ete Leo akweya lisusu na maladi ya ndeke ezali moke. Alobelaki kolongola nkisi ya Leo mokemoke, likambo oyo etondisaki ngai na elikya mpe kobanga.

Ntango nabimaki na biro ya Dr. Kapoor, nayokaki kilo moko elongwe na mapeka na ngai. Kobanga oyo ezalaki moninga na ngai ya ntango nyonso na baposo ebandaki kosila, mpe esengo ya mwa moke eyaki na esika na yango. Leo akokaki kobika. Tokokaki kokoma malamu.

Ntango tozalaki kobima na lopitalo, moi engengaki makasi, natalaki mobali na ngai mpe nasekaki. Nlobaki ete "Mbala mosusu tokoki kobanda kobongisa feti yango ya mbotama ya liboso," mwa ndabu ya bomoto na ngai ya kala ebandaki kozonga. Asimbaki loboko na ngai, miso na ye etondaki na bolingo mpe esengo. Alobaki na ngai "Ya solo". "Mpe ntangu mosusu kutu, ata mabala mwa mingi lisusu."

srcs: Okay, let's talk about those lab results, Ms. Vance.  I can see you're worried, but try to relax a bit.  Your blood work came back looking good overall, except for your blood sugar levels which are a bit higher than we'd like to see.  That can sometimes affect your vision, you know.  Wait, are you having trouble focusing up close?  Like when you're sorting mail or reading those tiny addresses?  That's exactly what I'm talking about – presbyopia. It's super common as we get older, basically your eyes losing their flexibility.  But with the higher blood sugar, it could be making it a bit worse or happening sooner than expected.  Don't panic!  We'll get you set up with an eye doctor, maybe get some reading glasses or adjust your prescription if you already wear them.  And we'll definitely keep an eye on that blood sugar too.  Maybe make some tweaks to your diet or exercise routine?  Nothing drastic, just some small changes can make a big difference.  You're a mail carrier, right? So you're already getting plenty of exercise, which is awesome!  We just want to make sure you can see clearly to deliver all those important letters and packages.  So, take a breath, Ms. Vance. We're going to figure this out together.  Sound like a plan?
trgs: Ok, Madame Vance, tólobela mwa moke mbano oyo emonani na ba ekzame ya laboratware. Namoni ozali kotungisama mingi, kasi meka kokitisa motema mwa moke. Na mokuse, ekzame ya makila na yo ezali malamu, longola kaka sukali ya makila na yo oyo ezali likolo mingi koleka ndenge tolingeli ezala. Oyebi, ekoki mbala mosusu kobebisa miso na yo. Zelá nanu, ozali kokoka te kotala malamu biloko ya penepene? Na ndakisa, ntango ozali kokabola mikanda to kotanga baadrɛsi ya mikemike? Yango nde nabandaki koloba – presbiti. Esalemaka mingi ntango tozali kokola, miso na yo ezali kobungisa makoki na yango ya komona. Kasi ntangu sukali ya makila ezali ya komata, ekoki kobebisa makambo lisusu koleka to kosala ete ekoma noki koleka ndenge ekanisamaki. Kobanga te ! Tokotinda yo epai ya monganga ya miso, ntangu mosusu akopesa yo manɛti mpo na kotanga to akobongisa mokanda na yo ya monganga soki osilá kozala na yango. Mpe tokolandela sukali na yo ya makila. Ntangu mosusu, osengeli kobongisa bilei na yo to programe na yo ya ngalasisi? Eloko ya mpasi te, mwa mbongwana moke ekoki kopesa bokeseni monene. Ozalaka mosali ya posita, boye te ? Ezali likambu ya malamu penza, mpamba te, osalaka bangalasisi mingi. Tolingi kaka komindimisama ete okoki komona malamu mpo na kokaba mikanda mpe biloko wana nyonso ya ntina. Yango wana, komintungisa te, Madame Vance. Tokosilisi likambo oyo elongo. Osepeli na likanisi yango?

srcs: Hey kid, listen up. We've got a patient here for a postpartum depression screening. She's here at the urgent care, which, let's be honest, isn't exactly the Ritz-Carlton for mental health, but we do what we can.

Now, this isn't your typical "run-of-the-mill" check-up. We're dealing with a new mom, probably running on fumes and coffee, possibly feeling like she's drowning. So, tread lightly, okay? Be gentle, be empathetic. This isn't the time for your usual blunt force trauma approach.

First things first, establish rapport. Make her feel comfortable, like she can actually talk to you without judgment. Ask about the baby, how she's sleeping (or not sleeping), how she's feeling emotionally. Don't just stick to the script; listen to what she's saying, and more importantly, what she's not saying.

Then, dive into the screening tool. Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale, anyone? Yeah, I know, thrilling stuff. But it's important. Go through the questions, explain what they mean, and pay attention to her answers. A high score doesn't automatically mean she's got PPD, but it's a red flag waving in your face.

If she does score high, don't panic. This isn't a death sentence. Talk to her about treatment options, therapy, medication, support groups. Let her know she's not alone, that this is common and treatable. And for the love of all that is holy, make sure she has a follow-up plan. Don't just send her out into the wild with a pat on the back and a "good luck."

Remember, we're not just treating symptoms here; we're dealing with a person, a mother, someone's wife, daughter, friend. So, treat her with the respect and compassion she deserves. And if you screw up, well, that's on you. But don't worry, I'll be watching like a hawk. Now go get 'em, tiger.
trgs: Hey mwana, yoka malamu. Tozali na mobeli awa mpo na kotala soki azali na mitungisi ya makanisi na nsima ya kobota. Azali awa na esika ya lobiko ya nokinoki, oyo, toloba solo, ezali penza te nsuka na mae matali kolongono ya makanisi, kasi tozali kosala oyo tokoki.

Sikoyo, oyo ezali te botaleli ya momeseno. Tozali kolobela mama ya elenge, ntangu mosusu azali bolembu mpe asuki motema, ntangu mosusu azali koyoka lokola azali kozinda. Bongo, kende malembe, ok? Zala na boboto, zala na mawa. Oyo ezali ntango te ya kosalela bandenge ya mobulu mpe ya makasi.

Ya liboso mpenza, bongisa boyokani. Sala ete amiyoka malamu, lokola akoki kosolola na yo na kozanga kosambisama na nsima. Tuna ye bebe azali ndenge nini, ndenge nini azali kolala (to kolala te), ndenge nini azali komiyoka. Kokakatana te na kotya likebi na oyo azali koloba, mpe ya ntina koleka, makambo oyo azali koloba te.

Na nsima, bolobela bisaleli ya ekzame. Emekelo ya mitungisi ya makanisi oyo eyaka na nsima ya kobota ya Edinburgh, moto moko ayebi? Iyo, nayebi, eloko ya kokamwa. Kasi ezali na ntina. Talela mituna, sosola ndimbola na yango mpe tyela biyano na ye likebi. Pwé ya likolo elimboli te ete azali na bokono ya PPD, kasi ezali elembo ya likama.

Soki azwi pwé ya likolo, kobanga te. Oyo ezali etumbu ya liwa te. Solola na ye mpo na bankisi oyo akoki kozwa, lobiko, bankisi, bituluku ya lisungi. Yebisa ye ete azali ye moko te, ete oyo ekomelaka batu ebele mpe ekoki kosila. Mpe mingimingi penza, sala ete azala na mwango ya bolandeli. Kotinda ye kaka libanda te akende kobunda ye moko na koyebisa ye kaka ete ''Ekosimba''.

Kobosana te, ezali kaka likambu ya kosilisa bilembo te; ezali likambo ya moto, mama, mwasi ya moto, mwana mwasi, moninga. Bongo, monisa ye limemya mpe mawa oyo abongi na yango. Mpe soki obebisi, wana eza likambo na yo. Kasi komitungisa te, nakokengela yo na mosika. Sikoyo, kende liboso.

srcs: Hey there, Dr. Navarro here. Just finished up with a patient, Leticia Ramirez, who came in for her follow-up on that encephalitis she's been battling. Poor thing was limping pretty noticeably when she walked in, favoring her left leg quite a bit.

She's a hotel housekeeper, you know, on her feet all day, so that limp's gotta be tough. Said she's been feeling a bit better overall, head's cleared up some, fever's down, but that leg's giving her trouble. Mentioned it started hurting a few days ago, kinda dull ache at first, then got worse. Doesn't recall any specific injury, just woke up with it sore one morning.

Examined the leg, didn't see any obvious swelling or redness, but she winced when I pressed around the calf area. Range of motion seemed okay, but definitely some tenderness there. Neurological exam was mostly normal, reflexes intact, though she did seem a bit unsteady on her feet, maybe related to the encephalitis still lingering a bit.

We talked about her work, how demanding it is physically. She's worried about taking time off, needs the money, but I told her she really needs to rest that leg if she wants it to heal properly. Suggested some light duty if possible, or maybe even a few days off to let things settle down. Also prescribed some anti-inflammatories and told her to keep an eye on it, let me know if it gets worse or if she notices any other symptoms.

Overall, she seems in good spirits despite everything. Tough cookie, that Leticia. Just hope we can get her back on her feet – literally – soon. Encephalitis is no joke, and adding a leg issue on top of it just complicates things. But we'll keep monitoring her closely, make sure she gets the care she needs.
trgs: Mbote, ezali Monganga Navarro. Nautaki kosilisa na mobeli moko, Leticia Ramirez, oyo ayaki mpo na kolandela maladi na ye ya ensefalite oyo azalaki kobunda na yango. Mawa mingi, abandaki kotenguma makasi ntango akotaki, kotambolela mingi na lokolo na ye ya mwasi.

Azali mwana-mosala na otele, boyebi, azalaka ya kotelema mokolo mobimba, yango wana kotenguma yango ezali penza mpasi. Alobaki ete azali koyoka mwa malamu na nzoto mobimba, makanisi na ye ebongi mwa moke, fefele na ye ekiti, kasi lokolo wana ezali komonisa ye mpasi. Alobaki ete mpasi yango ebandaki mwa mikolo mileki, mpasi ya moke na ebandeli, na nsima ekomaki makasi penza. Azali kominkundola pota moko te azokaki na esika moko, na ntongo moko boye, alamukaki kaka na mpasi yango.

Natalaki lokolo, namonaki te kovimba to esika moko oyo ekomaki motane, kasi agangaki ntango nabandaki kofina zingazinga ya lokolo. Koningisa lokolo ezalaki mwa malamu, kasi mpasi moko ezalaki mpenza wana. Ekzame ya misisa ezalaki mwa malamu, mimesano ebebaki te, atako azalaki na mpasi ya kotelema tende na makolo na ye, ntango mosusu mpo na ensefalite oyo ezalaki naino mwa moke.

Tolobelaki mosala na ye, ndenge nini esengaka makasi ya nzoto. Azali komitungisa mpo na kozwa konje, azali na mposa ya mbongo, kasi nayebisaki ye ete asengeli mpenza kopema na lokolo wana soki alingi ete ebika malamu. Napesaki ye makanisi ya kosala misala ya pɛpɛlɛ soki likoki ezali, to mbala mosusu kozwa mwa mikolo ya konje mpo na kotika makambo ezonga na molongo. Nakomelaki ye mpe bankisi ya kokitisa mpasi mpe nayebisaki ye atala yango malamu, ayebisa ngai soki ekomi makasi to soki amoni bilembo mosusu.

Na mokuse, azali komonana na esengo atako minyoko nyonso. Leticia azali mwasi ya makasi. Tozali kolikya ete toko sunga ye mpo abika – kala mingi te. Ensefalite ezali liseki te, mpe kobakisa lisusu likambo ya lokolo ezali kokómisa makambo mpasi koleka. Kasi tokokoba kolandela ye penepene, koyeba penza ete azali kozwa lisalisi oyo abongi na yango.

srcs: Dr. Aris Thorne: Good afternoon, Mr. Sterling. I see you're concerned about the changes you've noticed in your skin, particularly on your face, neck, hands, and arms. It's quite common for individuals in high-stress professions like yours to notice these signs of aging.
Atticus Sterling: Yes, doctor. It's not just vanity; it's affecting my confidence in the courtroom. I feel like I look older than I am, and I worry it might impact my clients' perception of me.

Dr. Thorne: I understand completely. Let's talk about what's happening. As we age, our skin loses collagen and elastin, the proteins that give it structure and elasticity. This leads to wrinkles, sagging, and thinning skin. Sun exposure, which I imagine you get plenty of during your travels, accelerates this process.
Atticus Sterling: I do spend a lot of time outdoors, and I haven't always been diligent with sunscreen.

Dr. Thorne: That's a significant factor. Sun damage causes age spots, uneven pigmentation, and further breakdown of collagen. Additionally, stress can contribute to premature aging by increasing cortisol levels, which can damage skin cells.
Atticus Sterling: So, what can be done? Is it too late to reverse the damage?

Dr. Thorne: Not at all. There are several options available, ranging from topical treatments to minimally invasive procedures. We can start with a personalized skincare regimen incorporating retinoids, antioxidants, and broad-spectrum sunscreen. For more noticeable results, we could consider chemical peels, laser therapy, or injectables like Botox or fillers.
Atticus Sterling: I've heard of those, but I'm hesitant about anything too invasive.

Dr. Thorne: That's perfectly understandable. We can tailor a plan that suits your comfort level and goals. Perhaps we can start with a series of chemical peels to improve skin texture and tone, coupled with a consistent home care routine. As we see progress, we can discuss other options if you wish.
Atticus Sterling: That sounds reasonable. I appreciate your thorough explanation, Dr. Thorne. It's reassuring to know there are steps I can take to improve my skin's appearance.

Dr. Thorne: My pleasure, Mr. Sterling. Remember, taking care of your skin is an investment in yourself, both personally and professionally. Let's schedule a follow-up appointment to monitor your progress and adjust the plan as needed.
trgs: Dr. Aris Thorne: Mbote, Mr. Sterling. Namoni ozali komitungisa mpo na mbongwana oyo omoni na loposo na yo, mingi mpenza na elongi, na nkingo, na maboko mpe na loboko. Ezali likambo ya somo te mpo na bato oyo basalaka misala ya mpasi makasi lokola yo bakoka komona bilembo oyo ya konuna.

Atticus Sterling: Iyo, monganga. Ezali kaka te likambo ya lolendo; ezali kobebisa komindima na ngai na esika ya esambiselo. Namiyokaka lokola nazali konuna koleka ndenge nazali, mpe nazali komitungisa ete ekoki kobebisa ndenge oyo bakiliya na ngai batalelaka ngai.

Dr. Thorne: Nayoki yo malamu. Tolobela mpo na oyo ezali kosalema. Ntango tozali kokola, mposo na biso ebungisaka collagene na elastine, ba proteini oyo epesaka yango kozalela mpe kobendana. Yango ememaka na kobimisa banzelanzela na elongi, na kosilisa makasi na loposo, mpe na kokomisa loposo patatalu. Kotikala na moi, oyo nakanisi ozwaka mingi ntango osalaka mibembo, epusaka noki na nzela wana.
Atticus Sterling: Nasalaka ngonga mingi na libanda, mpe nazalaka ntango nyonso makasi te na kopakola pomade ya moi.

Dr. Thorne: Wana ezali likambo ya ntina mingi. Mbeba ya moi ememaka na matona ya konuna, langi ya loposo ebebaka, mpe ebevisaka lisusu colagene. Lisusu, mitungisi ya makanisi ekoki kopesa maboko na konuna ya mbangu na komatisa nivo ya kortisole, oyo ekoki kobebisa baselile ya loposo.
Atticus Sterling: Boye, nini ekoki kosalema? Ngonga esi eleki mpo na kobongisa mbeba wana?

Dr. Thorne: Ata moke te. Ezali na banzela mingi, kobanda na lobiko ya loposo kino na lipaso ya moke. Tokoki kobanda na programe ya kobatela loposo oyo ebongisami mpo na yo na kosangisa retinoide, ba antioxydant, na pomade ya moi ya makasi. Mpo mbano ya komona, tokoki kokanisa ba peeling chimique, lobiko na ba laser, to biloko ya kotshiuba lokola Botox to fillers.
Atticus Sterling: Nayokaka mpo na yango, kasi nazali na kobanga mpo na eloko nyonso oyo ezali kozwa loposo mingi.

Dr. Thorne: Wana ezali mpenza likambo ya koyeba. Tokoki kobongisa mwango oyo ekokani na nivo na yo ya malamu mpe na mikano na yo. Mbala mosusu tokoki kobanda na molongo ya ba peeling chimique mpo na kobongisa bonene mpe langi ya loposo na yo, elongo na momesano ya bobateli na ndako ntango nyonso. Ntango tokomona bokoli, tokoki kotalela banzela misusu soki okosepela.
Atticus Sterling: Eza malamu. Nasepeli na ndenge olimboli, Dr. Thorne. Ezali kopesa kimia koyeba ete ezali na matambe oyo nakoki kozwa mpo na kobongisa ndenge loposo na ngai emonanaka.

Dr. Thorne: Ezali esengo na ngai, M. Sterling. Kobosana te, kobatela loposo na yo ezali botyami mosolo na mopanzi moko mpo na yo moko, ezala na bomoi na yo mpe na mosala. Tozwa mokolo ya bokotani mpo na kolandela bokoli na yo mpe kobongisa mwango soki ezali ntina.

srcs: I'm back again, Dr. Idrissi. I know you said those lifestyle changes would take time to kick in, but it's been months and I'm just not seeing any improvement. The anxiety is still crippling, and I'm exhausted all the time. I'm still waking up at 3 AM with my heart racing, and I can barely drag myself out of bed in the morning. My work is suffering, too. I can't focus on my cases, and I'm constantly on edge. I've tried everything you suggested - the meditation, the exercise, the diet changes - but nothing seems to help. I feel like I'm failing, like maybe I'm just not trying hard enough. But honestly, I'm trying my best. Is there anything else we can do? Maybe medication or a different kind of therapy? I just want to feel like myself again. I want to be able to do my job properly and actually enjoy my life. Please, tell me there's something else we can try.
trgs: Nazongi lisusu, Dr. Idrissi. Nayebi olobaki ete mbongwana ya lolenge ya bomoi ekoki kozwa ntango mpo ebanda kosala, kasi basanza eleki mpe nazali komona mbongwana te. Mitungisi ezali naino makasi, mpe nalembaka ntango nyonso. Nalamukaka naino na ngonga ya misato ya ntongo na motema kobeta makasi, mpe nakokaka te kobima na mbeto na ntongo. Mosala na ngai mpe ezali kobeba. Nakokaka te kotya makanisi na makambo na ngai, mpe nazalaka ntango nyonso na kanda. Nameki nyonso oyo olobaki - kosala ngalasisi, kobongola bilei, kasi eloko moko te ezali kosunga. Nazali komiyoka ete nazali kolonga te, mbala mosusu nazali komeka makasi te. Kasi ya solo, nazali komeka na makasi na ngai nyonso. Ezali na eloko mosusu oyo tokoki kosala? Mbala mosusu nkisi to lolenge mosusu ya lisalisi? Nalingi kaka komiyoka lisusu lokola ngai moko. Nalingi nakoka kosala mosala na ngai malamu mpe kosepela na bomoi na ngai. Palado, yebisa ngai ete ezali na eloko mosusu oyo tokoki komeka.

srcs: Doctor, you know how sometimes you get that burning feeling in your chest after eating something spicy or heavy, like acid indigestion? My son, Efua Appiah, gets that a lot, especially when he's lying down. It's like his stomach acid keeps coming back up and irritating his throat. And he's been having trouble swallowing sometimes, like food gets stuck on the way down. Plus, he's been losing weight without really trying, which worries me. I've also noticed he's been coughing more, especially at night, and his voice sounds a bit hoarse sometimes. Could these be signs of Barrett's esophagus? I know it's more common in adults, but with his wheelchair use and the acid reflux, I wanted to be sure we're not missing anything.
trgs: Monganga, oyebi ndenge ntangu mosusu moto oyokaka motema kopela moto na nsima ya kolia biloko ya koswa to ya kilo, neti libumu pasi na asidi? Mwana na ngai, Efua Appiah, ayokaka yango mingi, mingimingi soki alali. Ezali neti asidi ya likundu na ye ezali kozongela ye mpe kopesa ye mpasi na mongongo. Mpe azali na mokakatano ya komela mbala mosusu, neti bilei bikangamaka ye na mongongo. Lisusu, azali kobungisa bakilo oyo akanaki te, yango ezali kotungisa ngai. Namoni mpe ete azali kokosola makasi, mingimingi na butu, mpe mongongo na ye ezali koyokana ya kozika. Ekoki kozala elembo ya maladi ya œsophage ya Barrett? Nayebi ete ekomelaka mingi bato ya mikolo, kasi lokola asalelaka kiti ya bibosono mpe azali na asisi ezongelaka ye na mongongo, nalingaki namindimisa ete tozali kobunga eloko te.

srcs: Frequent urination, especially at night, is a common issue during pregnancy. It happens because your growing uterus presses on your bladder, and your body is producing more fluids. While it can be annoying, it's usually harmless.
Here are some tips to help manage it:
Drink plenty of fluids during the day, but limit your intake in the evening.
Avoid caffeine and alcohol, which can irritate your bladder.
Try to empty your bladder completely when you go.
Lean forward when you urinate to help empty your bladder.
If you experience pain or burning when you urinate, or if you have a fever or chills, see your doctor right away, as these could be signs of a urinary tract infection.
Don't hesitate to talk to your doctor if you have any other concerns. They can offer more personalized advice and support.
trgs: Kosuba mbala na mbala, mingimingi na butu, ezali likambo esalemaka mingi na ntango ya zemi. Esalemaka mpo matrisi na yo ezali kokola mpe ezali kofina libenga ya masuba, mpe nzoto na yo ezali kobimisa mayi mingi. Atako ekoki koyokisa mwa nsoni, ememaka penza likama te.
Tala mwa batoli mpo na kosunga yo na yango:
Mela biloko ya mayi mingi na moi, kasi kitisa komela yango na mpokwa.
Boya kafe na masanga, mpo ekoki kotungisa libenga na yo ya masuba.
Meka kobimisa masuba nyonso soki okei kosuba.
Gumbama liboso ntango ozali kosuba mpo esunga yo na kobimisa masuba nyonso.

Soki oyoki mpasi to kozika moko ntango ozali kosuba, to soki ozali na fefele to ozali koyoka nzoto kolenga, kende kokutana monganga na yo mbala moko, mpo ekoki kozala bilembo ya bokono ya nzela ya masuba.
Kokakatana te mpo na kosolola na monganga na yo soki ozali na mitungisi misusu. Akoki kopesa yo toli mpe lisungi oyo ebongi na yo moko.

srcs: Provider: Hi there, I'm Dr. Yusuf. You must be Ichiro. Nice to meet you.
Ichiro: Yeah, hi.
Provider: I understand you're here because of some abnormal Pap smear results. Can you tell me a bit about what brought you in today?
Ichiro: My partner made me come. I feel fine, honestly. I don't see why this is such a big deal.

Provider: I hear you. It can be frustrating to come in when you're feeling okay. But abnormal Pap results are something we want to keep an eye on. It doesn't necessarily mean anything bad, but it's important to follow up just to be sure.
Ichiro: I guess. But what does it even mean? Is it cancer or something?

Provider: Not necessarily. Abnormal results can mean a few different things, most of which are easily treatable. It could be something as simple as an infection or inflammation. We just need to do a few more tests to figure out exactly what's going on.
Ichiro: Okay, so what kind of tests?

Provider: We'll start with a colposcopy. It sounds scary, but it's really just a close look at your cervix with a special magnifying instrument. It's quick and usually painless. Depending on what we see, we might take a small sample of tissue for further testing.
Ichiro: And then what?

Provider: Once we have the results from the colposcopy and any biopsy, we'll have a better idea of what's causing the abnormal cells. Then we can discuss the best course of action, whether it's just monitoring, medication, or a minor procedure.
Ichiro: Alright, I suppose that makes sense. Thanks for explaining it.
Provider: Of course. It's always better to be safe than sorry, right? And remember, we're here to help you through this every step of the way. Any other questions for me right now?
Ichiro: No, I think I'm good for now. Thanks.
Provider: You're welcome. Let's get started with the exam then.

srcs: Nurse Adeline: Good morning, Mr. Kianpour. I see you're here to discuss some drug interactions with Dr. Ortiz. Could you tell me a little bit more about what's going on?
Mr. Kianpour: Uh, yeah. I've been having some... stomach issues lately. And I think it might be because of the new medication I started taking for my anxiety.
Nurse Adeline: I see. And what medication is that?
Mr. Kianpour: It's called Alprazolam. My psychiatrist prescribed it about a week ago.
Nurse Adeline: Okay. And what other medications are you currently taking?
Mr. Kianpour: Just some over-the-counter stuff for allergies. Claritin, I think.
Nurse Adeline: Alright. And have you noticed any other symptoms besides the stomach issues?
Mr. Kianpour: Well, I've been feeling really tired lately. Like, more than usual. And sometimes I get dizzy when I stand up too fast.
Nurse Adeline: Okay, those are important things to note. Have you experienced any changes in your mood or behavior?
Mr. Kianpour: Not really. Just a little anxious about... everything.

Nurse Adeline: Understandable. It sounds like you might be experiencing some side effects from the Alprazolam, or possibly an interaction with the Claritin. Dr. Ortiz will be able to review your medications and discuss your symptoms in more detail. Is there anything else you'd like to mention before you see him?
Mr. Kianpour: No, I think that's it. I just... I really need to get this sorted out. I have a big event coming up next week and I can't afford to be feeling like this.
Nurse Adeline: I understand completely. Dr. Ortiz is very experienced and I'm sure he'll be able to help you find a solution. Just have a seat in the waiting area and he'll be with you shortly.
Mr. Kianpour: Thank you.

Mr Kianpour: Te, nakanisi yango wana. Kaka... nazali na mposa ya kobongisa likambo oyo. Nazali na milulu moko ya motuya oyo ekokoma poso ekoya mpe nakoki te koyoka boye.

srcs: Doctor: Hey, Uche. You're back already? Didn't the treatment work?
Uche Okafor: No, Doc, it didn't. I'm still tired all the time, and I'm starting to get really frustrated. I have a deadline coming up, and I can't focus on my work.

Uche Okafor: I know, but I need something to help me now. Can't you give me something stronger?
Doctor: I can't just prescribe something stronger without knowing what's causing your fatigue. We need to run some more tests.
Uche Okafor: More tests? I don't have time for more tests! I need a solution now!
Doctor: I know you're impatient, Uche, but we need to be thorough. Rushing into treatment could make things worse. Let's schedule some tests and see what we find.
Uche Okafor: Fine. But make it quick. I can't keep living like this.

Monganga: Nayebi ete ozangi motema molai, Uche, kasi tosengeli kotala malamumalamu. Kokende mbangu na kopesa nkisi ekoki kobebisa makambo. Tika totya programɛ ya ba ekzamɛ mpe totala nini tokozwa.
