srcs: Cashier: Hi Dr. Islam, thanks for fitting me in. I'm a cashier at the grocery store, and standing all day has been getting tougher lately. My back and hips have been aching a lot, and I'm worried it might be my osteoporosis.
Dr. Islam: I understand. Osteoporosis can definitely cause pain and make it harder to do things like stand for long periods. Have you noticed any new or worsening pain recently?
Cashier: Yeah, especially after a few hours on my feet. It feels like a deep ache, and sometimes sharp pains shoot down my legs. I've had to call out a few times because it's just too much.
Dr. Islam: That sounds tough. It's important to listen to your body. Have you been taking your medication and doing any exercises we discussed?
Cashier: I try, but it's hard to find time with my schedule. And honestly, sometimes the exercises make it hurt more.

Dr. Islam: That's understandable. Maybe we can adjust your exercise plan to something gentler. In the meantime, given your pain and the nature of your job, I think it would be reasonable to provide you with a note for a few days off to rest and see if that helps.
Cashier: Really? That would be amazing. I don't want to lose my job, but I just can't keep pushing through the pain like this.

Dr. Islam: I can write a note excusing you from work for the next three days. That should give you some time to rest and see if the pain improves. We can also schedule a follow-up appointment to check in and discuss adjusting your treatment plan if needed.
Cashier: Thank you so much, Dr. Islam. That's a huge relief. I'll definitely rest up and try to do some gentle stretching like you suggested.
Dr. Islam: You're welcome. Remember, taking care of yourself is the most important thing. If the pain gets worse or doesn't improve after resting, please don't hesitate to call the office.
Cashier: I will. Thanks again!
trgs: Kalaka: Mbote Dr. Islam, matondi na ndenge oyambi ngai. Nazalaka kalaka na magazini ya monene biloko ya kolia, mpe kotelema mokolo mobimba ekomi mpasi mingi mikolo oyo. Mokongo mpe loketo na ngai ezali kosala mpasi mingi, mpe nazali komitungisa ete ekoki kozala osteoporose na ngai.
Dr. Islam: Nasosoli. Osteoporose ekoki mpenza kopesa mpasi mpe kokomisa makambo makasi lokola kotelema ntango molayi. Omoni mpasi ya sika to oyo ezali kobakisama mikolo oyo?

Kalaka: Ee, mingi mingi na nsima ya mwa bangonga na kotelema. Nazali koyoka mpasi na ndenge ya kati, mpe ntango mosusu mpasi ya makasi ezali kokita mpe komata na makolo na ngai. Esengelaki nabenga mpo na kozwa konje mbala mibale to misato mpo eleki ndelo.
Dr. Islam: Yango ezali penza mpasi. Ezali ntina koyoka nzoto na yo. Ozali komela nkisi na yo mpe kosala ngalasisi oyo tosololaki?
Kalaka: Namekaka, kasi ezali mpasi kozwa ntango na programe na ngai. Mpe ya solo, ntango mosusu ngalasisi ezali kopesa mpasi koleka.

Dr. Islam: Yango ezali kososolama. Ntangu mosusuete tokoki kobongisa programe ya ngalasisi na yo na eloko ya pete koleka. Na ntango wana, kotalela mpasi na yo mpe lolenge ya mosala na yo, nakanisi ete ekozala malamu kopesa yo mokanda mpo na mwa mikolo ya konje mpo opema mpe omona soki yango ekosalisa yo.
Kalaka: Ya solo? Yango ekozala malamu mingi. Nalingi kobungisa mosala na ngai te, kasi nazali kokoka lisusu te mpasi oyo.

Dr. Islam: Nakoki kokoma mokanda ya kopesa yo konje na mosala mpo na mikolo misato oyo ekoya. Yango esengeli kopesa yo mwa ntango ya kopema mpe komona soki mpasi ekokita. Tokoki mpe kobongisa mokolo ya bokutani ya bolandeli mpo na kotala mpe kosolola bambongwana ya programe ya lisalisi na yo soki esengeli.
Kalaka: Matondi mingi, Dr. Islam. Yango ezali libondisi monene. Nakopema mpenza mpe nakomeka konyolola nzoto na ndenge ya pete lokola opesaki toli.
Dr. Islam: Likambo te. Kobosana te, komibatela yo moko ezali likambo ya ntina mingi koleka. Soki mpasi ekomi makasi to ezali kobonga te na nsima ya kopema, kokakatana te na kobenga na biro.
Kalaka: Nakosala yango. Matondi lisusu!

srcs: Patient Instructions
Diagnosis: Post-Cholecystectomy Syndrome
Medication:
Cholestyramine powder: Take 1 scoop mixed with water or juice once daily before breakfast. This medication helps bind bile acids and can relieve diarrhea.
Omeprazole 20 mg capsule: Take 1 capsule daily before breakfast. This medication reduces stomach acid and can help with heartburn and indigestion.
Dicyclomine 10 mg tablet: Take 1 tablet three times daily as needed for abdominal cramping.
Diet:
Low-Fat Diet: Avoid fatty, greasy, and fried foods. These can worsen diarrhea and gas.
Small, Frequent Meals: Eat smaller meals throughout the day instead of three large ones. This helps your digestive system handle food more easily.
Fiber: Gradually increase fiber intake from fruits, vegetables, and whole grains. Fiber can help regulate bowel movements.
Hydration: Drink plenty of fluids to prevent dehydration, especially if experiencing diarrhea.
Activity:
Gradually return to normal activities as tolerated.
Avoid heavy lifting or strenuous exercise for the first few weeks.
Follow-up:
Schedule a follow-up appointment in 2 weeks to monitor progress.
Call the office if symptoms worsen or do not improve.
Additional Instructions:
Keep a food diary to identify trigger foods that worsen symptoms.
Avoid alcohol and caffeine, as they can irritate the digestive system.
Quit smoking, as it can delay healing and worsen digestive problems.
Manage stress, as it can exacerbate symptoms.
Emergency Warning Signs:
Seek immediate medical attention if you experience:
Severe abdominal pain
Fever over 101°F (38.3°C)
Jaundice (yellowing of the skin or eyes)
Persistent vomiting
Bloody or black stools
Please do not hesitate to contact our office with any questions or concerns. We are committed to helping you feel better.
trgs: Malako ya babeli
Diagnostiki: Maladi ya nsima ya kolongola sakosi ya nsongi
Nkisi:
Mputulu ya Cholestyramine: Mela lutu 1 esangisami na mayi to jus mbala moko na mokolo liboso ya kolia bilei ya ntongo. Nkisi oyo esalisaka kokanga acidi ya nsongi mpe ekoki kosilisa pulupulu.
Liyunda ya Omeprazole 20 mg: Mela liyunda 1 na mokolo liboso ya kolia bilei ya ntongo. Nkisi oyo ekitisaka asidi ya likundu mpe ekoki kosalisa na kotumba na motema mpe mpasi ya konika bilei.
Mbuma ya Dicyclomine 10 mg: Mela mbuma 1 mbala misato na mokolo soki osengeli mpo na mpasi ya libumu.
Bilei:
Bilei ya mafuta moke: Boya bilei ya mafuta, oyo ya kalingama mpe oyo etonda mafuta. Oyo ekoki kovimbisa pulupulu mpe mikinza.
Bilei ya mike, mbala na mbala: Lya bilei ya mike na boumeli ya mokolo na esika ya misato ya minene. Yango ekosalisa nzoto na yo na konika bilei.
Bafibre: Bakisa malembe malembe kolya na yo ya bafibre uta na bambuma, bandunda, mpe mbuma ya mobimba. Fibre ekoki kosalisa kobongisa botamboli ya misopo.
Komela: Mela biloko ya mayi mingi mpo na kopekisa bokawuki ya mayi na nzoto, mingimingi soki ozali na pulupulu.
Mosala:
Zongela malembe malembe misala ya momeseno na kolanda bokoki na yo.
Boya komema biloko ya kilo to kosala ngalasisi ya makasi na baposo ya liboso.
Kolandela:
Bongisa mokolo ya bokutani ya kolandelama na baposo 2 mpo na kotala bokoli.
Benga biro soki bilembo bibebi to bibongi te.
Malako mosusu:
Batela kahier ya bilei mpo na koyeba bilei oyo ebandisaka bilembo.
Boya masanga mpe kaféine, mpamba te ekoki kosuasa binama ya konikela bilei.
Tika komela makaya, mpamba te ekoki kowumisa lobiko mpe kobebisa mikakatano ya bonikami ya bilei.
Yeba koyangela mitungisi na yo ya makanisi, mpamba te ekoki kobakisa bilembo.
Bilembo ya likebisi ya mbangu:
Luka lisalisi ya monganga nokinoki soki ozali na bilembo biye bilandi:
Mpasi makasi ya libumu
Fefele koleka 101°F (38.3°C)
Jonise (Loposo to miso ekomi na langi ya mosaka)
Kosanza mbala na mbala
Nyei ya makila to ya moindo
Soki ozali na mituna to mitungisi, kokakatana te kobenga biro na biso. Tozali awa mpo na kosalisa yo oyoka malamu.

srcs: Doctor, the patient is a 67-year-old retired librarian who has been experiencing dyspareunia, or pain during intercourse, for the past few months. She describes the pain as a sharp, burning sensation localized near the vaginal entrance, occurring at the beginning of penetration and lasting throughout the act. She also reports vaginal dryness and occasional spotting after intercourse. Her past medical history is significant for hypertension and hyperlipidemia, both well-controlled with medication. She underwent menopause at age 52 and has not used hormone replacement therapy. There's no history of sexually transmitted infections or pelvic inflammatory disease. On pelvic examination, there is evidence of vulvovaginal atrophy, with thinning and pale vaginal mucosa, loss of vaginal rugae, and petechiae. A speculum examination was difficult due to discomfort and narrowing of the introitus. The cervix appeared normal, and bimanual examination revealed no adnexal masses or tenderness. Based on her history and physical examination, the most likely diagnosis is genitourinary syndrome of menopause (GSM), formerly known as atrophic vaginitis. Further evaluation might include a vaginal pH test and a wet mount to rule out infection, but GSM seems the most probable cause of her symptoms. We can discuss treatment options such as vaginal moisturizers, lubricants, and potentially local estrogen therapy to alleviate her discomfort and improve her quality of life.
trgs: Monganga, mobeli na ngai azali mwasi mosali ya kala makasi na biblioteke ya mibu 67 mpe azali na bokono ya dyspareni, to koyoka mpasi na ntango ya kosangisa nzoto, na mwa basanza oyo euti koleka. Azali kolimbola mpasi yango neti mwa kozika moko ya makasi na pembeni ya monoko na ye ya nzoto ya mwasi, ebandaka ntango babandi kokotisa mpe eumelaka na boumeli ya bosangisi nzoto. Azali mpe koloba ete nzoto ya mwasi na ye ekauka mpe mwa makila moke ebimaka ntango mosusu na nsima ya kosangisa nzoto. Na lisolo ya bomoi na ye ya kala na mae matali kolongono ya nzoto na ye, abela maladi ya tensyo mpe ya mafuta mingi na makila, maladi yango nyonso mibale elandelamaki malamu na bankisi. Amonaka lisusu basanza na ye te banda akokisaki mibu 52 mpe atikala kosalela te lisalisai ya monganga ya kozongisaka ba-hormone. Azanga lisolo ya bomoi ya kolongono ya nzoto na mae matali babokono oyo ezwamaka na nzela ya kosangisa nzoto to maladi oyo evimbisaka biboti ya mwasi. Ekzame ya nse ya libumu na ye elakisi kokondakonda moko ya binama biboteli, loposo ya nzoto ya mwasi elemba mpe enzuluka, kobungisa masusa ya nzoto ya mwasi mpe bilembo ya motane na loposo. Ekzame na spekulum ezalaki mpasi mpo na mokakatano mpe kokonda ya munoko ya nzoto ya mwasi. Kingo ya matrisi emonanaki malamu, mpe ekzame ya bomekimeki na maboko mibale emonisaki bambuma ata moko te na matrisi. Na kolanda lisolo ya bomoi na ye ya kolongono ya nzoto mpe ekzame ya nzoto, mbano oyo ekoki kozala mpenza ezali bokono ya biboteli mpe bisubeli ya kozanga komona bansanza (GSM), oyo eyebanaki na kala na kombo ya kokonda ya nzoto ya mwasi. Baekzame misusu na ndakisa botaleli ya pH ya nzoto ya mwasi mpe botaleli ya matangi ya nzoto na ye ya basi ekoki kosunga na kotika likanisi ya bokono, Kasi GSM emonani neti ntina ya solo ya bilembo na ye. Tokoki kolobela maponi ya lobiko lokola kosalela bakreme ya kopakola, bamafuta oyo bapakolaka na nzoto ya mwasi, mpe mbala mosusu lobiko na estrogenoterapi mpo na kosilisa mokakatano na ye mpe kobongisa bomoi na ye.

srcs: First, please fill out this medical release form authorizing us to communicate with your employer regarding your absence. Once completed, our medical staff will evaluate your condition and determine the appropriate diagnosis and duration of necessary leave. If a personality disorder is diagnosed, we will document it in your medical records. Following the evaluation, the doctor will prepare a note detailing the recommended time off work. This note will specify the start and end dates of your leave, along with any necessary restrictions or accommodations. You will receive a copy of this note for your records. Please present the original note to your employer's human resources department or supervisor. If your employer requires additional information or clarification, they may contact our clinic directly with your consent. We recommend scheduling a follow-up appointment to monitor your progress and adjust your treatment plan as needed. Remember to adhere to the prescribed treatment regimen and attend all scheduled therapy sessions. Should you experience any worsening symptoms or concerns, please contact our clinic immediately. We are here to support you throughout your recovery process.
trgs: Yambo, tosengi otondisa formulere oyo ya bopasi nzela ya monganga mpo na kopesa biso nzela ya kosolola na patro na yo mpo na kozanga na yo na mosala. Soki etondisami, ekipi na biso ya baminganga bakotala ndenge ozali mpe bakoyeba maladi nini ozali na yango mpe ntango boni esengeli opema. Soki bamoni ete ozali na maladi ya makanisi, bakokoma yango na dosye na yo ya monganga. Nsima ya botaleli yango, monganga akokoma mokanda oyo ekolimbola ntango oyo esengeli ozanga mosala. Mokanda yango ekolobela dati ya kobanda mpe ya kosilisa konje na yo, mpe soki ezali na makambo oyo esengeli opekisa to obongisa. Okozwa kopi ya mokanda oyo mpo na kobomba. Tosengi opesa mokanda ya yambo na departema oyo bazwaka batu na mosala to ya mokambi na yo. Soki patro na yo azali na mposa ya koyeba makambo mosusu to alingi balimbolela ye, akoki kobenga mbala moko na lopitalo na biso soki opesi ye nzela. Tosengi obongisa bokutani mosusu mpo na kolandela ndenge ozali koyoka mpe kobongisa mwango ya lisalisi na yo soki esengeli. Kobosana te kolanda bankisi oyo bapesaki yo mpe kokende na ba seansi nionso ya lobiko oyo ebongisami. Soki oyoki ete bilembo ya maladi ezali kobakisama to ozali na mitungisi, tosengi obenga mbala moko na lopitalo na biso. Tozali awa mpo na kosunga yo na ntango nyonso ya kobika na yo.

srcs: The doctor says I'm short of breath and have a cough because of the tumor in my lung. They say it's also why my chest hurts sometimes and I've been coughing up blood. I've also been losing weight without trying, which they say is another sign. My voice has been getting hoarse lately too, and they think the tumor might be pressing on a nerve. I've been feeling really tired and run down, which they say is common with cancer. And I've had some pain in my shoulder and arm, which they think might be from the cancer spreading. I'm still not sure about all this, but my husband insisted I come see you.
trgs: Monganga na ngai alobi ete nazali kopepa malamu te mpe nazali kokosola mingi mpo na etutuluku moko ezali na mimpululu na ngai. Balobi ete yango mpe nde ezali kosala ete ntolo na ngai ezala koswa na bantango mosusu mpe nazali kosanza makila. Nazali mpe kokonda kozanga ete namona ntina na yango, mpe balobi ezali elembo mosusu. Mongongo na ngai ezali mpe ya kozikama mikolo oyo, mpe bazali kokanisa ete etutuluku yango ekoki kofina mosisa moko. Nazali koyoka nzoi koleka ndelo mpe nazali kolamba, mpe balobi ete yango emonanaka mingi epai ya bato ya kansere. Nazali mpe koyoka mpasi na lipeka na ngai mpe na loboko, mpe bazali kokanisa ete ekoki kozala mpo kansere ezali kopanzana. Nazali naino koyeba malamu te makambo nyonso oyo, kasi mobali na ngai atyaki milende mpo naya komona yo.

srcs: Doctor: Kwame! Oh, my goodness, it's so good to see you! I was just telling my husband the other day that I hadn't seen you in ages. How are you doing? How's the family?
Kwame: Hello, Dr. Rodriguez. It's good to see you too, although I wish it were under better circumstances. The family is fine, thank you.
Doctor: I understand, I understand. Now, I see here that you're in for some pain. Can you tell me a little more about what's going on?
Kwame: Yes, well, it's... it's embarrassing, really. I've been having these terrible cramps in my lower abdomen, and it feels just like... well, like period pain.
Doctor: Oh, Kwame, I'm so sorry to hear that. I can imagine how uncomfortable and confusing that must be for you. Have you been experiencing any other symptoms? Nausea, vomiting, anything like that?
Kwame: No, just the pain. It comes and goes, but when it hits, it's excruciating.
Doctor: I see. And how long has this been going on?
Kwame: A few days now. I tried taking some painkillers, but they haven't really helped.

Doctor: Okay. Well, let's get you checked out and see if we can figure out what's causing this. It could be a number of things, so we'll need to run some tests. But don't worry, we'll get to the bottom of it.
Kwame: Thank you, Dr. Rodriguez. I appreciate your help.
Doctor: Of course, Kwame. You know I'm always here for you. Now, let's get you into an exam room and see what we can find.
trgs: Monganga: Kwame! Ee, Nzambe na ngai, nasepeli makasi penza komona yo! Nabandaki koyebisa mobali na ngai lobi kuna ete namoni yo te banda kala penza. Boni yo? Boni libota?
Kwame: Mbote, Dr. Rodriguez. Nasepeli komona yo mpe, atako nalingaki ezala na libaku moko ya malamu. Libota ezali malamu, matondi.
Monganga: Nayebi, nayebi. Sikoyo, namoni awa ete ozali na mpasi. Okoki koyebisa ngai mwa moke makambo oyo ezali koleka?
Kwame: Ee, likambu te, ezali... ezali kosala ngai nsoni. Nazali koyoka mpasi ya makasi penza na nse ya libumu na ngai, mpe ezali koyokana lokola... lokola mpasi ya kokoma ya sanza na ngai.

Monganga: Oh, Kwame, nazali na mawa mingi koyoka yango. Nakoki kokanisa ndenge nini omiyoki mabe mpe ozali kotungisama mingi mpo na yango. Otikala kozala na bilembo misusu? Motema ya kobaluka, kosanza, to eloko ya ndenge wana?
Kwame: Te, kaka mpasi. Eyaka mpe ekendaka, kasi ntangu eyaka, epesaka mpasi makasi.
Monganga: Namoni. Mpe ezali kosalayo bongo banda ntango nini?
Kwame: Esali mwa mikolo sikoyo. Namekaki komela mwa bankisi ya mpasi, kasi esalisaki mpenza te.

Monganga: OK. Tiká tósala yo ekzame mpe tómona soki tokoki koyeba mpo na nini ezali kosala bongo. Ekoki kolakisa makambo ebele, yango wana tosengeli kosala mwa ba ekzame. Kasi komitungisa te, tokoyeba ntina na yango.
Kwame: Matondi, Dr. Rodriguez. Nazali kosepela na lisalisi na yo.
Monganga: Ya solo, Kwame. Oyebi ete nazalaka ntango nyonso awa mpo na yo. Sikoyo, tókende na esika ya kosala ekzame mpe tómona nini tokoki kozwa.

srcs: Doctor: Good morning, Mrs. Gutierrez. I see you've been experiencing some symptoms after your injury at work. Can you tell me more about what's been going on?

Mrs. Gutierrez: Good morning, Doctor. Yes, ever since the accident, I've been having these terrible headaches. And my stomach... it just feels like it's in knots all the time. I've seen a few other doctors, but they can't seem to find anything wrong with me physically.

Doctor: I understand that must be frustrating. It's important to explore all possibilities. Have you noticed any patterns with these symptoms? Do they get worse at certain times or in certain situations?

Mrs. Gutierrez: Now that you mention it, they do seem to get worse when I think about going back to work. Or even just when I drive past the building where it happened. My heart starts racing, and I just feel... panicked.

Doctor: It sounds like you might be experiencing something called somatic symptom disorder. Sometimes, our bodies react to emotional stress or trauma with physical symptoms. It's like your body is trying to tell you something that your mind is having trouble processing.
Mrs. Gutierrez: Really? I never thought of it that way. But it makes sense. I've been so worried about everything – money, my job, whether I'll ever feel normal again.

Doctor: It's completely understandable to feel that way after a traumatic event. The good news is that there are treatments available that can help. We can work together to address both the physical symptoms and the underlying emotional stress.
Mrs. Gutierrez: That sounds promising. What kind of treatments are we talking about?

Doctor: Cognitive-behavioral therapy, or CBT, is often very effective. It can help you identify and change negative thought patterns that might be contributing to your symptoms. We can also discuss medication options if necessary, or other therapies like relaxation techniques or mindfulness.
Mrs. Gutierrez: I'm willing to try anything that might help. I just want to feel like myself again.

Doctor: That's a great attitude to have. We'll take it one step at a time. Let's start by scheduling some regular appointments so we can monitor your progress and adjust your treatment plan as needed. And remember, you're not alone in this. We're here to support you every step of the way.
Mrs. Gutierrez: Thank you, Doctor. I really appreciate that.
trgs: Monganga: Mbote, Madame Gutierrez. Namoni ozali na bilembo na nsima ya likama na yo na mosala. Okoki koyebisa ngai mwa makambo mingi oyo ezali kosalema?

Madame Gutierrez: Mbote, Monganga. Iyo, uta likama esalemaki, nazali koyoka motu mpasi makasi. Mpe libumu na ngai... nayokaka lokola nde ekangamaka ntango nyonso. Namonaki minganga mosusu, kasi bamonaki eloko te ya mabe na nzoto na ngai.

Monganga: Nayebi ete ezali mpasi. Ezali na ntina kotala makambo nyonso oyo ekoki kozala. Omonaki soki bilembo yango ezali koya na lolenge moko boye? Ezali kokoma makasi na bantango mosusu to na bantangu mosusu?

Madame Gutierrez: Sikoyo lokola olobi yango, emonani ete ezali kokoma makasi ntango nazali kokanisa kozonga na mosala. To ata ntango naleki pene ya ndako esika likama esalemaki. Motema na ngai ebandi kobeta makasi, mpe nayokaka... kobanga.

Monganga: Emonani lokola ozali na maladi oyo babengi somatoform. Ntango mosusu, nzoto na biso esalaka makambo mpo na mitungisi na biso ya makanisi to likama na nzela ya bilembo ya nzoto. Ezali lokola nzoto na yo ezali komeka koyebisa yo likambo oyo makanisi na yo ezali na mokakatano ya kokanga ntina.
Madame Gutierrez: Ya solo? Nakanisaki naino bongo te. Kasi ezali na ntina. Nazalaki komitungisa mingi mpo na makambo nyonso – mbongo, mosala na ngai, soki nakozala lisusu malamu.

Monganga: Ezali mpenza mabe te komiyoka bongo nsima ya likama ya mpasi. Nsango ya malamu ezali ete ezali na bankisi oyo ekoki kosunga. Tokoki kosala elongo mpo na kosilisa bilembo ya nzoto mpe mitungisi ya makanisi na mayoki oyo ezali ekomaka.
Madame Gutierrez: Emonani malamu ete ekoki kosunga. Tozali kolobela bankisi ya ndenge nini?

Monganga: Lobiko ya bizaleli ya komona, to CBT, mbala mingi ezalaka na mosala makasi. Ekoki kosunga yo koyeba mpe kobongola makanisi ya mabe oyo ekoki kozala kopesa nzela na bilembo na yo. Tokoki mpe kolobela nkisi soki esengeli, to lobiko mosusu lokola mayele ya kominyolisisa nzoto to kobenda makanisi.
Madame Gutierrez: Nalingi komeka eloko nyonso oyo ekoki kosunga ngai. Nalingi kaka komiyoka lisusu ngai moko.

Monganga: Yango ezali makanisi ya malamu. Tokokende mokemoke. Tokobanda na kozwa bokutana ya mbala na mbala mpo tokoka kolanda bokoli na yo mpe kobongisa mwango ya lobiko na yo soki esengeli. Mpe kobosana te, ozali yo moko te na likambo oyo. Tozali awa mpo na kosunga yo na bitambe nyonso.
Madame Gutierrez: Matondi, Monganga. Nasepeli mingi na yango.

srcs: My dad, John, has been sleeping terribly lately. He's up all night wandering around, confused, and then sleeps all day. He's getting so agitated and suspicious of everyone, especially doctors. He thinks they're just trying to drug him or put him away. It's heartbreaking to see him like this, so scared and untrusting. I'm exhausted too, trying to keep him safe and calm him down. We're at the Urgent Care now, hoping someone can help us figure out what's going on without making things worse for him.
trgs: Tata na ngai, John, azali kolala mabe mpenza mikolo oyo. Azali kotambola butu mobimba, abuli, mpe na nsima azali kolala moi mobimba. Azali kotungisama mpe kobanga bato, mingimingi minganga. Akanisaka ete bazali kaka koluka kopesa ye bankisi to kobwaka ye. Ezali mawa mingi komona ye ndenge wana, kobanga mpe kokanisela bato mabe. Ngai mpe nalembi, nazali komeka kobatela ye mpe kokitisa ye motema. Tozali sikoyo na lopitalo ya lobangu, na elikya ete moto moko akoki kosalisa biso toyeba likambo oyo ezali kosalema kozanga ete akomisa makambo mabe mpo na ye.

srcs: So, I've been feeling this weird numbness and tingling in my fingers and toes lately, like pins and needles. It started a few weeks ago and hasn't really gone away. And my vision has been a bit blurry too, especially when I'm looking at things up close. I've been getting headaches more often than usual, and sometimes I feel a bit dizzy or off-balance. I'm not sure if it's just stress or something more serious, but I figured I should get it checked out. I was hoping to maybe get a scan or something to see if there's anything going on. Oh, and my name's John, by the way. I'm 52.
trgs: Boye, nazali koyoka lokola misapi na ngai ya maboko mpe makolo ezali kokufa mpe kosua mwa moke na mikolo mileki, lokola nde bazotshiuba ngai tonga. Ebandaki mwa baposo eleki mpe esili naino te. Mpe miso na ngai ezali komona mpe malamu te, mingimingi ntango nazali kotala biloko oyo ezali pene. Nazali koyoka moto mpasi mingi koleka ndenge namesanaka, mpe ntango mosusu nazali koyoka lokola nazali kozwa kizunguzungu to nazali kokwea. Nayebi te soki ezali kaka mitungisi to likambo ya makasi, kasi nakanisaki ete nasengeli kotalisa yango na monganga. Nazalaki kolikya ete mbala mosusu nakoki kosala ekzame ya scan to eloko mosusu mpo na komona soki ezali na likambo oyo ezali kosalema. Kutu, nkombo na ngai John. Nazali na bambula 52.

srcs: Pharmacist: I understand you're looking for something to help with your adrenal glands and fatigue. Can you tell me more about what your doctor said and what symptoms you're experiencing?

Patient: Look, I just told you! I'm tired, I'm stressed, and my doctor said it might be adrenal fatigue. I need a supplement or something to fix it. Don't you have anything like that? Why do you need to know all the details? Just give me something that works!

Pharmacist: I appreciate you sharing that. To recommend the best product, I need to know if you're taking any other medications or have any other health conditions. Some supplements can interact with medications. Did your doctor recommend a specific product or ingredient?

Patient: No, he didn't give me a specific name. He just said to look for something for adrenal support. And I'm not taking any other medications, okay? Just give me whatever is best. I don't have all day to stand here answering questions!

Pharmacist: Okay, I can show you some options for adrenal support supplements. However, since you haven't had a specific recommendation, I would advise consulting your doctor again to be sure which product is right for you. These supplements are not regulated like prescription drugs, and their effectiveness for "adrenal fatigue" isn't fully established medically.

Patient: What do you mean "not established"? My doctor said it's a real thing! Are you saying he's wrong? I just want something to help me feel better! Why are you making this so difficult? Just give me the best one you have!

Pharmacist: I'm not saying your doctor is wrong. I'm just saying that different products have different ingredients and effects. Without a specific recommendation, it's hard to know which one would be most helpful and safe for you. I can show you the aisle where these supplements are located, but I recommend discussing specific options with your doctor.
Patient: Fine! Just show me where they are. I'll figure it out myself. You pharmacists are useless sometimes! I'll talk to my doctor, but I'm buying something today regardless!
trgs: Moteki na Farmasi: Nayoki ete ozali koluka eloko mpo na kosalisa yo na maladi ya glande surrénale mpe kolemba. Okoki koyebisa ngai lisusu nini monganga na yo alobaki mpe bilembo nini ozali komona?

Mobeli: Tala, nauti koyebisa yo! Nazali na bolembu, nazali kotungisama na makanisi, mpe monganga na ngai alobaki ete ekoki kozala bolembu ya baselile. Nazali na mposa ya bilei moko ya kobakisama to eloko mosusu mpo na kobongisa yango. Ozali na eloko ya bongo te? Mpo na nini ozali na mposa ya koyeba makambo nyonso? Pesa ngai kaka eloko oyo esalaka!

Moteki na Farmasi: Natondi botondi na ndenge oyebisi ngai yango. Mpo na kopesa toli ya nkisi oyo eleki malamu, nasengeli koyeba soki ozali komela nkisi mosusu to ozali na maladi mosusu. Bilei misusu ya kobakisa ekoki kobebisa makasi ya bankisi mosusu. Monganga na yo apesaki yo toli moko na oyo etali nkisi to vitamini moko boye?

Mobeli: Te, apesaki ngai kombo moko te. Alobaki na ngai kaka ete naluka nkisi moko mpo na kosunga baselile. Mpe nazali komela nkisi mosusu te, oyoki? Pesa ngai kaka oyo eleki malamu. Nazali na mokolo mobimba awa te mpo na kopesa biyano na mituna!

Moteki na Farmasi: Ok, nakoki kolakisa yo biponi mwa mingi ya bilei ya kobakisa mpo na kosunga baselile. Kasi, lokola otikala kozwa toli moko boye te, nasengi yo osolola lisusu na monganga na yo mpo na koyeba eloko nini ebongi na yo. Bilei ya kobakisa oyo ezalaka ndenge moko te na bankisi oyo monganga akomaka, mpe makasi na yango mpo na "bolembu ya baselile" endimisami naino malamu te na baminganga.

Mobeli: Olingi koloba nini na "eendimami naino malamu te"? Monganga na ngai alobaki ete ezali likambo ya solo! Olingi koloba ete azali na libunga nini? Nalingi kaka eloko mpo na kosalisa ngai na koyoka malamu! Mpo na nini ozali kokomisa likambo oyo pasi boye? Pesa ngai kaka oyo eleki malamu oza na yango!

Moteki na Farmasi: Nazali koloba te ete monganga na yo azali na libunga. Nazali kaka koloba ete nkisi nyonso ezalaka na ndenge na yango mpe mbuma na yango. Soki toli moko boye ezali te, ezali mpasi koyeba oyo wapi ekoki kosunga yo mingi mpe kozala malamu mpo na yo. Nakoki kolakisa yo esika bilei ya kobakisa yango ezalaka, kasi napesi yo toli ya kosolola na monganga na yo mpo na koyeba oyo wapi okopona.

Mobeli: Ezali malamu! Lakisa ngai kaka esika ezali. Nakoluka ngai moko. Bino bateki nkisi bozali na ntina te na bantango mosusu! Nakosolola na monganga na ngai, kasi nakosomba eloko lelo atako ndenge nini!

srcs: Hello Mr. Song, I see you're experiencing quite a bit of sweating. It's important to understand that excessive sweating can sometimes be related to the medications you are taking or an underlying condition. I'll make sure to review your current prescriptions to check for any side effects that might be causing this. Additionally, we should discuss any other symptoms you might be having, as they could provide clues to the cause. Staying hydrated is crucial, especially when losing fluids through sweat, so please drink plenty of water. Wearing breathable clothing can also help manage your comfort. If this persists, it might be worth consulting with your doctor to rule out other potential issues. We can also look into over-the-counter options that might provide some relief. Remember, your health and comfort are our top priorities. If you have any questions about your billing or insurance coverage regarding these consultations, feel free to ask. We're here to help you navigate both your health and the administrative side of your care. Let's work together to find a solution that makes you feel better.
trgs: Mbote Mr. Song, namoni ozali kobimisa sueur mingi. Ezali na ntina oyeba ete kobimisa sueur mingi ekoki kozala na boyokani na bankisi ozali komela to na maladi mosusu ozali na yango. Nakotala malamu bankisi na yo ya lelo mpo na komona soki ezali na mabe moko oyo ekoki kobimisa motoki. Lisusu, tosengeli kosolola na ntina ya bilembo mosusu oyo okoki kozala na yango, mpo ekoki kopesa biso nzela ya koyeba ntina ya likambo oyo. Ezali na ntina mingi komela biloko ya mayi ebele, mingimingi soki ozali kobimisa mayi na nzoto na nzela ya motoki, yango wana nabondeli yo omela mayi mingi. Kolata bilamba oyo epesaka mopepe nzela ekoki mpe kosalisa yo oyoka malamu. Soki likambo oyo ezali kokoba, ekoki kozala malamu kosolola na monganga na yo mpo na koyeba soki ezali na makambo mosusu. Tokoki mpe kotala bankisi oyo batekaka na farmasi oyo ekoki kosunga yo. Kobosana te, kolongono na yo ya nzoto mpe esengo na yo ezali na ntina mingi mpo na biso. Soki ozali na motuna etali kofuta mbongo to asiransi na yo na ntina ya botaleli oyo, okoki kotuna. Tozali awa mpo na kosalisa yo na makambo ya kolongono na yo ya nzoto mpe na makambo ya kosalisa mikanda ya leta. Tika tosalisana mpo na kozwa lobiko oyo ekosala ete oyoka malamu.

srcs: I'm here for an evaluation, I guess. My boss said I needed to come after I got hurt at work. I fell off a ladder, maybe six feet? I don't remember much, just waking up with a headache and my back hurting. I've always been a bit clumsy, I suppose. My mom used to say I had two left feet.

But this is about more than just the fall, right? They keep asking me about school and stuff. I struggled a lot in school. Reading and math were always hard. I got held back in second grade, and I think I was in special classes for reading until high school. I dropped out in 11th grade. Just couldn't keep up.

I've always had trouble learning new things. Like, at work, if they change the way we do something, it takes me a long time to get it. My boss gets frustrated sometimes. I try my best, but things just don't stick in my head like they do for other people.
And remembering things... that's a struggle too. I forget names, appointments, even simple things like where I put my keys. My wife helps me keep track of stuff, but it's embarrassing sometimes.
I've had other health problems too. Diabetes, high blood pressure... I take a lot of pills. And I get these headaches sometimes, really bad ones. They make me dizzy and sick to my stomach.

I just want to know if there's something wrong with me, you know? Like, why is everything so hard for me? Maybe this evaluation will give me some answers. I just want to be able to do my job and take care of my family without feeling like I'm always messing up.
trgs: Nazali awa mpo na komekama, nakanisi. Patron na ngai alobaki na ngai ete nasengeli koya nsima ya kozoka na ngai na mosala. Nakweaki na ebutelo, mbala mosusu na bolai ya makolo motoba? Nazali komikundola makambu mingi te, nayebi kaka ete ntangu nalamukaki, motó na mukongo ebandaki kosala ngaoi mpasi. Nazalaka ntango nyonso mwa kilo, nakanisi. Mama na ngai azalaki koloba nazalaka na makolo mibale ya mwasi.

Kasi oyo etali makambo mosusu longola kaka kokwea, boye te? Bazali kotuna ngai makambo ya kelasi mpe biloko mosusu. Nasalaki milende mingi na kelasi. Kotanga mpe matematiki ezalaki ntango nyonso mpasi. Nazongaki nsima na kelasi ya mibale, mpe nakanisi nazalaki na bakelasi ya sipesiale mpo na kotanga tii na secondaire. Natikaki kelasi na kelasi ya 11. Nabandaki kokoka lisusu makambu te.

Nazalaka na mokakatano ya koyekola makambo ya sika. Na ndakisa, na mosala, soki babongoli lolenge tomesana kosala eloko moko, ezwaka ngai ntango molai mpo nako kanga yango. Patro na ngai asilikaka ntango mosusu. Nasala milende penza, kasi makambo ekotaka na motó na ngai te ndenge ekotaka na mitó ya bato misusu.

Mpe komikundola makambo... wana mpe ezali etumba. Nabosanaka bankombo, bokutani, ata biloko ya mpamba lokola esika natie bafungola na ngai. Mwasi na ngai asalisaka ngai mpo na kolandela yango, kasi ezali koyokisa ngai nsoni ntango mosusu.

Nazwaki mpe mikakatano mosusu ya kolongono ya nzoto mpe. Diabeti, tansyo... Namelaka bankisi mingi. Mpe motó ebetaka ngai na bantango mosusu, ya makasi mpenza. Epasaka ngai kizunguzungu mpe ebelisaka likundu na ngai.

Nalingi kaka koyeba soki ezali na eloko moko ya mabe epai na ngai, oyebi? Lokola, mpo na nini nyonso ezali mpasi mpo na ngai? Ntangu mosusu, komekama oyo ekomemela ngai biyano. Nalingi kaka kokoka kosala mosala na ngai mpe kobokola libota na ngai na kozanga komiyoka lokola nazali ntango nyonso kobebisa makambu.

srcs: Instructions for Mr. Zondi:
Medications:
Furosemide: Take one 40 mg tablet by mouth every morning. This medication helps remove excess fluid from your body, which can improve your heart function and reduce swelling.
Metoprolol: Take one 50 mg tablet by mouth twice daily, once in the morning and once in the evening. This medication helps control your heart rate and blood pressure.
Lisinopril: Take one 20 mg tablet by mouth once daily. This medication helps relax your blood vessels and lower your blood pressure.
Atorvastatin: Take one 40 mg tablet by mouth once daily at bedtime. This medication helps lower your cholesterol levels.
Aspirin: Take one 81 mg tablet by mouth once daily. This medication helps prevent blood clots.
Diet:
Limit your salt intake to less than 2,000 mg per day. Avoid adding salt to your food and choose low-sodium options when possible.
Limit your fluid intake to 2 liters per day. This includes water, juice, soup, and other beverages.
Eat a balanced diet rich in fruits, vegetables, and whole grains. Avoid processed foods, sugary drinks, and excessive amounts of saturated and trans fats.
Activity:
Engage in moderate-intensity exercise for at least 30 minutes most days of the week. Walking is a great option.
Avoid strenuous activity or heavy lifting.
Rest when you feel tired.
Monitoring:
Weigh yourself every morning after using the bathroom and before eating or drinking. Record your weight in a journal.
Check your blood pressure daily and record the readings.
Monitor your blood sugar levels as directed by your doctor if you have diabetes.
Follow-up:
Please schedule a follow-up appointment with your primary care physician within 2 weeks.
Contact your home health nurse or doctor immediately if you experience any worsening symptoms, such as shortness of breath, chest pain, dizziness, or swelling in your legs or feet.
Additional Instructions:
Please use your hearing aids as prescribed.
Make sure to keep your hearing aids clean and free of debris.
If you have any questions or concerns about your hearing aids, please contact your audiologist.

We understand that managing multiple health conditions can be challenging. Please don't hesitate to ask questions or express any concerns you may have. We are here to support you in your journey to better health.
trgs: Malako mpo na Mesyé Zondi:
Bankisi:
Furosemide: Mela komprimé moko ya 40 mg na monoko ntongo nyonso. Nkisi oyo esalisaka na kokawusa mayi oyo eleki na nzoto, oyo ekoki kobongisa esaleli ya motema na yo mpe kokitisa kovimba.
Metoprolol: Mela komprimé moko ya 50 mg na monoko mbala mibale na mokolo, moko na ntongo mpe moko na mpokwa. Nkisi oyo esalisaka na kotalela ebeteli ya motema na yo mpe tensyo ya makila.
Lisinopril: Mela komprimé moko ya 20 mg na monoko mbala moko na mokolo. Nkisi oyo esalisaka na kofongola misisa ya makila mpe kokitisa tensyo ya makila na yo.
Atorvastatin: Mela komprimé moko ya 40 mg na monoko mbala moko na mokolo na ntango ya kolala. Nkisi oyo esalisaka na kokitisa kolesterole na yo.
Aspirin: Mela komprimé moko ya 81 mg na monoko mbala moko na mokolo. Nkisi oyo esalisaka na kopekisa kokangama ya makila.
Bilei:
Kitisa kolya mungwa na yo na nse ya 2,000 mg na mokolo. Boya kobakisa mungwa na bilei na yo mpe pona biloko oyo ezali na sodium moke soki likoki ezali.
Kitisa komela na yo ya biloko ya mayi na balitre 2 na mokolo. Yango etali mayi, jus, supu, mpe masanga mosusu.
Lya bilei ya malamu oyo ezali na bambuma mingi, bandunda, mpe loso na masango ya mobimba ebele. Boya bilei oyo ebongolama, masanga ya sukali, mpe mafuta ya mabe ebele mpe oyo ebongolama.
Misala:
Sala ngalasisi ya makasi te ata na baminiti 30 mikolo ebele na poso. Kotambola ezali liponi ya malamu penza.
Boya misala ya makasi to komema bakilo.
Pema soki ozali komiyoka ya kolemba.
Kokengela:
Mata kilo na ntongo nyonso na nsima ya kokende na twaleti mpe liboso ya kolya to komela. Koma kilo na yo na mokanda moko.
Landela tensyo ya makila na yo mokolo na mokolo mpe koma yango.
Kengela sukali na makila na yo na kolanda lolenge monganga na yo alobaki soki ozali na diabèti.
Kolandela:
Palado, zwa bokutani ya kolandela na monganga na yo ya liboso na kati ya bapɔsɔ 2.

Benga na mbala moko lifulume na yo ya ndako to monganga na yo soki omoni bilembo ekomi makasi koleka, lokola mpasi ya kopema, mpasi na ntolo, kuzwa kizunguzungu to kuvimba moko na makolo to na matambe.
Malako mosusu:
Salela baapareyi na yo ya koyoka ndenge bakomelaki yo yango.
Sala makasi mpo na kobomba baapareyi na yo ya koyoka peto mpe na kozanga bosoto.
Soki ozali na mituna to mitungisi mpo na mae matali baapareyi na yo ya koyoka, benga monganga na yo ya matoyi.

Toyebi ete kozala na maladi ebele ekoki kozala mpasi. Kokakatana te na kotuna mituna to kolobela mitungisi nyonso oyo okoki kozala na yango. Tozali awa mpo na kosunga yo na nzela ya kozwa lobiko mpo na kolongono ya nzoto.

srcs: Today, I saw Dr. Wilson because I've been struggling lately, acting in ways that feel completely out of character. It's embarrassing to admit, but I've been having these intense outbursts—tantrums, even hitting things—and it's honestly scary. I'm a PhD candidate, researching complex social dynamics, and here I am, unable to regulate my own emotions. It feels like a huge pressure cooker inside me, and sometimes the lid just blows off.

I tried to explain to Dr. Wilson that the stress of my dissertation, the constant deadlines, and the isolation of academic work are getting to me. But it's more than just stress; it feels like something deeper is wrong. Maybe it's a lack of sleep, or maybe it's just the sheer weight of expectations I've placed on myself. I found myself getting teary-eyed just talking about it, which is another thing I'm not used to.

Dr. Wilson listened patiently, which I appreciated. She didn't dismiss my feelings or tell me to just "toughen up." Instead, she asked about my sleep patterns, my diet, and even my social life outside of academia. It made me realize how neglected those areas have been. I left the appointment feeling a little lighter, knowing that I'm not alone in this and that there are steps I can take to regain control. It's going to be a process, but acknowledging the problem is the first step, right? I just hope I can find a way to balance my academic ambitions with my mental health before things spiral further out of control.
trgs: Lelo, nakutanaki Dr. Wilson mpo nazali konyokwama mikolo oyo, kozala na bizaleli oyo ezali ya ngai te. Ezali kosala mwa nsoni kondima, kasi nazali na nkanda makasi, ata kobeta biloko, mpe ezali kobangisa. Nazali moyekoli ya PhD, nasalaka bolukiluki ya makambo ya bomoi ya bato, mpe sikoyo, nakoki te koyangela mayoki na ngai moko. Ezali lokola esaleli ya kikuku na kati na ngai, mpe na bantango mosusu epanzanaka.

Namekaki kolimbwela Dr. Wilson ete mitungisi ya ekzame na ngai, ntango ya kosilisa mosala, mpe kozanga komona bato na mosala ya kelasi ezali kopesa ngai mitungisi. Kasi ezali koleka mitungisi ya mpamba; emonani lokola likambo mosusu ya mozindo ezali mabe. Mbala mosusu ezali kozanga mpongi, to mbala mosusu ezali kaka kilo ya makambo oyo namityelaki. Namonaki ete nazali kolela ntango nazalaki kolobela yango, likambo oyo namesana na yango te.

Dr. Wilson ayokaki ngai na motema molai, likambo oyo nasepelaki na yango. Akitisaki mayoki na ngai te to alobaki na ngai te ete "nabunda." Kasi, atunaki mituna na ntina na ndenge na ngai ya kolala, bilei na ngai, mpe ata bomoi na ngai ya bato libanda ya kelasi. Yango esalaki ete namona ndenge nini nabosanaki makambo wana. Nabimaki na rendez-vous na mwa esengo, koyebaka ete nazali ngai moko te na likambo oyo mpe ete ezali na makambo oyo nakoki kosala mpo na kozongisa bokambi. Ekozala molongo, kasi kondima mokakatano ezali litambe ya liboso, boye te? Nazali na elikya ete nakoki kozwa lolenge ya kokokisa bamposa na ngai ya kelasi na kolongono ya nzoto na ngai ya makanisi liboso ete makambo ebeba lisusu.

srcs: Dear Dr. Montgomery,

I am writing to refer Mr. George Reynolds, an 82-year-old Caucasian male, for further evaluation and management of his symptoms. Mr. Darko was previously seen in our clinic for a family history of Bloom syndrome. Despite initial management, his symptoms have persisted and even worsened slightly since his last visit.

Given his age and family history, I believe a more specialized assessment is warranted to rule out any potential complications or underlying conditions associated with Bloom syndrome or other age-related factors. Mr. Darko has expressed concern about his lack of improvement and is eager for further investigation.
Please find enclosed his medical records, including details of his previous visit and any relevant test results. I would appreciate your expert opinion on the best course of action for Mr. Darko.
Thank you for your attention to this matter.
Sincerely,
Dr. Rui Ferreira
trgs: Molingami Dr. Montgomery,

Nakomeli yo mpo na kotindela yo George Reynolds, mobali ya mposo mpembe ya mbula 82, mpo na botali mpe bolandeli malamumalamu ya bilembo ya maladi na ye. Mr. George Reynolds asi asalisaki baekzame na lopitalo na biso na ntina ya lisolo ya bomoi na ye na mae matali kolongono ya nzoto ya kala mpo na maladi ya Bloom oyo ezalaka na libota na bango. Atako na botaleli ya ebandeli, bilembo na ye esili te mpe ebebi mwa moke banda mbala ya nsuka oyo ayaki.

Na kolanda bambula na ye mpe makambo oyo esalemaki na kala na libota na bango, nakanisi ete esengeli otala ye malamu mpo toyeba soki maladi ya Bloom to makambo mosusu ya bobange nde ememeli ye bampasi mosusu to maladi mosusu oyo emonanaka te. Mr. Darko azali komitungisa mpo azali koyoka malamu te mpe alingi mpenza ete botaleli yango esalema malamu.

Nakangi na kati awa mikanda na ye ya monganga, na makambo ya mbala ya nsuka oyo ayaki mpe bambano ya baekzame oyo ebongi. Nakosepela kozwa makanisi na yo ya moto atanga mingi mpo na koyeba lolenge ya kopesa na Mr. Darko lobiko oyo esengeli.
Matondi mpo na likebi oyo ozali kopesa na likambo yango.
Na motema nyonso,
Dr. Rui Ferreira
